instances.label: Fabricate/assemble a prototype unit from released design files in the company lab or model shop: 3D-print or machine brackets, mount motors, gearboxes and sensors, fit the populated control board, route and terminate the wiring, so a settled design can be evaluated. Parts and drawings are complete; the job is to physically realize the design, sometimes several identical units.

Realize and verify a prototype control/electronics board: send schematic, layout and BOM out for quick-turn assembly or build it in-house, then confirm electrically and functionally (continuity/short checks, in-circuit or flying-probe test, optical inspection, power-up smoke test) that the built board matches design intent.

Bench bring-up, integration and debugging of a new mechatronic prototype in an engineering lab that does not yet work to spec: clip on scope probes and current shunts, flash and re-flash firmware, tune gains, swap components, cut and re-solder traces or re-crimp connectors, re-shim mechanics, iterating between hardware and code until behavior meets the requirement.

Run a defined validation/qualification protocol on a completed prototype at a purpose-built rig in a test lab or proving ground: mount and instrument the unit, then execute endurance, thermal-chamber, EMC, load or vehicle-dynamics test sequences and log the data for the report.

Install, commission and test the design on a customer or in-house production floor: mount and wire sensors, drives and safety devices onto an existing machine or line, verify I/O point-by-point, download and tune PLC/motion programs, run dry cycles and first-article parts, and troubleshoot faults alongside maintenance and operators while adjacent production continues.

Field trial of the system in its intended real-world setting (customer site, vehicle, farm, construction yard, outdoor installation): deploy the hardware as found, run it under real loads, weather and clutter, observe failures, and make on-the-spot mechanical, wiring or parameter adjustments.

instances.label: Routine monitoring rounds of automated production equipment on the plant floor: walking the line and the machine rooms, observing machines in operation, reading gauges/indicators/HMI screens, checking for hot bearings, abnormal noise/vibration, leaks or misfeeds, logging readings and flagging anomalies that threaten throughput.

Calibration and verification of instruments and system components — pressure/temperature transmitters, load cells, flow meters, proximity and photoelectric sensors — either in place on installed plant equipment or on a bench in the instrument shop/test lab: hooking up a reference calibrator or test rig, applying reference inputs, comparing and trimming zero/span, documenting results in the calibration system.

Calibrating and aligning robot/vision components inside an automation cell to restore production accuracy after drift, a crash or component replacement: TCP/tool calibration, joint mastering recovery, hand-eye/vision calibration, verification runs against reference features, updating offsets in the controller.

Monitoring a machine's process data and tuning its control parameters to maximize throughput without losing quality: watching spindle load/cycle-time/quality trends, adjusting feeds, servo gains, PID setpoints and timing, then verifying the effect over subsequent cycles.

Hands-on tuning of a line after a changeover or a gradual performance loss: physically repositioning sensors and guides, re-tensioning belts, shimming and aligning mechanisms, swapping a worn component, then running trial batches, measuring cycle time and scrap, and iterating until the OEE target is met.

On-site commissioning, monitoring and calibration of a delivered automated system at a customer or remote installation (integrator/OEM-side work): unfamiliar and partially built layouts, retrofit conditions, temporary access, calibrating sensors and drives and tuning the system to acceptance criteria.

instances.label: Wafer-level characterization of a MEMS lot (e.g., resonators, inertial or pressure sensors) in a cleanroom/fab probe bay: wafers in SEMI cassettes are loaded on an automated probe station, an existing recipe runs electrical parametrics plus optical/laser-Doppler dynamic measurements die by die, and wafer maps and process-variation statistics are produced for the design team.

Bespoke bench characterization/debug of a new prototype in an R&D lab: the engineer builds a one-off rig (mounts the die or module, wire-bonds or sockets it onto a carrier board, cables instruments, aligns an interferometer/vibrometer or positions manual probes), then iterates the setup as unexpected results appear, and interprets the data.

Characterization and calibration of packaged MEMS sensors across temperature with applied physical stimulus (rate table for gyros, pressure/vacuum for pressure sensors, acoustic chamber for microphones, magnetic coils), devices supplied in JEDEC trays or fixtures, running automated tri-temperature sequences and writing calibration coefficients / spec compliance reports.

Accelerated aging campaign at wafer or die level: burn-in / HTOL style voltage-temperature stress with automated stress-and-test hardware, pre- and post-stress parametric comparison, and lifetime/early-failure statistics.

Board-level harsh-environment qualification campaign: populate and solder DUT boards or socket parts, cable them and instrument them, load thermal-cycling / thermal-shock / 85C-85%RH / HAST chambers, pull samples for interim electrical readouts over days-to-weeks, and inspect and document failures (optical/X-ray/CSAM).

Mechanical shock, vibration and drop qualification of packaged MEMS devices: bolt DUTs and their boards to a shaker or shock table fixture, bond accelerometers and route cabling, run the standard profiles, and perform pre/post functional and parametric checks.

Field trial of prototype devices in real-world use: install units in a vehicle, industrial plant, outdoor site or on a wearer, verify installation, monitor and retrieve logged data over weeks, troubleshoot failures in situ and recover the hardware.

instances.label: Running a prototype MEMS lot through an R&D/university or corporate development cleanroom: solvent/RCA cleans, resist spin, mask-aligner or stepper exposure, develop, DRIE/RIE etch, PVD/LPCVD/ALD deposition, resist strip; few wafers or cleaved coupons, custom non-standard steps, recipe tweaks between runs.

In-line metrology and inspection to verify the prototype meets specification: film thickness (ellipsometer/reflectometer), CD and profile measurement (optical, SEM, profilometer), etch-depth and membrane-thickness checks, particle/defect inspection, recording data against spec limits and deciding rework/scrap.

Prototype die release, assembly, packaging and characterization: dicing, MEMS release and dry, die attach, wire bonding, cap/lid seal, then wafer-level or packaged electrical/functional probe test and characterization of the prototype device.

Overseeing others conducting the work: directing technicians or a MEMS foundry running the process, walking the line, watching tool operation and operator technique, reviewing run cards/SPC charts and excursion reports, approving travelers and deviations, directing corrective action.

Transferring the prototype process to a pilot/production line: running split lots and qualification wafers on production tools in an automated 200/300 mm fab, monitoring yields, and adjusting process windows to promote effective production.

tasks.label: Conduct experimental or virtual studies to investigate characteristics and processing principles of potential microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) technology.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Virtual study only: engineer builds and runs multiphysics/FEA models (COMSOL, CoventorWare, ANSYS) of a candidate MEMS device or process — parametric sweeps of geometry, damping, residual stress, electrostatic pull-in — calibrates against literature data and writes up characteristics. Done at a workstation in an engineering office; no physical artifact is touched.

Fabrication-process characterization experiment in a cleanroom (research fab or pilot line): split-lot wafers through resist spin/expose/develop, thin-film deposition (sputter/PECVD/ALD) and DRIE etch at varied parameters, followed by in-line metrology (profilometry, ellipsometry, SEM) to extract etch rates, film stress, selectivity and other processing principles.

Device characterization of fabricated prototypes: die or wafer mounted on a probe station or bench rig, electrically driven and measured (capacitance, resonance frequency, Q, sensitivity) with laser Doppler vibrometry, network analyzers, vacuum chamber or shaker; data reduced to device characteristics.

Materials/failure analysis supporting the study: FIB cross-sectioning and SEM/TEM imaging of released structures, stiction or sidewall-profile inspection, film microstructure and residual-stress test structures; images and measurements interpreted to explain process behavior.

Reliability/environmental study of prototype MEMS: packaged parts fixtured into thermal chambers, shock/vibration rigs or pressure/humidity stimuli, cycled over temperature and time while sensor output drift, offset and failure modes are logged and analyzed.

Refining or re-specifying a production recipe from experimental and metrology data: designing a DOE, interpreting yield/CD/stress/etch-profile results supplied by the fab, and issuing revised process parameters and control limits.

Devising a monolithic CMOS-MEMS integration scheme (pre-, intra-, or post-CMOS): specifying thermal budget, materials compatibility, and step ordering so MEMS structures can be built alongside the IC, then documenting the integrated flow and design rules for the manufacturing partner.

instances.label: R&D bench characterization of a prototype photonic component or subassembly (PIC, laser diode, fiber-coupled module, free-space optic) in an optics lab: the engineer builds a one-off setup on an optical table, mounts and aligns the device to fibers or beams, cables up sources, power meters, OSA and scope, sweeps drive current/wavelength/temperature, records loss, spectra, LIV and bandwidth, and iterates when the setup misbehaves.

End-of-line and design-verification testing of packaged photonic products (optical transceivers, lidar sensor heads, laser modules, camera/optical assemblies) on a manufacturing test floor: units are presented in trays or nests, optically and electrically connected, and run through functional, alignment, beam/spectral and performance-limit sequences with pass/fail sorting.

Environmental and reliability limit testing in a reliability lab: devices loaded into burn-in racks, thermal chambers or wafer-level burn-in systems, driven at elevated current/temperature for hours to weeks, with periodic LIV/spectral/power measurements to establish drift, wear-out and operating limits.

Installed optical link and network-level testing inside a data center, central office or integration facility: verifying end-to-end links through patch panels and cross-connects, measuring insertion loss, running OTDR traces and BER/power checks, and documenting results for acceptance or troubleshooting.

Field testing of deployed photonic systems outside a controlled facility: outside-plant fiber spans, customer-premises installations, or outdoor trials of lidar/laser rangefinding systems, measured under weather, ambient light, vibration and site-to-site layout variation.

instances.label: R&D optics lab: build and characterize a bench prototype of a laser/optical sensing head for a production line, using standard catalog free-space optics (lasers, lenses, mirrors, polarizers, detectors) on an optical table — assemble the configuration, align it, and run characterization sweeps (beam profile, sensitivity, noise, spectral response) against reference samples, iterating the layout.

R&D optics lab/shop: build a custom prototype sensing module — machined optomechanics, fiber splicing/pigtailing, detector electronics and wiring, embedded acquisition code, potting/enclosure — then bench-test on real production samples, diagnose anomalies and redesign parts for a manufacturable version.

Laser applications lab / process-development cell: closed-loop parameter optimization for a laser manufacturing process (marking, texturing, annealing, thin-film processing) using an automated stage-and-laser platform with in-line optical characterization; run large parameter matrices to find the recipe that maximizes throughput/quality.

Laser applications lab: process development on real production parts — fixture awkward workpieces, run welding/cutting/drilling trials with gas and clamping variations, section and metallographically inspect coupons, judge spatter/porosity/HAZ, and define a validated process window and cycle-time improvement for manufacturing.

Cleanroom / photonic packaging facility: develop and qualify a photonic device manufacturing process (PIC fiber-attach, laser diode packaging, wafer-level optical test) — design DOEs, tune active-alignment and attach recipes on the assembly machine, analyze yield and failure modes, specify tooling, and release the process.

Factory floor pilot: install and commission the developed photonics sensing/laser system on a live production line — mount hardware and enclosures, route cabling and interlocks, align to moving product, calibrate against reference gauges, tune for vibration, dust and ambient light, validate gauge R&R and hand off to operators.

Customer/supplier site or outdoor industrial asset: deploy and troubleshoot fiber-optic or laser-based sensing (distributed temperature/strain, process spectroscopy) in as-found conditions — route and splice fiber, mount optics in awkward locations, diagnose intermittent signal faults, and adapt the design to the site.

instances.label: Optical design of the beam delivery train for a high-speed ablation machine (source-to-workpiece): beam expander, galvo scanner, f-theta objective. Engineer builds and optimizes the layout in optical design software (Zemax/CODE V), runs spot-size, fluence, thermal-lensing and tolerance analyses, and issues an optical prescription and drawings. Output is a design package reviewed by colleagues.

Specifying the laser source and process window for a customer's ablation application (e.g., ultrafast picosecond/femtosecond source for thin-film patterning or micro-drilling): trading off wavelength, pulse duration, repetition rate, fluence, and scan speed against throughput and heat-affected-zone requirements, then writing the requirements/specification document and vendor selection rationale.

Machine-level integration design: laying out the opto-mechanical assembly with motion stages, chiller, fume extraction, vision alignment and control electronics in CAD; designing the Class 1 laser-safe enclosure, interlocks and beam dumps; producing assembly models, BOM, wiring/control architecture and compliance documentation.

Design iteration driven by prototype or process-trial data: reviewing ablation-rate, edge-quality, and taper measurements and scanner-calibration data, diagnosing the cause (e.g., pulse overlap, focal shift, scanner distortion), and revising the optical, control, or mechanical design accordingly; documenting the engineering change.

Design reviews and documentation deliverables: preparing and presenting the design to peers, safety officers and customers, resolving review comments, updating drawings, interface control documents, cost estimates and manufacturing/service documentation for release.

tasks.label: Select, purchase, set up, operate, or troubleshoot state-of-the-art laser cutting equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Running production/qualification cutting work on an existing state-of-the-art laser cutting system (2D fiber flatbed, tube laser, or laser dicing/micromachining tool) in a plant, fab or pilot line: load material or cassette, call up the nested/parameterized program, run the job, watch the cut, unload and verify parts meet dimensional and edge-quality spec.

Job setup and cutting-process/parameter development for a new part, material grade or thickness on existing equipment: choose nozzle/lens/assist gas, set focus and standoff, verify beam centering, run test coupons, inspect kerf/edge quality and iterate parameters until first articles are accepted and the recipe is released.

Troubleshooting cut-quality deterioration while the machine is running production: burr/dross, incomplete cuts, tip-ups or pierce failures caused by nozzle wear, focus drift, feed rate versus material variation (rust, coating, thickness tolerance); detect the cause and restore acceptable cuts without scrapping the job.

Diagnosing and repairing hardware/subsystem faults on the laser cutting equipment: contaminated or cracked protective glass and focusing optics, damaged fiber connector or beam-delivery misalignment, chiller/assist-gas/exhaust problems, drive and controller error codes — requiring disassembly, cleaning or component replacement, re-alignment and re-qualification.

Installing and commissioning newly purchased laser cutting equipment (industrial cell or lab micromachining workstation): positioning and leveling, connecting power, chiller, assist gas and fume extraction, mounting/aligning beam delivery, scanner and focusing optics on the bench, verifying enclosure interlocks and laser-safety compliance, calibrating axes and running acceptance cuts.

Selecting and purchasing equipment: writing the technical specification (power, beam quality, wavelength, cut range, tolerances, throughput), evaluating vendor proposals, sending benchmark parts to suppliers, physically inspecting and measuring returned benchmark cut samples, negotiating and issuing the purchase order with acceptance criteria.

Building, integrating and configuring a robotic application/work cell on a production or customer floor: bolting the robot and end-of-arm tool in place, wiring I/O and safety devices, installing fixtures and vision hardware, teaching and tuning paths until the cell passes an acceptance run.

Bench and rig testing/debugging of a development unit in the lab: fixturing it, adding instrumentation (load cells, trackers, scopes), running functional, payload and endurance protocols, diagnosing unexpected faults, swapping parts and re-running.

Bring-up and configuration of a standard, already-designed robot unit: mating power/comm connectors, loading firmware and parameter sets, executing calibration routines (mastering, TCP, payload, hand-eye) and a scripted functional checkout with pass/fail criteria.

Protocol-driven validation/endurance test campaigns at a company test facility or proving ground: repeated scripted scenario runs, duty-cycle or mileage accumulation on the robot/robotic vehicle, with automatic data capture and monitoring.

Field trial of a robot in an unstructured target environment (farm field, construction site, public sidewalk, customer home): setting the machine up on site, supervising runs, recovering failures, tweaking configuration and collecting data over changing conditions.

tasks.label: Investigate mechanical failures or unexpected maintenance problems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Production floor of a manufacturing plant: a fenced industrial robot cell faults unexpectedly (servo overload, position/encoder error, gripper or tool-changer failure, suspected collision damage). The robotics engineer performs lockout/tagout, enters the cell, reads controller alarms and torque/current traces, jogs axes by hand and by pendant, inspects cabling, dress packs, fasteners, brakes and gearbox backlash, runs functional tests, isolates the root cause, and verifies the fix before release to production.

R&D lab or failure-analysis bench: a prototype joint module or a returned/failed actuator, harness or end effector is investigated. The engineer disassembles the unit with hand tools, inspects bearings, gear teeth, seals and fracture/wear surfaces (loupe, microscope, calipers, torque checks), re-runs the unit instrumented on a test rig, correlates with design data, and writes a root-cause report with corrective action.

Field service at a customer's structured facility (fulfillment center, warehouse with an AMR/ASRS fleet, or an automated assembly line at an integrator's customer): a robot shows intermittent drive-wheel noise, lift-mechanism stalling, or repeated aborts. The engineer works on-site amid racking and moving traffic, reproduces the fault, swaps suspect components, measures, and determines the cause across mechanical, electrical and software factors.

Field investigation in an unstructured setting: an agricultural, construction, inspection, or service robot fails in the field, at a construction site, or in a residential/customer-owned environment. The engineer inspects the damaged machine as found — mud, weather, uneven ground, unknown local modifications and layout — recovers/opens it, checks mechanical damage and contamination, and determines what failed and why.

Office/desk and remote investigation: engineer pulls robot telemetry, controller error logs, joint current and vibration data, and camera footage of the incident, cross-references maintenance and parts history and CAD/ECO records, remotely interrogates the machine, directs an on-site technician through checks by phone/video, and issues the root-cause finding and corrective action.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Integrator's build bay / customer shop floor: engineer integrates an arc-welding package onto an industrial arm — mounts torch and wire feeder, routes the dress pack, wires the weld power source to the robot controller, configures the fieldbus (EtherNet/IP, DeviceNet) and analog/digital I/O, then runs and tunes test welds until the joint passes inspection.

R&D lab / bench: engineer integrates a new peripheral onto an arm or mobile base — machines or fits an adapter plate, mounts a gripper, force sensor or 3D camera, runs power and signal cabling, installs/writes the driver, does hand-eye and TCP calibration, and verifies the device responds correctly end to end.

On-site commissioning at a customer plant: engineer ties the robot to surrounding equipment — lands I/O to a PLC, conveyors, fixtures, light curtains and E-stops, wires and labels the control panel, verifies each signal with a meter/HMI, debugs mismatched addresses and timing, and signs off the interlocked cell.

Repeat build of an already-proven, standardized cell in the integrator's build area: bolt pre-designed brackets and a known end-effector to the arm, plug pre-made harnesses and pneumatic lines into keyed connectors, load the standard configuration, and run a scripted acceptance/validation routine.

Field integration on a mobile or outdoor machine (AMR, agricultural implement carrier, construction platform): mount a lidar/GNSS unit or implement on the vehicle, run and weatherproof cabling to the controller, configure the interface, and validate operation in situ on the yard, field or site.

instances.label: Install and commission a new industrial robot or robot cell at a production site: uncrate and rig the manipulator, bolt the base to a pedestal/floor, route and land power, signal and air lines to the controller, mount and plumb the end-of-arm tool, install guarding/light curtains and safety I/O, power up, set zero position, and verify first motion programs against the machine tool or conveyor it serves.

Calibrate an industrial robot arm inside its production cell: define/refresh the tool center point after a torch, nozzle or gripper change or a collision, identify tool and payload data, set work-object and vision frames, and verify positional accuracy before releasing the cell back to production.

Bring up and calibrate a mobile, legged, or field robot in a lab or at a customer site: joint/kinematic zeroing after a hardware change, camera and LiDAR extrinsic calibration, gripper calibration, and verification runs on the shop or lab floor.

Operate a robot system so it carries out its intended work over a long run: start a production cell for an unattended shift, dispatch an inspection drone or mobile robot on its route, or run an endurance/validation cycle, including startup checks, keeping the machine powered and serviced, and returning it to the run after routine stops.

Hands-on operation of robots for development, integration testing, and demonstrations: rig the test setup, jog and teach positions on the pendant or via API, run experimental controllers and trials, swap payloads and sensors between runs, catch and recover the robot when a trial fails, and iterate on hardware/software.

Maintain and repair robots: scheduled preventive maintenance (grease and gearbox oil changes, cable dress-pack inspection, controller battery replacement), and corrective repair — diagnose a fault, replace a servo motor, encoder, harmonic drive, belt or damaged harness, re-master the axes, and verify the robot back into service in a plant, lab, or field location.

instances.label: Biotech/pharma or CRO lab: implement a straightforward liquid-handling assay on a benchtop handler (OT-2/Flex, Biomek, Fluent) — serial dilution series, reagent addition, mixing, absorbance/fluorescence readout. Engineer writes the method, lays out the deck with tips/plates/reservoirs, runs a water dry-run, iterates, and hands over a working protocol.

Build a complex multi-instrument automated assay (ELISA with plate washer and incubator, NGS library prep with thermal cycler and magnet, cell-based screen) — deck and workcell design, scheduling with timed incubations, error handling and recovery, then validation against the manual method and documentation for production use.

Develop and verify pipetting performance for the assay's reagents: build/tune liquid classes for water, DMSO, plasma, viscous or volatile liquids across the assay's volume range using gravimetric (on-deck balance) or photometric (dye) testing, iterate parameters until accuracy/precision criteria are met, and issue a verification report.

Physically integrate and commission an assay workcell: mount/dock a plate reader, washer, incubator or shaker around a plate-handling arm, cable and configure drivers, teach or verify arm hand-off positions and nests, and prove reliable plate transfers through the whole assay sequence in the lab bay.

Run the finished automated assay for validation or production: load real reagents, cells, samples, tips and plates; start and monitor the run; handle mid-run interventions; collect and export the data; compare results with the manual assay to demonstrate equivalence.

Support a deployed automated assay: diagnose failures (tip pickup errors, clot/liquid-level detection faults, plate misalignment, gripper crashes, scheduler deadlocks) at the bench, replace or re-seat hardware, re-teach positions after a repair, patch the method, and requalify.

instances.label: Colloidal/solution-phase nanomaterial research campaign in a university or corporate wet lab: dispensing precursors and solvents, dispersing/sonicating nanoparticles or growing quantum dots, then measuring absorbance, photoluminescence/fluorescence and particle size, and iterating the formulation across a defined parameter space to hit a target property.

Advanced microscopy/spectroscopy characterization study: preparing specimens (FIB lamella, grids, mounted coupons), loading them into TEM/SEM/SPM, acquiring images and spectra at selected regions of interest, and analyzing structure at the nanoscale.

tasks.label: Synthesize, process, or characterize nanomaterials, using advanced tools or techniques.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine solution-phase preparation and processing of nanomaterial dispersions/formulations at the bench in a research wet-chemistry lab: weigh and dispense powders and solvents into standard vialware, mix/sonicate/disperse, and run a property measurement (UV-vis, DLS, GC/HPLC readout) on shared benchtop instruments. Recipe is established; the campaign varies composition across many samples.

Bench synthesis of a nanomaterial by an established but demanding recipe: heated reaction (hot-injection colloidal QDs/metal nanoparticles, hydrothermal autoclave, or solid-state calcination), inert-atmosphere or sealed-vessel operation, then purification by centrifugation/washing/drying and a phase- or size-check (XRD, UV-vis, TEM grid prep).

Non-routine work: developing a new synthesis or process, or diagnosing an unexpected result. Requires assembling or modifying apparatus (Schlenk line, custom reactor, glovebox air-sensitive handling), improvising when a step fails, and choosing and interpreting characterization of an unknown or artifact-prone specimen.

Cleanroom / thin-film nanofabrication processing of substrates: solution coating or vacuum deposition, patterning, anneal/etch, followed by in-line metrology (thickness, conductivity, defect imaging) to confirm the film or structure meets spec. Substrates are standard wafers or coupons handled in a class-controlled cleanroom.

Routine characterization runs on advanced instruments in a shared instrument facility: mount/load a standard-format specimen (wafer, stub, grid, powder holder), prepare the site if needed (FIB lamella), align and acquire SEM/TEM/AFM/XRD data, quantify dimensions or phase, and report numbers against spec.

Pilot-scale processing / scale-up run: producing a batch of nanomaterial to specification on process equipment (continuous-flow or microfluidic formulation, milling/dispersion, spray drying, coating line), with in-process monitoring, sampling and batch documentation in a pilot plant or GMP suite.

instances.label: Closed-loop bench testing of a new nanomaterial formulation in a corporate or university R&D wet lab: the engineer lays out a design of experiments, weighs solid precursors and dispenses solvents/ligands into vials or a small flow reactor, runs reactions on hotplates/sonicators, then screens each batch with standard readouts (UV-Vis, photoluminescence, DLS/zeta, sometimes benchtop XRD), and iterates the recipe over days until target properties are met. Standard glassware and commercial benchtop instruments; lab shared with other researchers.

Bespoke bench-top test of a new nanotech product/process: the engineer builds a one-off setup (mounting a prototype nanosensor or nanocomposite coupon, wiring probes/electrodes, plumbing a gas or fluid line, aligning a laser or fixture), debugs it, runs the measurement, and troubleshoots unexpected behavior. Setup and sample geometry differ from test to test; done at a bench or fume hood in an R&D lab.

Nanofabrication process/device test in an industrial cleanroom line: split lots of wafers are run through deposition/lithography/etch steps to evaluate a new process, then measured with in-line metrology (film thickness, CD-SEM, defect inspection/review) and wafer-level DC/RF parametric test on a probe station; results are compared against the process-qualification criteria the engineer defined.

Nanoscale characterization campaign on a new sample set in a research or analytical lab: preparing specimens (dispersing powder on TEM grids, cleaving/mounting a chip, FIB lamella extraction), booking and aligning shared instruments (SEM, TEM/STEM, AFM, XPS, Raman), acquiring images/spectra at representative sites, and interpreting them into a characterization test report.

Performance and reliability testing of a prototype nanotechnology product in a test lab: loading coupons, cells or specimens into fixtures and running mechanical (tensile, nanoindentation, adhesion), environmental (thermal cycling, humidity, accelerated weathering) or electrical cycling tests over long durations, logging data and comparing against acceptance specs.

Scale-up or field validation of a nanotech product: trials on a pilot coating/dispersion line at a partner plant, or testing product samples in situ at a customer site or in outdoor exposure racks, where the layout, equipment and conditions are taken as found and the engineer improvises instrumentation and sampling.

One-off benchtop instrument build: assembling a custom scanning-probe head or test rig from machined brackets, piezo stacks, cabling, connectors and optics; fitting, wiring, gluing, adjusting and debugging a unique mechanical/electromechanical assembly on a lab bench.

instances.label: Cleanroom nanofabrication: develop and qualify a device fabrication process (lithography/resist, etch, liftoff, deposition, CMP) for production of a nanoscale device. Engineer runs split lots on shared or production fab tools, prepares samples, adjusts tool hardware and recipes, takes CD-SEM/ellipsometry/AFM metrology, iterates a DOE, then fixes the process window and releases a spec. Multi-step flow across many separate tools; substrates and chemistries change project to project.

Transfer and qualification of a nanotech process onto a pilot or production line (wafer/parts plating line, epoxy dispense-and-cure station, roll or slot-die coater): install and tune the process on production equipment, run capability/qualification lots, set control limits, troubleshoot yield or defect excursions with operators, write SOPs and travelers.

Bench/pilot closed-loop recipe development for a nanomaterial synthesis or film-growth process (CVD nanotube or 2D-material growth, ALD/PLD/sputter film, colloidal nanocrystal synthesis): iterate growth parameters (temperature, pressure, precursor flows, pulse timing) with in-situ or offline characterization until the targeted growth rate/phase/property is hit, then document the recipe for production use.

Solution-processing / coating process development for nanostructured functional films (conductive polymer or nanoparticle inks): optimize solution formulation, coating speed, substrate temperature, doping and anneal to hit conductivity/uniformity/defect targets on coupons, and hand off a scale-up coating recipe.

Bench electroplating/electrodeposition process development for nanoscale coatings or features: vary bath composition and additives, current density/pulse waveform and time on coupons or small substrates, measure film properties (thickness, morphology, optical/electrochemical response), and converge on a deposition recipe and process window.

Bench epoxy/nanocomposite process development: disperse nanofiller in resin, dose and mix components, apply/bond or mold specimens, run cure schedules, test adhesion or mechanical performance, and iterate formulation and cure profile to a spec.

tasks.label: Apply nanotechnology to improve the performance or reduce the environmental impact of energy products, such as fuel cells or solar cells.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Solar-cell improvement loop in an R&D lab/glovebox: formulate nanostructured precursor inks and additives (perovskite, quantum-dot, organic, or nano-textured layers), deposit layers by spin/blade coating and evaporation, finish the device stack, measure J-V under a solar simulator plus stability, and iterate recipes to raise efficiency and durability.

Wet-chemistry synthesis and screening of nanomaterials for hydrogen/fuel-cell/photocatalytic energy applications: weigh powders and precursors, make dispersions and solutions in a fume hood or glovebox, heat/centrifuge/dry, screen activity of many formulations, and iterate the composition search.

Fuel-cell or electrolyzer device build and test: prepare nanoparticle catalyst inks, coat electrodes or membranes, assemble the MEA/cell hardware, then run polarization curves, EIS and durability protocols on a test stand and feed results back into the nanomaterial design.

Nanostructure characterization and diagnostics of energy-device samples: prepare and mount films/powders, run XRD, electron microscopy, profilometry and spectroscopy (often in a shared user facility), and correlate nanoscale structure with device performance or degradation/failure.

Scale-up and pilot-line integration: take the improved nanomaterial process to larger-area coating and module/stack fabrication on pilot or production equipment, run trials, diagnose defects and yield loss on the floor, and verify performance of the scaled product.

tasks.label: Reengineer nanomaterials to improve biodegradability.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Nanomedicine/biomaterials wet lab: tune the composition of an established degradable nanocarrier family (e.g., PLGA lactide:glycolide ratio, polyester block length, ester-containing ionizable lipid tails, PEG density) so the particle clears/degrades faster. Engineer plans a variant matrix, makes batches by nanoprecipitation/microfluidic mixing or flow polymerization, characterizes size/PDI/molar mass (DLS, GPC, NMR), runs accelerated hydrolytic/enzymatic degradation time-courses in buffer or serum, and iterates to a target degradation profile.

Inorganic or carbon nanomaterial surface engineering in a fume-hood lab: re-coat or re-ligand silica, iron-oxide, quantum-dot, metal or CNT nanomaterials (degradable silica shells, biodegradable polymer coatings, doping) so they dissolve or clear. Involves wet synthesis, centrifuge/wash purification, UV-vis/TEM/DLS characterization and multi-day dissolution kinetics (supernatant sampling, ICP-MS), iterated over several coating variants.

Novel-chemistry redesign in a research lab: design and synthesize new degradable building blocks (cleavable linkers, disulfide/acetal crosslinkers, new monomers), run inert-atmosphere/Schlenk or glovebox polymerizations, purify, confirm structure across several instruments, and devise a bespoke degradation validation (enzyme cocktails, cell/biological media, cytotoxicity of degradation products), troubleshooting unexpected failures.

Industrial R&D/pilot facility: reformulate a nanocomposite product (nanocellulose or nano-additive filled bioplastic film, coating, nanofiber mat) for improved biodegradability — compound/extrude/cast samples, cut specimens, run standardized biodegradation tests (ISO 14855 composting respirometry, soil or seawater burial, disintegration), and retest mechanical/barrier properties on aged samples.

Scale-up and transfer of a reengineered biodegradable nanomaterial from bench to pilot/GMP production: adapt the formulation and process to production equipment (larger reactors, tangential-flow filtration, microfluidic manufacturing skids), sample batches, and verify that degradability and product specs are retained in QC batches.

sources.claim: LUMI-lab is a self-driving lab (two liquid handlers, robotic arm, cell incubator, plate reader) that autonomously proposed new ionizable lipid structures, synthesized them, formulated them into lipid nanoparticles, and screened >1,700 LNPs over ten active-learning cycles, finding lipids beating clinical benchmarks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: closed-loop redesign of nanocarrier chemistry against a measured property (transfection potency) rather than degradability. Transfer holds because the objects (lipid nanoparticles), the chemical levers (lipid tail/linker structure — the same levers used to make lipids ester-cleavable/biodegradable), the wet-lab unit operations (dispensing, reaction, formulation, plate-based assay) and the design-make-test-analyze loop are the same; only the assay readout differs.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous optimisation of polymer nanoparticle composition, molar mass distribution and particle size. Transfer holds because hydrolytic degradation rate of polyester/polymer nanocarriers is governed by exactly these variables (comonomer ratio, molar mass, particle size), and the platform already runs the same synthesis-plus-characterisation loop with the GPC and DLS instruments used to follow degradation.

Transfer holds because coating/ligand modification for dissolution uses the same unit operations the platform automates (dispensing, heated agitation, centrifugal washing, spectroscopic readout) on the same class of nanomaterials.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous synthetic chemistry campaigns in a human-occupied laboratory. Cited to bound the E2 case: the demonstrations cover molecular synthesis and analysis decisions, not nanoparticle formulation plus multi-day degradation validation, so they do not substantiate completion of this task's instances outside a purpose-built platform.

tasks.label: Integrate nanotechnology with antimicrobial properties into products, such as household or medical appliances, to reduce the development of bacteria or other microbes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: R&D lab bench work: formulating and synthesizing the antimicrobial nanomaterial itself (silver, copper or ZnO nanoparticle dispersions, silane-silver solutions) — weighing precursors, dispensing reagents, sonicating/stirring vials, varying loading and stabilizer chemistry, and running UV-vis/DLS characterization to hit a target particle size and stability spec for a household-appliance or medical-device product.

Lab-scale integration onto the product substrate: dip-, spin-, or ultrasonic-spray coating the nanomaterial onto coupons and prototype parts (appliance polymer panels, door handles, catheter tubing), curing/annealing, then checking coating thickness, uniformity, adhesion and wash durability in a coatings lab or small cleanroom.

Antimicrobial efficacy testing in a microbiology lab (ISO 22196 / JIS Z 2801 or suspension kill / MIC assays): preparing bacterial inocula, inoculating treated and control coupons, incubating, recovering and serially diluting, plating on agar, incubating and counting colonies, computing log reduction against the untreated control.

Pilot-scale trial: compounding an antimicrobial nanoparticle masterbatch into the product resin and running an injection-molding or extrusion trial in a pilot plant — dosing the additive, running the machine at trial settings, extracting parts, and pulling sample parts for dispersion and efficacy checks.

Transfer and qualification of the antimicrobial process on a contract manufacturer's or OEM's production line (appliance plant or medical-device facility): installing/adjusting spray or dip coating equipment on the existing line, running qualification lots, troubleshooting defects at the line, and signing off the process.

Validation of the finished product in use conditions: assembling the treated component into a working appliance or device, then swabbing and sampling surfaces of installed units in a clinic, kitchen or other in-use setting over time to confirm reduced microbial load.

tasks.label: Develop catalysis or other green chemistry methods to synthesize nanomaterials, such as nanotubes, nanocrystals, nanorods, or nanowires.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Closed-loop optimization of a solution-phase nanocrystal/nanorod synthesis in an R&D wet lab: vary precursor, reductant, surfactant, temperature and time to hit a target size/shape/optical property while cutting hazardous reagent, solvent or energy use; tens to hundreds of vial-scale runs judged by UV-vis/DLS feedback.

Exploratory bench synthesis in a fume hood with non-standardized chemistry: trying a green reductant/capping agent (ascorbate, biopolymer, plant extract), air-free hot-injection on a Schlenk line, ad hoc glassware, dealing with batches that gel, foam or crash out, then centrifuge-wash-redisperse workup.

Catalytic vapor-phase growth of nanotubes or nanowires: deposit/condition the metal catalyst, load substrates into a CVD tube furnace, run temperature and gas-flow programs, monitor growth in situ, and iterate toward lower-temperature or bio-derived-feedstock (greener) growth conditions.

Verification loop using diffraction and spectroscopy integrated with the synthesis: dose/heat powders or solutions, run XRD, UV-vis or similar, identify the phase/product obtained, and revise the recipe accordingly.

Electron-microscopy morphology verification: prepare TEM grids or SEM stubs from the colloid (dilute, drop-cast, blot, dry), image on a shared-facility microscope, measure size/shape distributions and aspect ratios, and decide what to change in the synthesis.

Scale-up and green-metric validation of a developed recipe: move it from vials to a larger batch reactor or a continuous-flow line in a kilo/pilot lab, check reproducibility and yield over extended runs, and tune the process for solvent recovery, throughput and waste (E-factor).

tasks.label: Design nanoparticle catalysts to detect or remove chemical or other pollutants from water, soil, or air.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Computational design and screening of a photocatalytic nanoparticle (e.g., doped TiO2 or metal-oxide heterojunction) for degrading organic contaminants in wastewater: reviewing literature and prior in-house data, running DFT/kinetic or materials-informatics screens at a workstation, and specifying composition, particle size, dopant loading, and morphology in a design record.

Designing a nanoparticle formulation for soil/groundwater remediation (e.g., nanoscale zero-valent iron with a polymer coating and catalytic dopant) at an environmental engineering or materials firm: selecting core/shell chemistry, surface stabilizers, and support, and documenting the specification and intended synthesis route for the lab or vendor to produce.

Designing a nanoparticle catalyst/sensing element for detecting an air pollutant (e.g., NOx, VOC, or ozone) in a chemiresistive or electrochemical sensor: specifying the catalytic nanomaterial, loading, film thickness, and operating temperature as a materials stack definition for the device team.

Iterating an existing catalyst design against test data: interpreting characterization and performance results (XRD, BET, TEM, degradation-rate curves) returned from technicians or a pilot, then revising composition, loading, or support and issuing updated design parameters for the next synthesis batch.

Producing the design deliverables around the catalyst concept: writing the design specification, tolerance and safety/regulatory notes, cost and scale-up assumptions, and presenting the design in a review with the project team, client, or regulator.

tasks.label: Develop green building nanocoatings, such as self-cleaning, anti-stain, depolluting, anti-fogging, anti-icing, antimicrobial, moisture-resistant, or ultraviolet protectant coatings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench formulation/synthesis in an R&D wet-chemistry lab: gravimetrically weighing nano-powders (TiO2, silica, ZnO, Ag) in a fume hood, adding solvents, silanes, binders and dispersants, high-shear mixing/sonication, pH and stability adjustment, and bottling candidate green-building coating formulations for screening.

Depositing the candidate formulations onto small test coupons (glass, ceramic tile, mortar, coated aluminum, wood) by spin, dip, spray or drawdown bar, then flash-off, curing/annealing on a hotplate or in an oven, and labeling/storing the sample set.

Instrumented characterization of the coated coupons: water/oil contact angle and roll-off (anti-fogging, self-cleaning, moisture resistance), UV-vis transmission/haze and UV-blocking, gloss/color, film thickness, and optical/electron imaging for defects and coverage uniformity.

Functional efficacy assays: photocatalytic self-cleaning/depolluting activity (dye or NOx degradation under UV with spectroscopic readout) and antimicrobial efficacy (inoculating coupons, incubating, recovering, plating and counting colonies).

Durability qualification of coated coupons: loading and cycling QUV/xenon accelerated weathering, Taber abrasion and scratch tests, cross-hatch/pull-off adhesion, freeze-thaw and ice-adhesion rigs, with before/after property measurement.

Scale-up and field validation: applying the down-selected formulation to full-size building substrates (facade panels, glazing units, concrete walls) at a pilot line, applicator's booth or building mockup, then mounting outdoor exposure racks and returning periodically to inspect, measure and sample in-place performance.

sources.system: Mobile robotic chemist (KUKA LBR iiwa on mobile base)
sources.title: A mobile robotic chemist (Nature 583, 237-241)
sources.claim: A free-roaming KUKA mobile manipulator worked autonomously for eight days in an otherwise unmodified university wet-chemistry lab, performing 688 photocatalyst formulation experiments: gravimetric solid dispensing, liquid dispensing, vial capping, sonication, irradiation and chromatographic readout, choosing its own next experiments by Bayesian optimization.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: optimizing photocatalyst mixtures. It uses the same physical operations and objects as nanocoating formulation and photocatalytic (self-cleaning/depolluting) screening — weighing nanopowder solids, dispensing liquids into vials, sonicating dispersions, irradiating samples and reading out activity — at the same milligram/microlitre precision, in an ordinary lab.

sources.system: Polybot

sources.title: Polybot - The Center for Nanoscale Materials
sources.claim: Polybot, an autonomous discovery platform at Argonne's Center for Nanoscale Materials, performs materials synthesis, thin-film fabrication, robotic sample transfer between stations, and automated characterization and testing; it comprises enclosed robotic solution-processing frames with a blade-coating station and heating stage, a Chemspeed synthesis robot, an MIR200/UR5e mobile manipulator, and automated imaging, UV-vis and electrical characterization.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous processing/characterization of electronic polymer thin films. The physical acts (blade-coating a solution onto a substrate, annealing, imaging for coating defects, optical/UV-vis measurement) are the same acts used to deposit and characterize functional building nanocoatings on coupons.

sources.system: Polybot
sources.title: Self-driving lab transforms materials discovery
sources.claim: Using Polybot, researchers autonomously explored solution-processing pathways and produced polymer films optimized simultaneously for conductivity and low coating-defect density, i.e. the robot deposited films and machine-scored their coating quality without human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: coating-defect optimization of polymer films. Automated deposition plus image-based defect/uniformity scoring is the same physical work as depositing candidate nanocoatings on coupons and inspecting coverage uniformity.

sources.system: Ada self-driving laboratory
sources.developer: University of British Columbia (Berlinguette group) / Acceleration Consortium
sources.title: Self-driving laboratory for accelerated discovery of thin-film materials (arXiv preprint of Sci. Adv. 6, eaaz8867)
sources.claim: Ada, a self-driving laboratory, autonomously spin-coats films from formulated inks, anneals them, images them and measures optical/electronic properties, closing the loop with an optimization algorithm that sets the next composition and processing conditions; campaigns of 35 samples ran in under 30 hours with about one failed sample each.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous thin-film discovery. Spin-coating a formulated solution onto a glass/ITO coupon, annealing it and measuring optical properties are the same operations, substrates and precision required for depositing and characterizing candidate building nanocoatings.

sources.system: Ada spray-coating self-driving laboratory
sources.title: A self-driving laboratory optimizes a scalable process for making functional coatings (Cell Reports Physical Science)
sources.claim: A self-driving laboratory autonomously optimized a scalable spray-coating process (91 closed-loop experiments, seven input variables including ink composition and nozzle parameters), producing films whose conductivity rivaled vacuum-sputtered coatings, and the optimized process was then scaled to an eight-times-larger area.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous optimization of a functional spray coating. Spray application of a liquid precursor onto substrates and measurement of the resulting film is the same physical workflow as spraying and evaluating a green-building nanocoating.

sources.system: Ada spray-coating self-driving laboratory

sources.transferJustification: Same system as the previous item; cited to establish that the demonstrated environment is a purpose-built robotic cell (E1) rather than an ordinary bench.

sources.system: APAS Independence

sources.claim: The APAS Independence, an automated plate assessment instrument that processes more than 200 culture plates ..., received FDA clearance as the first US-authorized instrument to automate reading, screening, interpretation and sorting ...; it is distributed by Thermo Fisher and used in clinical and pharma QC labs.

sources.system: In-situ contact angle monitoring module for autonomous spin coating
sources.developer: Fischer et al. (published in Advanced Intelligent Discovery, Wiley)
sources.title: In Situ Contact Angle Measurement for Autonomous Spin Coating in Self-Driving Labs
sources.claim: A vision-based monitoring module integrated into a commercial spin coater measures wetting/contact angle in situ and tracks substrate position, turning the spin coater into an autonomous material-screening module without a separate goniometer, with about 4 degrees agreement against commercial contact-angle instruments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated wettability measurement during self-driving-lab spin coating. Contact angle is the primary acceptance metric for self-cleaning, anti-fogging and moisture-resistant nanocoatings, measured on the same kind of coated coupon.

instances.label: Bench testing of electrical/electronic turbine subassemblies in a manufacturer's or research lab: converter modules, controller PCBs, pitch/yaw motors, cable harnesses and sensors checked with power analyzers, oscilloscopes, insulation/continuity testers and functional test rigs; parts are brought to the bench, wired up, run through a test script, and pass/fail data logged.

Materials and small-part mechanical testing in a lab: composite laminate coupons, adhesive bonds, bolts and cast samples loaded into universal testing/fatigue machines with extensometers and load cells, tested to standard, results reduced into a report.

Full-scale structural and drivetrain testing on purpose-built stands: blade static and resonant fatigue tests to IEC 61400-23, gearbox/generator/nacelle dynamometer runs, main-bearing rigs; the article is fixtured to the test block, instrumented, and cycled for weeks under a computer-controlled load program.

In-situ testing inside an installed turbine at an operating wind farm: climbing to the nacelle/hub, measuring insulation resistance and continuity, checking converter and pitch-system electronics, calibrating sensors, taking vibration and torque measurements during commissioning or troubleshooting, in a cramped enclosure at height with weather limits.

In-situ blade condition testing campaigns on operating turbines: surveying every blade for cracks, erosion, delamination and coating damage with imaging/thermographic equipment, outdoors at height, weather-dependent, producing a graded damage report for the operator.

In-situ contact testing on installed blades and structures: lightning-protection-system continuity/resistance measurement from tip receptors to earth, ultrasonic scans of spar caps and root bolts, performed from rope access or platforms at height in the field.

tasks.label: Conduct engineering site audits to collect structural, electrical, and related site information for use in the design of residential or commercial solar power systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full engineering site audit at a single-family home with a pitched composition-shingle roof: measure and photograph each roof plane, pitch and azimuth, note roof condition and obstructions (vents, chimneys), run a shade analysis, go into the attic to record rafter/truss size, spacing and span, open the main service panel to record busbar and main-breaker ratings, meter and service-entrance location, and identify inverter/conduit routing.

Preliminary/feasibility exterior capture at a residence where only roof geometry, orientation, obstructions, roof condition and shading are needed to true up a remote design; no interior or electrical access is part of this visit.

Full audit of a small commercial building (retail, office, small warehouse) with a low-slope membrane roof: roof dimensions, penetrations, parapets, HVAC and setback constraints, membrane condition, plus verification of structural framing capacity from below or from drawings, and a walk of the electrical room to record the main distribution panel/switchgear ratings, available breaker space and conduit routing to the roof.

Commercial roof-only capture for array layout on an owner-controlled building: measure roof planes and obstruction heights and collect shade data for the layout, with structural and electrical inputs supplied separately from drawings or another trade.

Solar domestic hot water / space heating audit at a home or small building: inspect the mechanical room, existing water heater or boiler, available space for a storage tank, plumbing run lengths and penetration paths to the collector location, plus collector mounting area on the roof.

Audit of a site with an existing PV system for an expansion, repair or as-built verification: identify module and inverter nameplates, existing string and conduit routing, condition of roof penetrations and attic wiring, and remaining capacity at the point of interconnection.

instances.label: Walkthrough of an active construction site (building or civil project) to document installed conditions and deviations from the drawings — capturing dimensions, 360° imagery and scans of structure, slabs and overhead MEP so the drafter can revise/redline the construction documents. Site is congested, changing daily, with other trades, debris and partial enclosure.

Outdoor topographic/site-condition survey of an existing or in-progress site (grades, stockpiles, pads, drainage swales, roadway corridor features) to update civil site or grading drawings. Open, largely unobstructed terrain; data must tie to project coordinates at engineering accuracy.

Ground-level field investigation in a street or right-of-way requiring physical access: recovering property corners/monuments, opening manholes and measuring pipe inverts and sizes, measuring curb, drainage structures and obscured or vegetated features, occupying control points with a total station/GNSS rover; often supervising a two-person crew amid traffic.

As-built measurement of accessible interiors of an existing commercial, institutional or industrial building (plant, warehouse, office floor, school) for renovation/retrofit drawings: room geometry, ceiling heights, column grid, exposed piping/ductwork and equipment locations. Building owner controls access; layout fixed and lit.

Measure-up of a private home or small occupied building for renovation/addition drawings: room dimensions, window/door sizes, stairs, exterior elevations, plus attic/crawlspace framing checks. Furniture and occupants present; no institutional control of the space.

Technical investigation of concealed or inaccessible conditions during a field visit: lifting ceiling tiles, opening access panels and electrical panels, probing wall/floor assemblies, verifying framing in attics or crawlspaces, and questioning site personnel to resolve discrepancies before revising details.

instances.label: Visit to an existing occupied commercial or institutional building (office suite, school, clinic) where new electrical work is proposed: walk accessible rooms, corridors and the electrical room, note existing panel/feeder/fixture locations, take rough dimensions, and produce a rough field sketch of the layout for later drafting.

Visit to an active construction site or gut-renovation project: unfinished floors with studs open, debris, temporary lighting, ladders and changing layout; walk the areas of proposed rough-in, note where conduit, boxes, gear pads and service entrance will go, and sketch the location plan.

Visit to an industrial or manufacturing plant for equipment power/controls work: walk the plant floor among machines, motor control centers and cable tray, note equipment positions and clearances, elevated mezzanines and noisy/PPE conditions, and sketch equipment locations and routing.

Access-restricted or concealed-condition survey: locked electrical closets, above-ceiling plenums, crawl spaces, roofs and switchgear rooms; requires opening enclosure/panel doors, lifting ceiling tiles, reading nameplates and breaker schedules in tight quarters, and sketching what is behind or above finished surfaces.

Outdoor institution-controlled site: substation yard, campus service entrance, solar array field, parking-lot lighting or plant yard; pace off distances between transformer pads, poles and building service, note obstructions, and sketch a rough site plan.

Visit to private residential or small-business premises (house, small retail shop) for a service upgrade or small installation: cluttered rooms, basements and attics, occupants and pets present, sketch service panel location, meter and routing.

tasks.label: Test aircraft systems under simulated operational conditions, performing systems readiness tests and pre- and post-operational checkouts, to establish design or fabrication parameters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench/ATE functional test of an avionics or electrical line-replaceable unit or cockpit control panel in an equipment lab: technician mounts the unit in the test fixture, mates the interface harness, runs the automated test program that applies simulated operational stimuli (power, bus traffic, signals), actuates front-panel switches and verifies lamps/displays/outputs, records pass-fail data, then powers down and safes the setup.

Systems integration lab / iron bird / hardware-in-the-loop rig test of an aircraft subsystem (flight controls, hydraulics, landing gear steering, ECS): the article is installed on the rig with real actuators and simulated loads, the technician configures the run, drives simulated flight or ground profiles including degraded and fault cases, monitors alarms and limits, and records/reviews channel data.

On-aircraft ground checkout of a development or flight-test aircraft in a hangar or on the ramp: connect ground power and test carts, power up systems, run built-in test and functional checks of control surfaces and subsystems, install/verify flight-test instrumentation and telemetry with the control room, then post-flight download data, inspect instrumentation and safe the aircraft.

Environmental or structural qualification test of a component or structure (vibration, thermal/altitude chamber, pressure, fatigue load spectrum): article fixtured and instrumented with thermocouples/strain gauges/accelerometers, simulated operational profile applied, run monitored for exceedances, data recorded, article inspected and removed afterward.

Space-vehicle or propulsion ground systems readiness test (static fire, wet dress rehearsal, stage checkout) at a test stand or launch complex: ground support equipment and umbilicals hooked up, console procedures and countdown run with automated sequencing and abort monitoring, propellants loaded, telemetry verified, post-test safing and data review.

tasks.label: Identify required data, data acquisition plans, and test parameters, setting up equipment to conform to these specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Structures/loads lab: instrument a one-off test article (wing box, fuselage panel, fitting) for a static or fatigue test — pick gauge types and locations from the engineer's data requirements, surface-prep and bond dozens to hundreds of strain gauges, install LVDTs, load cells and DIC targets, solder and route labelled harnesses to DAQ racks, build the channel list, shunt-calibrate and verify every channel.

Production/acceptance functional test of an avionics LRU or electromechanical component: determine from the part/serial number which test procedure, stimuli and measurement parameters apply, load the unit into the automated test set, mate the interface connectors, initiate the multi-hour functional test that exercises every interface, and archive the accepted data package.

Vibration/modal survey setup in an environmental or structural dynamics lab: article on a fixture or soft suspension with exciter installed; define measurement DOFs from the FE mesh, set excitation type, frequency range and resolution, position response measurement over the whole surface, acquire the FRF data set and verify coherence/quality before releasing data.

Flight-test instrumentation installation on a vehicle in a hangar or integration high bay: mount transducers, thermocouples, cameras and antennas at engineer-specified stations, fabricate and route cable runs through confined airframe structure with clamps and grommets, terminate to the onboard DAQ/telemetry unit, program sample rates and calibrations, and run end-to-end signal checks.

Propulsion test cell or wind tunnel setup: install the engine/model on the stand or sting, plumb pressure lines and install thermocouples, flow meters and load cells per the test matrix, connect to the facility data system, set ranges and sampling rates, and perform pre-test calibration and leak/continuity checks.

Pre-mission ground station / control room setup for a launch or flight test: configure the telemetry, tracking and recording chain to the mission data requirements — patch signal routing between receivers, decoms, recorders and consoles, set receiver/decom/recorder parameters, and verify end-to-end data flow and display pages before the operation.

tasks.label: Inspect, diagnose, maintain, and operate test setups and equipment to detect malfunctions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine operation of an established bench/automated test station in an avionics or component test lab: install the unit in its fixture, mate the interface connectors, verify the instruments are ready and in calibration, run the automated test sequence, record results and flag units that fail. No fault in the test setup itself.

Troubleshooting a malfunctioning bench test setup: a data-acquisition channel reads zero or noisy during checkout; the technician inspects cabling and connectors, traces the signal path with a meter/scope, isolates a broken pin, failed card, loose ground or out-of-tolerance instrument, replaces or repairs it, and re-verifies the setup.

Structural/environmental test setup in a lab or high bay (shaker table, thermal-vacuum chamber, load frame): bond and route strain gauges, accelerometers and thermocouples on the article, check fixture and cabling, verify every channel, chase dead/noisy channels and chamber faults (pump, seal, feedthrough), then operate the test.

Propulsion component or hot-fire test stand: inspect plumbing, valves, regulators and pressure transducers, perform leak checks, replace seals/filters and faulty sensors, maintain purge and hydraulic systems, then operate the test from the control room and diagnose anomalies in the data.

Routine inspection/monitoring rounds of test facility and ground support equipment to detect malfunctions: walk the stand and facility, read gauges and indicator lights, listen to pumps/compressors, check for gas or fluid leaks and thermal hotspots, log readings and report anomalies for maintenance action.

Vehicle integration high bay or flight line: connect ground test sets, umbilicals and instrumentation to the air or space vehicle, power up, run built-in test and functional checks, and diagnose whether an indication is a real vehicle fault or a problem in the test set/cabling, correcting the latter.

instances.label: Pre-test instrumentation setup and in-situ calibration at a test stand, wind tunnel or engine test cell: connect pressure scanners, thermocouples, strain gauges and load cells to signal conditioning, apply reference pressures/shunt cals, enter scale factors in the DAQ, and verify each channel end-to-end before the run.

Operating the data acquisition and control console during a test run, engine firing, or launch countdown: configure channels/sample rates and limits to the test requirements, arm and start acquisition, monitor real-time data and alarms, and record the run.

Post-test data reduction and analysis at a workstation: import raw files, apply calibration coefficients and filters, generate engineering-unit plots and summary tables, flag out-of-spec channels, and deliver the data package/report to engineering.

Installing, adjusting and troubleshooting DAQ hardware on a flight-test aircraft, test article, or remote range/telemetry site: racking chassis and signal conditioning modules, routing and dressing cabling, swapping failed modules, and chasing noisy or dead channels with a meter/scope.

tasks.label: Adjust, repair, or replace faulty components of test setups and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In a structural/environmental/propulsion test lab, instrumentation on the test article or rig has gone bad mid-setup or mid-campaign: a dead strain gauge, drifting thermocouple, open accelerometer lead, chafed instrumentation cable or bad solder joint. The technician traces the fault, removes/re-bonds or replaces the sensor, re-solders and re-routes leads, re-terminates connectors, and re-verifies channel calibration on the DAQ before the test can continue. Every test article is bespoke; access is often cramped and around fragile hardware.

Heterogeneous fault in the data acquisition/console equipment in a control room or integration lab: intermittent signal traced to a bad interconnect cable, a loose backplane seat, a failed internal power supply or fan in a chassis, or a bad channel on a signal-conditioning unit. Requires disconnecting cabling, removing rack screws, sliding out and opening a chassis, swapping the internal part, re-cabling, and re-running a functional/loopback check.

Straightforward replacement of a standardized, front-panel-accessible, tool-less hot-swap module in an instrumentation rack (redundant power supply module, plug-in signal-conditioning or PXI/VXI-style card with thumb latches, no cabling to disturb): identify the failed slot from the indicator/diagnostic, pull the module, insert the spare, confirm it comes up.

Mechanical, fluid or fixture components of the test setup fail: a leaking tube fitting or seal on a pressurant line, a stuck solenoid valve, a faulty load cell or hydraulic actuator on a load frame, loose or galled fixture bolts, or a misaligned specimen requiring shimming and re-alignment. Work is done in a test cell or on a stand, with torque specs, leak/proof checks and re-alignment verification.

Shop-bench, component-level repair of a faulty circuit board pulled from test or measurement equipment: a failed op-amp, regulator, relay or connector on the board is desoldered and a replacement soldered in, then the board is functionally checked.

Repairs to test/telemetry/tracking equipment away from the lab: on an aircraft flight line or in a hangar, at a launch pad or a remote range/telemetry site. Faulty antenna cabling, transducer, junction box or power feed is adjusted or replaced outdoors under weather and schedule pressure, often at height or in awkward access, with hand tools carried to the site.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In an aerospace lab fab/machine shop, fabricate one-off mechanical hardware for a test setup (mounting brackets, adapter plates, load fittings, spacers, test coupons) from bar/plate stock per a sketch or engineering drawing: saw, mill/drill, tap, deburr, check dimensions.

Mount and secure a component or test article into bench test equipment (load frame, vibration shaker, thermal/vacuum chamber, pressure fixture): align to the fixture, install and torque bolts/screws with hand and power tools, verify fit and clearances before the test run.

Instrument the test article: surface-prep and adhesive-bond foil strain gauges, attach thermocouples, accelerometers and pressure taps, route/lace and strain-relieve lead wires, solder or crimp terminations, and verify each channel with a multimeter/DAQ before test.

Fabricate and connect test-support cabling and plumbing: cut/strip/terminate instrumentation cables and harnesses, build tube/hose runs with fittings, land connectors at the data-acquisition and control racks, then run continuity and leak checks.

Install test hardware onto a large article in a high bay, engine test cell, structural test rig or hangar (mount sensor packages, ducting, load-introduction fittings, brackets on an airframe or engine): work from lifts or in confined access with hand and power tools around ground-support equipment.

tasks.label: Finish vehicle instrumentation and deinstrumentation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Flight-test instrumentation install on an airframe in a hangar or on the flight line: abrade and solvent-clean the surface at drawing-specified locations, bond strain gauges and thermocouples (or spot-weld/mechanically fasten them) to wing, fuselage and control-surface structure, solder lead wires, route and clamp the leads, using scissor/boom lifts and working overhead and in awkward positions.

Installing the instrumentation system inside the vehicle: mounting data acquisition units, racks, transducers and cameras to brackets in cabins, wheel wells and equipment bays; routing, clamping and tying large test wire bundles through confined structure; mating and torquing hundreds of circular connectors; performing continuity/end-to-end functional checkout and signing off the paperwork.

Instrumenting a ground test article in a structures/component test lab: a fixtured specimen or component on a load frame or test rig receives dozens to hundreds of strain gauges, thermocouples, LVDTs and pressure taps, each wired back to the data system, labeled, and verified before the test series.

Deinstrumentation after test or flight: removing bonded gauges, thermocouples and accelerometers, cutting out and pulling test wire runs, removing clamps, brackets and mounting blocks, cleaning adhesive and tape residue without damaging paint or composite skin, restoring the vehicle to delivery configuration, and inspecting/documenting the affected areas.

Propulsion or launch-vehicle instrumentation at an engine test stand or integration facility: installing pressure transducers with tubing and fittings, high-temperature thermocouples and accelerometers on engines, stages and ground support hardware, routing harnesses to junction boxes, then leak-, continuity- and calibration-checking the installation (and removing it after the test campaign).

It shows the state of the art on comparable objects (flexible cables, circular/rectangular connectors) but only at ~77% success in a lab cell, so it does not substantiate completion of a whole instrumentation job at worker quality.

instances.label: Structural/fatigue test lab: build or modify a test rig for an aircraft component (wing rib, landing gear fitting, fuselage panel) per engineering drawings — erect or reconfigure the reaction frame, bolt in load-introduction fittings and whiffletrees, mount hydraulic actuators and load cells, shim and align to tolerance, then prove the rig out with a low-load shakedown.

Fabrication shop attached to the test facility: make the hardware for a rig from drawings — cut and fit structural members, weld up stands/brackets/adapter plates, and machine mounting plates and bushings, then deburr and inspect to print.

Instrumentation build-up: prepare surfaces and bond strain gauges, spot-weld or tape thermocouples, install pressure taps and transducers, route and tie down lead wires and harnesses on the test article and rig, terminate connectors into the DAQ patch panel, and verify each channel (resistance, shunt cal, continuity).

Engine/propulsion or environmental test cell: set up the cell for an incoming test article — mount the unit on the thrust stand or in the chamber, connect fuel, air, oil, hydraulic and instrumentation lines, install shrouds/ducting, torque and leak-check fittings, and verify the configuration against the test spec.

Facility upkeep: scheduled and corrective maintenance of test-facility equipment — service hydraulic power units and actuators (seals, filters, fluid), fix leaks, replace worn valves and fittings, service vacuum pumps, chamber compressors and wind-tunnel drive components, recalibrate load cells and transducers, and troubleshoot faults reported during a test campaign.

Systems-integration / avionics bench: build or modify a test bench — mount DAQ chassis, power supplies and signal conditioners in racks, wire the control/interface panel per schematic, build and dress interconnect cables with circular and D-sub connectors, label per drawing, and check out the bench end to end.

Acceptance/condition CCTV inspection of newly installed or rehabilitated sewer and storm mains between manholes in a public street: run camera through each segment, identify and code defects (offset joints, infiltration, sags, debris, lateral intrusions) and report which segments pass or require contractor correction.
