tasks.label: Inspect installation sites.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-installation site survey in an operating manufacturing plant for a new robot cell: technician walks the proposed footprint, measures floor area and overhead/side clearances against the layout drawing, checks slab condition/levelness and anchoring feasibility, verifies the electrical drop (voltage/amperage, disconnect), compressed air, and network drops, notes obstructions, forklift traffic and room for fencing/light curtains, and issues a site-readiness checklist and punch list.

Warehouse or distribution-center site inspection ahead of an AMR fleet, AS/RS or palletizer install: aisle widths and turning clearances, floor joints, drains and ramp slopes, dock-door and staging areas, rack alignment, charging/dock locations, Wi-Fi coverage walk test, and reporting deficiencies to the deployment team.

Verification walkthroughs during and after an installation inside a controlled facility: confirm equipment, conduit, anchors, guarding and utility stub-ups are placed per the approved drawings, capture as-built documentation, and flag deviations/conflicts for correction (repeated over the course of the install).

Site inspection at a non-industrial but institution-controlled customer site (hospital lab/pharmacy, retail store, hotel, restaurant, university) for a service or collaborative robot install: floor plan and thresholds, elevator and door interfaces, outlet locations and circuit capacity, lighting, floor surface and network coverage.

Field or greenfield inspection: an active construction site for a new plant, an outdoor/agricultural installation, or a utility yard — unfinished, cluttered and changing conditions, weather exposure; verify foundation pads, anchor-bolt patterns and conduit stub-ups against drawings and coordinate with other trades before equipment arrives.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot (Autowalk / Orbit)
sources.title: Automated Inspections Made Simple | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot's autonomous inspection missions in industrial facilities are created by a human manually driving the robot along the route once and recording actions; the robot then repeats that taught route autonomously. This means a first-visit survey of a novel site is not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: recurring equipment-condition inspection rounds in plants. It shows the state of the art for mobile inspection autonomy — repeat of a human-taught route — which is the capability a technician's one-off site survey would have to draw on.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine asset-condition inspection rounds in industrial facilities. It substantiates autonomous mobility and sensing in E2 plant settings, but the routes and inspection points are pre-defined and the output is asset condition, not a site-readiness determination for a new installation.

sources.system: Leica BLK ARC on Boston Dynamics Spot
sources.title: Leica BLK ARC now the first certified reality capture device available for Boston Dynamics’ Spot | Geo Week News
sources.claim: The BLK ARC reality-capture payload is certified for Spot, enabling autonomous robotic laser scanning that documents site conditions in plants, warehouses ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: capturing as-built site conditions in industrial facilities. It substantiates autonomous geometric documentation of a site, but not verification of utilities, floor load, or a readiness judgment.

sources.system: Skydio 3D Scan (Skydio 2/2+/X2/X10)

sources.claim: Skydio drones with 3D Scan autonomously plan and execute image capture of a structure inside an operator-defined scan volume without any prior map, including GPS-denied and indoor settings, producing 3D models for inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous first-visit geometric documentation of an unfamiliar structure. It covers the data-capture portion of a site survey, but the operator must define the scan volume and the output is imagery/3D models, not a site-readiness assessment.

sources.system: Ground robots / quadrupeds with LiDAR (industry survey)
sources.title: How autonomous construction scanning creates a repeatable site record | DroneDeploy
sources.claim: Ground robots and quadrupeds scanning active construction sites operate by following predefined routes to produce repeatable data for BIM comparison, rather than exploring and assessing a site on their own.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic site scanning. Establishes the limitation that deployed site-scanning robots repeat human-defined routes and deliver spatial data, not an independent site evaluation.

tasks.label: Maintain inventories of robotic production supplies, such as sensors or cables.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Periodic cycle count / physical inventory audit in the plant or integrator's parts crib: counting boxed sensors, drives and grippers on shelves plus loose small parts (connectors, ferrules, M12 cordsets, fasteners) in bins and drawers, and reconciling counts against the ERP/CMMS record.

Receiving inbound shipments of robotic supplies: unpacking vendor cartons at the receiving bench, verifying part numbers, revisions and quantities against the packing slip/PO, labeling items, and putting them away in the correct labeled bin or shelf location in the stockroom.

Picking and issuing supplies from the crib for a job or breakdown: retrieving specific cables, sensors, fuses or spare end-effector parts from bins/shelves, kitting them for the technician, and logging the withdrawal against a work order.

Replenishing point-of-use stock on the production floor: walking the robot cells, checking cell-side spares cabinets and kanban bins (weld tips, cable ties, proximity sensors, hoses, filters), topping them off from the crib and returning empties.

Monitoring stock levels against min/max: surveying shelves and kanban bins for shortages or discrepancies, flagging low or missing stock, and generating/expediting replenishment orders with purchasing or the vendor.

Stockroom housekeeping: reorganizing and relabeling bins and shelves after a layout change, coiling and racking cable reels, segregating damaged or returned parts, and purging obsolete stock for a discontinued robot model.

tasks.label: Prepare and package environmental samples for shipping or testing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field site (monitoring well, stream, stormwater outfall, remediation site): after collecting grab samples, the technician preserves them at the truck tailgate — adds acid to metals bottles and checks pH, fills 40 mL VOA vials headspace-free, caps and hand-labels several bottle types, wraps glass, packs a cooler with ice and bubble wrap, completes the chain-of-custody form, applies custody seals and readies the cooler for overnight courier. Weather, uneven ground, no fixed layout.

Analytical or consulting laboratory bench: preparing received environmental samples for testing — aliquoting water into vials, filtering, adding preservatives/reagents, running solid-phase extraction or digestion, homogenizing and sieving soil, weighing subsamples into tubes, then capping, labeling and racking them for instrument analysis.

Sample staging/receiving room at a consulting office or lab: assembling pre-cleaned bottle kits and coolers for upcoming field events; unpacking, verifying and logging returned coolers, relabeling and repacking bottles into insulated shipping containers with ice and packing material, taping, labeling and staging boxes for a subcontract lab courier.

Wastewater/drinking-water treatment plant or industrial facility sampling shed and lab: splitting composite and discrete samples from automatic samplers into permit-compliance containers, adding preservatives, labeling, refrigerating, and packing a routine daily/weekly shipment to the certified lab. Standard containers, fixed layout, institution-controlled premises.

Hazardous or specialty media: packaging waste-characterization and drum samples, air sampling media (sorbent tubes, filter cassettes, Summa canisters) — capping and sealing media, absorbent and cushioning per DOT/IATA hazmat rules, hazard-class labels, custody seals and shipping papers, often at a site trailer or staging pad.

sources.claim: The CVP Impack fit-to-size auto-boxing machine autonomously builds, fills, tapes, weighs and labels shipping boxes around the goods presented to it on a conveyor, running in commercial fulfillment operations in place of manual packers.

tasks.label: Assist in the cleanup of hazardous material spills.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Indoor spill inside a client or employer facility (plant floor, laboratory, warehouse aisle, water/wastewater treatment building): technician dons PPE, isolates the area, screens the atmosphere with a PID/4-gas meter, dikes the liquid with sorbent socks, applies absorbent or neutralizer, scoops the spent media into drums/overpacks, labels and stages the waste, decontaminates tools and surfaces, and documents the event.

Outdoor spill on facility grounds (tank farm, loading dock, fuel island, transformer pad, secondary containment): technician blocks storm drains, deploys sorbent booms and pads, spreads granular absorbent, hand-shovels stained gravel/soil into drums, assists a vac truck with recovery of free liquid, collects confirmation samples, and completes the spill report.

Transportation or public-area incident (overturned tote/drum, tanker leak on a roadway shoulder, spill into a ditch): technician works alongside fire/hazmat responders and a cleanup contractor in an uncontrolled setting with traffic, weather and unknown product, helping contain runoff, overpack leaking containers, place sorbents and stage recovered waste.

Bulk excavation and loading of spill-impacted soil at an open release/remediation site: with excavation limits staked or marked by the project engineer, impacted soil layers are stripped with an excavator and loaded into haul trucks or roll-off bins for offsite disposal, working around stockpiles and haul routes on unimproved ground.

Hand work at the release/remediation site around the machine work: hand-digging and hand-picking impacted material near utilities and structures, filling and sealing drums, field-screening soil headspace, collecting confirmation samples from sidewalls and floor, placing liner/backfill and decontaminating equipment before it leaves the site.

Spill reaching water (harbor, river, retention pond): technician assists an OSRO crew deploying containment and sorbent boom from a small boat or bank, operating or tending a skimmer, transferring recovered oil-water to a tank, and cleaning oiled shoreline/riprap by hand.

sources.system: ALICE / IOSB.BoB autonomous excavator (ROBDEKON, Fraunhofer IOSB)
sources.title: ROBDEKON showcases state of development – Progress in decontamination tasks: Robots have learnt new capabilities
sources.claim: Fraunhofer IOSB's driverless 24-ton excavator (ALICE / IOSB.BoB), developed in the ROBDEKON decontamination competence center, autonomously removes contaminated soil layers and loads them onto the ... an autonomous tractor, and can move autonomously in unknown, ....

tasks.label: Perform environmental quality work in field or office settings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine surface-water/effluent monitoring run: technician drives to scheduled points (stream stations, stormwater outfalls, permitted discharge points, reservoirs/harbors), records in-situ readings (pH, DO, conductivity, temperature, turbidity), collects grab or composite samples into preserved bottles, labels them, completes chain-of-custody forms, ices the cooler and delivers to the lab.

Site-investigation and remediation sampling: opening monitoring-well vaults at a landfill, brownfield or UST/Superfund site, gauging depth-to-water, low-flow purging with pump and tubing until parameters stabilize, filling and preserving VOC/metals bottles, decontaminating equipment between locations, plus hand-auger/direct-push soil and waste-characterization sampling on uneven, debris-strewn ground.

Fugitive-emissions and air-quality field monitoring: quarterly landfill surface emission monitoring (Method 21 grid walkover with an FID over the cover), fugitive-leak/optical-gas-imaging surveys at permitted industrial facilities, and servicing ambient monitoring stations; results compiled into compliance-ready reports.

Operating and monitoring treatment/remediation equipment on rounds: walking a wastewater treatment plant or a groundwater pump-and-treat / SVE / air-stripper compound, reading gauges, flow meters and totalizers, checking pumps, blowers and vessels for leaks, overheating or abnormal noise, logging readings and flagging abnormalities to the engineer.

Bench laboratory work on environmental samples in the employer's lab: logging in samples, preparing and running routine analyses (pH, alkalinity, DO, turbidity, conductivity, colorimetric nutrients, solids), running QC standards and duplicates, and entering results into the LIMS.

Office desk work: reducing and QA-reviewing monitoring data, tabulating results against permit limits, drafting monitoring/permit reports and correspondence, scheduling sampling events and coordinating with the contract lab.

tasks.label: Receive, set up, test, or decontaminate equipment.

instances.label: Receiving a shipment at the firm's equipment room/warehouse: unloading boxed instruments, sample bottles/coolers, filters, PPE and consumables from a delivery truck at the dock, checking contents against the packing list, inspecting for shipping damage, logging serial numbers/calibration certificates into inventory, and shelving the items. Indoor company facility, fixed layout, controlled access.

Setting up sampling/monitoring equipment in the field at a remediation or investigation site: erecting a tripod or mast for an ambient air monitor, assembling a sampling train (filter cassette, tubing, pump), lowering a bladder/peristaltic pump and water-level transducer into a monitoring well, connecting batteries/solar and dataloggers, then flow-checking and leak-checking. Outdoor, site layout differs each time, weather and terrain as found.

Bench calibration and functional testing of portable instruments in the lab/equipment room before and after fieldwork: multi-gas meter and PID span/zero with calibration gas, pH/conductivity/turbidity meter calibration with buffers and standards, air-sampling pump flow calibration against a primary standard, battery/sensor checks, and recording calibration logs. Indoor, standard bench and fume hood, institution-controlled.

Decontaminating field equipment at the site: scrubbing and triple-rinsing bailers, split-spoon samplers, trowels, pumps and tubing with Alconox, tap water and deionized water at a temporary decon pad; steam- or pressure-washing drill augers, backhoe buckets and rig components before they leave the exclusion zone; containerizing rinsate. Outdoor, in PPE, contaminated media, ad hoc pad layout.

Setting up and testing remediation/treatment system equipment at a facility: placing and connecting pumps, blowers, air strippers, carbon vessels, flow meters and pressure transducers on a skid or in a treatment shed; wiring/plumbing connections, powering up, running the unit, verifying readings and flows, and correcting leaks. Multi-media EHS compliance walkthrough with checklist at a manufacturing or commercial facility: hazardous-waste accumulation area container labels/accumulation dates/lid and bulge condition, secondary containment integrity, spill kits, aisle space, SPCC tank and drum areas, photo documentation and a signed inspection log.

Routine in-house compliance/condition monitoring rounds inside the employer's own treatment or process plant: fixed route through the facility reading gauges and panel indications, thermal and acoustic checks for leaks and overheating, noting equipment abnormalities and housekeeping, logging permit-relevant readings.

tasks.label: Decontaminate or test field equipment used to clean or test pollutants from soil, air, or water.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: At a soil-investigation/remediation site, the technician decontaminates drilling and soil-sampling tools (hand augers, split-spoon samplers, drill rods, trowels, bowls) on a poly-lined decon pad: scrape off soil, Alconox/tap-water scrub or steam-clean, tap rinse, deionized-water final rinse, air dry and wrap in foil; containerize the decon water. Outdoors, mud, wind, uneven ground, other crews and a drill rig working nearby.

Between groundwater/surface-water sampling locations, the technician decons water-sampling gear — bladder or submersible pump and its tubing, bailers, water-level meter tape, flow-through cell and multiparameter sonde — in wash/rinse tubs on a tailgate or in the field vehicle, pumping detergent and DI water through the pump, wiping the sonde and cables, and staging the clean gear for the next well.

Back at the office equipment room / warehouse bay, the technician washes, rinses with DI water, dries, wraps and re-stages returned sampling gear (bailers, glass and plastic sampleware, filter housings, coliwasas, tubing reels, pump heads), inspects for damage, and logs the equipment back into inventory. Indoor, fixed layout, sink/washer, benches.

In the equipment room before a field day, the technician function-tests and calibrates portable air/vapor instruments: bump test and span-calibrate 4-gas meters and photoionization detectors with cal gas, zero and flow-check personal air sampling pumps against a flow calibrator, check batteries and alarms, and print/log the calibration records.

In the lab or field trailer, the technician calibrates and function-checks water-quality instruments: multiparameter sonde (pH buffers, conductivity and turbidity standards, DO check), field turbidimeter and colorimeters, cleaning sensor faces and membranes, verifying post-calibration drift and recording results in the calibration log.

At a hazardous-waste site decon station, the technician steam-cleans or pressure-washes heavy field/remediation equipment — excavator buckets and tracks, well-development pumps, hoses, drums, treatment-system components, truck wheels and undercarriage — collecting and containerizing the wash water before equipment leaves the exclusion zone.

tasks.label: Collect and analyze pollution samples, such as air or ground water.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Quarterly groundwater monitoring round at a remediation site or landfill perimeter: drive a route of 10-30 monitoring wells taken as found (locked vaults, grass/gravel, weather), unlock and open each well, gauge depth to water, set a bladder/peristaltic pump, low-flow purge while watching pH/DO/conductivity/turbidity stabilize in a flow-through cell, field-filter for dissolved metals, fill and preserve VOC vials and bottles, label, ice, and complete chain-of-custody forms.

Bench analysis of received samples in an environmental/water testing laboratory: cooler receipt and temperature check, sample log-in, preparation (filtration, digestion, extraction, dilution), running routine methods (BOD, COD, pH, conductivity, alkalinity, turbidity, TSS, nutrients; metals by ICP; VOCs by GC-MS), QA/QC checks (blanks, spikes, duplicates) and reporting results.

Sampling at a wastewater treatment plant or industrial facility: program, install and retrieve 24-hour flow-proportional composite samplers at influent/effluent points and manholes, take grab samples of process streams, sludge and outfall discharge from walkways and basins, record field parameters, and bottle/preserve samples for permit compliance.

On-site air/gas survey inside an industrial facility (refinery, gas plant, chemical works, digester area): walk or fly a route through the plant taking pollutant readings with portable analyzers or optical gas imaging, locate and quantify fugitive leaks, check fenceline concentrations, and log measurements for compliance.

Servicing fixed monitoring points: ambient air monitoring station or landfill gas wellfield — swap filters in PM samplers, deploy/retrieve summa canisters and sorbent tubes, run flow and span calibrations, and take periodic gas composition readings at wellheads and probes at a permanent, institution-maintained installation.

Grab sampling at accessible outdoor field sites: surface water from a reservoir, pond, stream or river (boat or bank), and shallow soil cores from open unpaved ground on a grid, bagged/bottled and georeferenced for laboratory analysis, in ordinary weather with variable terrain.

instances.label: Monitored natural attenuation (MNA) round at a groundwater contamination site (former gas station, dry cleaner, or industrial plume): drive to the site, open flush-mount well vaults across pavement and brush, deploy pump and tubing in 6-20 wells, low-flow purge while watching a flow-through cell for stabilization of DO, ORP, pH, conductivity, collect VOC vials and geochemical bottles (nitrate, sulfate, methane, ferrous iron field kits), preserve, decontaminate, complete chain-of-custody, then evaluate whether the geochemical footprint and concentration trends show biodegradation.

Bench-scale evaluation in the firm's or a contract environmental laboratory: build microcosm bottles or batch/column tests from site soil and groundwater, spike parent contaminants or emerging compounds, incubate for weeks, periodically withdraw headspace/aqueous aliquots, run GC/GC-MS/IC analyses, and compute first-order degradation or sorption rate constants used as a line of evidence for attenuation capacity.

Field survey of a receiving water body's natural purification/assimilative capacity: run transects on a stream, lake, lagoon, or wetland from a small boat or by wading; profile DO, temperature, pH, ORP, conductivity, turbidity; collect grab samples for BOD, nutrients, and emerging contaminants; deploy and retrieve continuous sondes; assess reaeration, nutrient uptake, and contaminant decay along the reach.

Open-ground soil and gas work at a landfill, brownfield, or biocover: quarterly surface-emissions monitoring on a grid over the landfill cover with a hydrocarbon analyzer, soil-gas probe readings for methane/CO2/oxygen profiles indicating cover oxidation, and soil cores for organic carbon, moisture, and microbial-activity indicators; results used to judge how much contaminant the cover soil naturally degrades.

Vapor-intrusion attenuation assessment at occupied homes or commercial buildings over a dissolved plume: walk the building, inventory background sources, drill and seal sub-slab ports, collect sub-slab, indoor, and ambient air with Summa canisters or passive samplers over 8-24 hours, then compute attenuation factors between groundwater/soil gas and indoor air.

tasks.label: Improve chemical processes to reduce toxic emissions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Office/desk work at a plant or consulting firm: compile and analyze process and emissions data (CEMS records, stack test results, material balances, emission factors), screen alternative reagents/solvents or operating windows, model the expected reduction, and write up recommended process changes for the supervising engineer. Physical action limited to paperwork and keyboard.

Bench/lab-scale testing in an employer or contract laboratory: prepare reagents and real process samples, run a matrix of small-scale reactions, jar tests, treatability or scrubbing-liquor tests across temperature/dose/pH/catalyst variables, run analytical instruments (GC, spectrophotometer, titration, ion chromatography), and interpret results to identify conditions that cut toxic byproducts or VOC/HAP formation.

Pilot-scale or slipstream trial in a pilot hall or on a plant skid: set up and operate a pilot scrubber, thermal oxidizer, biofilter, or pilot treatment train; change reagent chemistry, dosing, residence time and temperature over days; draw stack and liquid samples; tune the unit to minimize emissions and log performance.

Full-scale trial and implementation at an operating industrial facility (refinery, chemical plant, foundry, coating line): walk the unit with operators, change reagent dosing, burner or scrubber setpoints, swap media/catalyst or nozzles, take field measurements with portable analyzers and at stack sample ports, verify the emission reduction, and document it for permit compliance.

Municipal water/wastewater or POTW chemical optimization: run jar tests and bench trials on coagulant, oxidant, or odor-control chemistry, then change dosing pumps and injection points in the field, sample for disinfection byproducts, H2S/odor and off-gas, and confirm the reduction while keeping the plant in compliance.

sources.system: Mobile robotic chemist (Cooper group, University of Liverpool)

sources.claim: A mobile robot working in a conventional chemistry laboratory autonomously ran a closed-loop, eight-day experimental campaign (688 experiments over ten variables) to find improved photocatalyst formulations, handling solids/liquids and analytical instruments and choosing its own next experiments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: closed-loop optimization of a chemical formulation in a human chemistry lab. It transfers to bench-scale testing of process modifications to reduce toxic byproducts because the objects (vials, reagent dispensing, sonication, instrument-based analysis), the precision required, and the lab setting are the same; only the objective function (minimize byproduct/emission rather than maximize hydrogen yield) differs.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous self-optimization of chemical process conditions (residence time, stoichiometry, catalyst loading, light intensity) on a purpose-built rig. This is the same activity as tuning a chemical process to suppress unwanted byproducts; the reactor rig plays the role of the pilot/bench apparatus and the closed loop replaces the technician's parameter sweep.

sources.transferJustification: Same platform as evidence 1; cited to show the optimization objective can include waste minimization, which is the analogue of reducing toxic emissions from a chemical process.

tasks.label: Maintain process parameters and evaluate process anomalies.

instances.label: Municipal wastewater treatment plant, routine shift control of the biological process: tracking DO, ammonia, nitrate, MLSS, flow and chemical feed on instruments/SCADA, adjusting blower/aeration and chemical dose setpoints, RAS/WAS rates and valves to hold effluent within permit, and acting on routine deviation alarms. Indoor control room plus outdoor tanks and catwalks on a utility-controlled site.

Wastewater or industrial treatment plant, investigating an unexplained process upset (effluent ammonia or TSS excursion, filamentous foaming, sludge bulking, clarifier carryover): walking the process, visual and microscopic examination, grab sampling, checking pumps/diffusers/screens for physical causes, then implementing and verifying corrective actions.

Drinking water treatment plant, holding coagulation/filtration/disinfection parameters against changing raw water: checking turbidity, pH, streaming current, filter headloss and chlorine residual, adjusting coagulant/polymer/chlorine feed rates, and correcting drifting parameters before finished-water limits are breached.

Manufacturing/industrial facility air pollution control: maintaining scrubber, thermal oxidizer or baghouse parameters (temperature, pressure drop, reagent feed, pH) and CEMS analyzer health — verifying daily calibration checks, tracking drift, and following up opacity or CO/NOx excursions during plant walk-downs.

Field groundwater remediation system (pump-and-treat, soil vapor extraction, air sparge) at a remote site or unmanned compound: checking flows, vacuums, pressures, water levels and treatment vessel condition, adjusting wellhead and manifold valves and blower/pump settings, and diagnosing shutdowns (fouling, high level, freeze) to restore operation. Layout differs site to site, outdoors, weather exposed.

Landfill gas collection wellfield tuning: measuring methane, oxygen, carbon dioxide, vacuum and temperature at each wellhead, throttling the wellhead valve to optimize methane capture and avoid air intrusion, and flagging anomalies such as liquid-filled or overpulled wells. Uneven, changing landfill terrain.

instances.label: Working the production floor of a manufacturing plant to run time-and-motion studies, layout walk-throughs and process observations while conforming to site EHS rules: required PPE (safety glasses, hearing protection, steel toes, hi-vis), staying in marked walkways, keeping clear of forklifts, cranes and moving equipment, and not entering restricted zones.

Accessing production equipment to mount instrumentation, take measurements, or trial a process/layout change: applying lockout/tagout (isolate energy, apply personal lock and tag, verify zero energy), respecting machine guarding and permit requirements before and after the work.

Health/environmental compliance around materials during process trials and studies: handling chemicals per SDS, segregating and containerizing process waste into the right stream, sealing/labeling containers, staging them in an accumulation area, and following spill-prevention/response procedures.

Working inside a regulated controlled area (semiconductor cleanroom, pharma GMP suite, or food-plant hygiene zone): gowning correctly, following hygiene/contamination-control and material-entry protocols while observing or measuring the process.

Participating in or conducting routine safety/EHS walkthroughs and hazard checks in the facility: verifying guards in place, egress and walkways clear, spills and slip/trip hazards absent, fire extinguishers and safety signage present, and flagging or correcting deviations found.

tasks.label: Oversee or inspect production processes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine floor round in an operating manufacturing plant (food, metals, plastics, aerospace composites): walk the production line, verify machines are running to set parameters, read gauges/HMIs, check for hot bearings, air/steam leaks, abnormal noise, spills and housekeeping deviations, log readings and flag anomalies for follow-up.

In-process quality check of sampled output: pull parts off the line at set intervals, measure critical dimensions/features with gauges, calipers, or a CMM/optical scanner, compare to print tolerances, record data into SPC charts and judge whether the process is drifting out of control.

Time-and-motion / cycle-time observation of manual workstations: stand at the station, time work elements with stopwatch or video, note method deviations and idle/waiting, rate operator pace, and derive a standard rate or improvement recommendation.

Oversight of a production trial, changeover, or new line startup: watch the first-article run, verify setup and tooling, coordinate with operators and maintenance, diagnose deviations (scrap, jams, feed problems), adjust process parameters and confirm the corrected run is acceptable.

Oversight of an automated production cell or fenced line (robotic weld, stamping, packaging): confirm the station is producing to spec, monitor in-line measurement/vision results and cycle data, and flag dimensional drift or out-of-tolerance conditions for correction.

Process inspection at a non-factory or rough site taken as found: an outdoor fabrication yard, a customer installation or construction/erection site, or a temporary pilot operation, where layout differs site to site and conditions are not kept to a plant standard.

Mechanical setup and adjustment by hand on the floor: indicating in a fixture or vise on a machine table, squaring tooling with a protractor and height gauge, shimming, adjusting mechanical stops, gibs, conveyor guides or sensor brackets with wrenches and hex keys, then re-checking and locking down.

Off-site/field work: at a supplier's plant, a customer site, or an installed system elsewhere in the company, the technician assesses installed equipment as found, takes measurements with portable gauges and indicators, and adjusts the machine in place amid non-standard layout, clutter and access constraints.

tasks.label: Produce images or measurements, using tools or techniques such as atomic force microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, optical microscopy, particle size analysis, or zeta potential analysis.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine, standardized SEM work in a characterization lab: a batch of repeat-format specimens (particulates on filters, polished/epoxy mounts, nominally identical QC parts) is imaged and quantified - BSE/SE images plus feature size, count and composition statistics reported to a set template.

Exploratory imaging of varied R&D specimens on the SEM (and ad-hoc optical inspection of loose coupons): novel nanomaterial morphologies, cross-sections, fragile or charge-prone samples mounted bespoke on stubs; the technician chooses region of interest, magnification, detector and beam conditions to answer a specific engineering question.

AFM session on a small lab coupon: place the coupon on the chuck, mount/exchange a probe, align the laser and detector, tune and engage, scan several areas in non-contact/tapping mode, and produce topography images with roughness, step-height or particle-height numbers.

Optical microscopy imaging and dimensional measurement of samples on standard carriers (patterned wafers from a cassette, mounted slides, standard fixtures) in a lab or cleanroom: load, autofocus, capture calibrated images, measure critical features, log results.

Particle size (DLS/laser diffraction) and zeta potential runs on prepared nanoparticle dispersions: fill and load cuvettes/capillary cells into the analyzer, run the size and zeta protocols, check quality criteria, and report size distribution, PDI and zeta values.

Inline/production metrology in a semiconductor fab or pilot production line: cassette/FOUP-loaded wafers measured per recipe on CD-SEM, automated AFM or automated inspection tools, dozens of wafers per shift, with data pushed to SPC charts.

tasks.label: Calibrate nanotechnology equipment, such as weighing, testing, or production equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Weighing equipment: verify and adjust analytical balances/microbalances used for nanomaterial and precursor weighing. Technician levels the unit, runs internal adjustment, places OIML class E2/F1 reference weights on the pan inside the draft shield, checks repeatability, linearity and eccentricity, adjusts, and signs the calibration log. Setting: lab weigh room or gowning-controlled cleanroom bay.

Nanoscale metrology instruments: calibrate AFM scanner XY/Z against certified pitch and step-height standards, mount and qualify a probe, align the laser and tune the cantilever; calibrate SEM/CD-SEM magnification on a pitch standard and align the column. Performed at the instrument in a lab or fab metrology bay.

Production/process equipment in a cleanroom: run monitor wafers to establish deposition or etch rate, measure thickness/CD on ellipsometer, reflectometer, profilometer or CD-SEM, and update tool recipe times/setpoints; re-baseline lithography focus/dose/overlay. Output is a documented tool qualification.

Analytical/test instrumentation: calibrate spectrometers, ICP-MS and similar analyzers, or particle counters by running certified reference standards and blanks, generating a multipoint calibration curve, verifying against a check standard, adjusting instrument response and recording results. Standards sit in vials/racks at the instrument.

Ancillary and in-place instrumentation and hand tools: mass flow controllers in a tool gas box, furnace thermocouple profiling, vacuum/pressure gauges, RH and temperature sensors, hand pipettes, torque tools, and electrical test gear. Requires breaking and remaking fittings, in-situ probing, cabling a portable calibrator or DMM/SMU to a reference source, trimming the device, then paperwork.

tasks.label: Maintain work area according to cleanroom or other processing standards.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Post-process wipe-down and tidying of the immediate work area in a gowned cleanroom bay (and adjacent open lab bench): wiping benchtops, tool front panels and load stations, spin-coater bowls/tops, laminar-flow hood interiors and microscope stage areas with IPA/DI-wetted cleanroom wipes in overlapping unidirectional strokes; moving wafers, carriers, tweezers and fixtures aside and returning them to their places; done between runs with other gowned staff and delicate tooling present.

Scheduled floor cleaning inside the controlled area: damp-mopping/scrubbing cleanroom aisles, corridors and the gowning anteroom, and ULPA/HEPA vacuuming of floors along defined routes to the facility's particulate standard.

Hauling carts between locations: taking full waste/soiled-garment carts and empty chemical-bottle carts out of the controlled area to the accumulation point or dock, and bringing supply carts of wipes, gowns, gloves and wafer boxes back to the cleanroom entry.

Emptying and re-lining individual bins in the bays, segregating trash into the correct waste streams (general, contaminated wipes, sharps, solvent-wetted material), and stocking loose consumables (wipe packs, glove boxes, gown packs, carriers) onto shelves and dispensers in the bay and gowning room.

Upkeep of the wet-processing/chemical area: wiping chemical residues and small spills from wet-bench decks and fume-hood interiors, rinsing and drying labware, quartz carriers and beakers, checking and changing bath chemistry, and moving spent chemical containers to satellite accumulation, all in a fume-extracted human-tended chemical hood.

Walkthrough verification that the area meets standard: taking non-viable particle counts (and, in bio-nano labs, air samples) at designated sample points, checking temperature/RH/differential pressure and tacky-mat/gowning compliance, and recording results in the log or monitoring system, flagging out-of-spec readings.

tasks.label: Repair nanotechnology processing or testing equipment or submit work orders for equipment repair.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled preventive maintenance / consumable and wear-part replacement on a production process tool (plasma etcher, PECVD, sputter or ALD system) in a fab or university nanofab cleanroom: vent and open the chamber, wet-clean or scrub deposits, swap edge rings, liners, O-rings, shields or targets, torque vacuum-seal bolts to spec, pump down, leak-check and run qualification wafers.

Unplanned fault on a processing tool during a run: the tool alarms or misprocesses (vacuum leak, RF match fault, failed mass-flow controller, sticking pneumatic valve, blown fuse, interlock or chiller fault). Technician troubleshoots with gauges, meters and service manuals in the cleanroom or sub-fab, replaces the failed component or fitting, and verifies recovery.

Repair and re-adjustment of characterization/metrology instruments in an instrument lab: replace an SEM filament or aperture and realign the column, swap an AFM head/cantilever and realign the laser, clear a stuck stage, repair a probe station or profilometer, then recalibrate and verify resolution.

Rounds-based detection of a degrading support/utility asset (sub-fab dry pump, chiller, compressor, abatement unit, exhaust fan): notice the out-of-range gauge, hot bearing, leak or noise during a walkthrough and submit a facilities work order for repair.

Escalation path on a process or testing tool beyond in-house repair: reproduce the fault, pull error codes and logs, photograph the condition, tag the tool down, write and submit a work order/service request to the vendor or equipment engineering with symptoms and parts needed, then coordinate and verify the service visit.

Repair of benchtop and support equipment in the lab: spin coater lid/motor, hot plate or oven controller, wire bonder, glovebox, gas cabinet fitting, DI-water or vacuum line leak, loose wiring or connectors — heterogeneous, often improvised fixes with hand tools on equipment of many vintages.

tasks.label: Assist nanoscientists or engineers in processing or characterizing materials according to physical or chemical properties.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench/fume-hood wet processing of nanomaterials for a PI's project in a university, national-lab or corporate R&D laboratory: weighing precursor powders, dispensing solvents and reagents, stirring/heating, sonicating dispersions, centrifuging and washing, drying, and logging conditions. Standard glassware, vials, balances, hotplates, centrifuges; several parallel batches per day.

Running bulk/solution property characterization requested by a scientist: preparing and loading samples for XRD, DLS/zeta, UV-vis/FTIR/Raman, thermal analysis or chromatography, running the instrument recipe, checking data quality and returning reduced data. Shared instrument room in an institution-controlled facility.

Cleanroom thin-film/device processing steps in support of engineers: substrate/wafer cleaning, spin-coating resist or solution films, lithographic exposure and development, etch or deposition runs, annealing, plus in-line metrology (thickness, sheet resistance). Gowned cleanroom with standard tools and recipes.

Electron/probe microscopy characterization: mounting specimens (powder on SEM stub, dispersion on TEM grid, coupon in holder), FIB cross-section or lamella preparation, loading and aligning the instrument, acquiring images/EDS/AFM maps at nanoscale, and delivering the image set to the requesting scientist.

Non-routine assistance: setting up a one-off apparatus or fixture for a new experiment, handling an unusual or air-sensitive sample in a glovebox, adapting a protocol on the fly at a scientist's verbal request, troubleshooting a misbehaving instrument or a failed run, and reconfiguring equipment between projects.

Shared R&D nanofabrication cleanroom (university/institute user facility): technician sets up and runs a varied set of human-facing tools - spin coater, mask aligner, e-beam evaporator, RIE, wet bench HF/piranha etch - on one-off samples, following facility SOPs, chemical hygiene and PPE rules.

Bench-scale nanomaterial compounding/synthesis in a lab: weigh nanopowders/precursors, prepare and dose solutions, run heated stirred reaction, centrifuge-wash and sonicate to redisperse, pull QC samples, log to SOP, handle nanopowders and solvents under a hood per hazmat restrictions.

Bulk analytical testing of nanomaterial samples per SOP: DLS/zeta particle sizing, UV-vis, chromatography, thermal analysis - load sample into the instrument, verify calibration/standards, run the standard method, record and report results in a lab or QC facility.

Electron/probe microscopy and nanomanipulation: prepare and mount specimens (stubs, TEM grids, FIB lamellae), load into SEM/TEM/AFM/FIB, align, image and measure nanoscale features or manipulate nanoscale objects with probes, document per SOP.

Pilot- or GMP-scale production batch: charge raw materials, operate mill/high-shear mixer/microfluidic nanoparticle formulation and filling equipment, take in-process samples, monitor parameters, clean and changeover, complete batch records under GMP in a controlled production suite.

tasks.label: Monitor hazardous waste cleanup procedures to ensure proper application of nanocomposites or accomplishment of objectives.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: On-site oversight while a crew applies/injects a nanomaterial slurry (e.g., nZVI or nanocomposite amendment) at a contaminated site: check batch mixing ratios and slurry quality, watch injection pressures, flow rates and volumes against the work plan, watch for surfacing/daylighting and containment, log deviations and direct corrections. Open outdoor site with heavy equipment, mud, weather.

Post-application performance verification in the field: go well to well, purge monitoring wells with a low-flow pump, read stabilizing field parameters (pH, ORP, DO, conductivity, turbidity), fill and label sample bottles under chain-of-custody, compare trends against remedial objectives.

Screening/mapping the treated area to confirm objectives: walk a grid over treated soil or a covered waste area collecting samples or portable-instrument readings (pXRF, PID, soil-gas/vapor screening), georeference results, and map residual contamination against action levels.

Monitoring ex-situ treatment operations inside a permitted treatment building or pilot plant where a nanocomposite sorbent/reactive media train treats a waste stream: instrument rounds, gauge/flow/pressure and temperature reads, check reactor vessels, filter housings and sorbent bed condition, look and listen for leaks or off-gas, log deviations from the operating procedure.

Laboratory verification and QC: run or oversee analysis of collected samples and of the nanocomposite batch (particle size/concentration, iron or metal content, contaminant concentrations), compare against acceptance criteria and treatment objectives, and document results for the project record.

In-facility decontamination and hazardous-waste handling verification in the nanomaterial lab/production area: particulate and air monitoring rounds after a spill or cleanup, surface wipe/contamination survey, confirm the area meets release criteria, check waste containers, labels and satellite accumulation compliance.

instances.label: Bench-scale solid precursor weighing: technician weighs several powders/solids (mg-g) on an analytical balance in a nanomaterials research or QC lab (often in a fume hood), transfers them to vials/flasks per a written formula, and dissolves/suspends them in measured solvent to make stock solutions.

Precise liquid measurement and reagent mixing: pipetting/syringing microliter-to-milliliter volumes of precursors, ligands, surfactants and solvents to make dilution series and multi-component reaction mixes per protocol in a standard lab, with concentrations verified by calculation.

Preparing nanoparticle dispersions/suspensions: combining nanopowder or colloid with solvent and dispersant per formula, then sonicating/stirring and adjusting pH or concentration to spec before use or characterization, at a lab bench.

Cleanroom/fab process chemical preparation: making up etchants, developers, resist dilutions or CMP slurry to a specified ratio/concentration from concentrates and DI water under contamination and safety controls, for use at wet benches or tools.

Pilot- or production-scale batch make-up: weighing kilogram-scale powders and drums/totes of liquids against a batch record and charging them into a mixer/reactor in a pilot plant or commercial-scale production area, in PPE, with in-process weight verification.

tasks.label: Inspect or measure thin films of carbon nanotubes, polymers, or inorganic coatings, using a variety of techniques or analytical tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-line/at-line film thickness and uniformity metrology on wafer or substrate lots in a semiconductor or MEMS cleanroom: run the recipe on an ellipsometer/reflectometer (or CD-SEM), map thickness/index across the substrate, compare to spec, upload results to SPC, flag out-of-spec lots. Samples arrive in standard cassettes/FOUPs.

Surface metrology of deposited films with AFM or profilometry in a fab metrology bay or industrial analytical lab: load wafer/substrate, exchange and align probe, scan several sites, measure roughness, step-height thickness and defect topography, report numbers against spec.

Electron-microscopy characterization of CNT, polymer or inorganic coatings in an analytical lab: cleave/mount/sputter-coat a coupon or make a FIB cross-section, image morphology and cross-section, measure film thickness/coverage/nanotube density, take EDS composition, and interpret what the images mean for the process.

Bench characterization of coated coupons (glass, flexible film, wafer pieces) in an R&D or QC lab using several techniques: four-point-probe sheet resistance mapping, UV-Vis transmittance/haze, Raman D/G ratio, optical microscopy for pinholes/agglomerates; mount each odd-sized sample, run instruments, tabulate results.

At-line quality control on a coating / roll-to-roll pilot production line: inspect the moving coated web or coated parts for streaks, pinholes, agglomerates and coat-weight variation, pull periodic samples for quick gauge measurement, log data and alert process engineers.

Non-routine characterization work in the lab: odd-geometry or novel samples, method development and technique selection for a new coating, correlating results across techniques, troubleshooting anomalous or contradictory data, and instrument calibration/qualification with standards.

instances.label: Electron microscopy session in a shared characterization lab: technician receives assorted research specimens (powders, films, chips, TEM grids), mounts them on stubs/holders, sputter-coats if needed, loads into the SEM/TEM chamber, pumps down, hunts for features of interest, acquires images and EDS/EELS spectra at multiple sites, and saves/logs the data with metadata for the engineer.

Process metrology inside a nanofabrication cleanroom or wafer fab during a fabrication run: measure film thickness (ellipsometry/reflectometry), critical dimensions (CD-SEM), particle/defect counts, sheet resistance or step height on wafers, and enter results into the process database / SPC charts.

Scanning probe microscopy characterization of research samples: mount a small chip, flake or coated substrate, align and engage the tip, scan several regions in topography/PFM/conductive modes, replace worn tips, extract roughness, height and electrical data, and export plots for the supervising engineer.

Solution-phase characterization of nanomaterial dispersions in a wet lab: dilute, sonicate and pipette suspensions, run DLS/zeta potential, UV-Vis/photoluminescence or chromatography using standard methods on shared bench instruments, and compile the results into a spreadsheet or notebook.

Powder/solid and batch-run characterization: sample material from a synthesis reactor, furnace or coating line at set intervals, pack XRD holders or TGA crucibles, run BET/XRD/TGA or QC measurements on the sampled product, and record process parameters and results in run logs.

Ad-hoc data collection on custom, one-off experimental setups: assemble or modify a test fixture, wire and probe a novel device, rig sensors or an environmental chamber for a non-standard sample geometry, take readings across conditions, and log them.

tasks.label: Implement new or enhanced methods or processes for the processing, testing, or manufacture of nanotechnology materials or products.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Nanofab/cleanroom: implement a new or revised process recipe on fab tools (ALD/CVD/PVD deposition, plasma etch, e-beam or optical lithography and resist development) — set parameters, run test wafers/chips, take metrology (thickness, CD, resistance), iterate to spec and qualify the recipe for routine use.

Wet chemistry lab: implement or scale a new nanomaterial synthesis/functionalization protocol (colloidal nanoparticle or quantum-dot synthesis, dispersion, surface functionalization) — dose precursors, control temperature/atmosphere, work up and purify, characterize product, tune conditions until output meets spec, document the protocol.

Analytical lab: implement a new or enhanced characterization/testing method (SEM/TEM/AFM/XRD/DLS) — prepare specimens (e.g., FIB lamella), calibrate against standards, define acquisition and analysis settings, validate repeatability, and put the method into routine use.

Pilot or production facility: physically install, retrofit and commission equipment required by the enhanced process — mount and align hardware on a roll-to-roll coater/electrospinner/reactor, connect gas, fluid and electrical lines, leak-check, calibrate sensors, and bring the line up.

Production floor: run qualification/trial batches of the new process on commercial-scale equipment alongside operators — set parameters, run material, pull in-process samples for QC, adjust conditions to bring output within spec, and record the run.

tasks.label: Develop or modify wet chemical or industrial laboratory experimental techniques for nanoscale use.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In an R&D wet lab (fume hood, hotplate-stirrers, syringes, centrifuge), modify an existing colloidal nanomaterial synthesis recipe (e.g., gold nanoparticles, quantum dots) to hit a target size/emission: run successive batches varying precursor concentration, temperature, injection rate and time, characterize each by UV-Vis/DLS/PL, and issue the revised written protocol.

Develop a genuinely new wet-chemical procedure for a novel nanomaterial or new application: select unfamiliar reagents, assemble non-standard glassware/Schlenk or glovebox apparatus, write the hazard assessment, then troubleshoot unexpected failures (aggregation, contamination, poor yield) by inventing or re-ordering process steps until a workable technique exists.

In a cleanroom or nanofab wet bench, adapt a wet-chemical substrate process (etch, clean, silanization, solution deposition) for nanoscale features: adjust bath chemistry, temperature, immersion time and rinse/dry steps across trial coupons or wafers, measure with ellipsometry/profilometry/SEM, and lock down the modified recipe.

Modify a nanoparticle surface-functionalization/conjugation workflow (ligand exchange, PEGylation, antibody coupling) together with its purification train (centrifugal washing, dialysis, filtration); iterate ligand ratios, pH and wash conditions and verify by zeta potential, DLS and binding assays.

Adapt a bench-scale wet-chemical nanomaterial technique to pilot- or production-scale equipment (larger jacketed reactor or continuous flow line): change addition rates, mixing, residence time and thermal profile, run scale-up trials on the plant equipment, and confirm product quality matches the bench material.

Modify a sample-preparation technique so nanoscale characterization works: develop a dispersion/sonication and dilution recipe, deposit by drop-casting on TEM grids or spin/blade coating on substrates, dry/anneal, then iterate until imaging or spectra are reproducible and artifact-free.

tasks.label: Measure emission of nanodust or nanoparticles during nanocomposite or other nano-scale production processes, using systems such as aerosol detection systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled area/route monitoring of a nanomaterial production suite or pilot line: technician carries real-time aerosol instruments (handheld CPC, diffusion-charger nanoparticle counter, optical counter) to a set of pre-defined points (background/outdoor reference, corridor, near reactor, near powder handling), samples each point for a defined time, logs concentrations and size data, and reports against baseline. Indoor, climate-controlled, institution-controlled facility.

Source-directed, task-based measurement during one specific production operation (reactor discharge, powder weighing/bagging, sonication or dispersion, compounding/extrusion, cutting or sanding of a nanocomposite part): technician positions the sampling inlet centimeters-to-tens-of-centimeters from the emission point and at the operator's work position, times the measurement to the process cycle, annotates process events, and compares near-field to far-field readings on a working production floor with people and moving equipment.

Area filter-cassette and TEM-grid sample collection alongside real-time data: pre-calibrate pump flow, load 25/37 mm cassettes or electrostatic/thermophoretic grid samplers, place at designated area locations for a shift, retrieve, post-calibrate, seal, label and submit for gravimetric/electron-microscopy analysis, in the production facility.

Personal breathing-zone sampling on operators handling nanomaterials: fit a pump and cassette/cyclone on the worker, calibrate flow, record the worker's activities through the shift, retrieve and log the sample so exposure can be attributed to specific handling tasks.

Fixed/continuous emission monitoring at process equipment: sampling lines plumbed to enclosure, glovebox exhaust or duct ports feeding a continuously running nanoparticle monitor; technician verifies zero/flow calibration, keeps the instrument running, checks alarm thresholds and reviews trend data over days-to-weeks in the plant.

Measurement at an off-site or non-standard location: partner pilot plant, a job shop machining nanocomposite parts, a customer installation, or the area around an outdoor exhaust vent. Layout unknown in advance, equipment and enclosures differ from site to site, no mapped sampling points, instruments set up on tripods and stands as space allows.

tasks.label: Perform functional tests of nano-enhanced assemblies, components, or systems, using equipment such as torque gauges or conductivity meters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine electrical functional characterization in an R&D/QC lab: a batch of nano-enhanced coupons, coated films or printed devices arrives from a process run; the technician measures sheet resistance/conductivity with a four-point probe or conductivity meter, takes I–V or continuity readings, checks against spec, and logs data into the lab notebook/LIMS.

Mechanical functional testing of nano-enhanced assemblies and materials: torque-gauge verification of coated/nano-lubricated fasteners and joints, torsion/break-loose checks, and tensile, flexure or adhesion tests on nanocomposite specimens using a universal testing machine, with pass/fail against a written procedure.

In-line or at-line functional test on a pilot or commercial-scale production line: repetitive probe/continuity/parametric test of nano-enhanced dies, sensors or components as they come off the line, high volume, standard carriers and fixtures, binning and yield reporting.

Environmental / reliability functional testing: loading nano-enhanced parts into thermal-cycling, humidity or burn-in chambers and re-measuring electrical or mechanical function at intervals over hours to days, tracking drift and failures.

First-article or novel prototype system-level functional test: a one-off nano-enhanced assembly with no established procedure; the technician improvises or adapts a fixture, connects instrumentation and leads, runs the functional test, diagnoses anomalous or intermittent readings, re-runs, and writes up results for the engineer.

tasks.label: Compare the performance or environmental impact of nanomaterials by nanoparticle size, shape, or organization.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench performance comparison in a company R&D or QC lab: technician draws 3-6 lots/batches of nanoparticles differing in nominal size or shape (e.g., Ag ink, TiO2 photocatalyst, CNT dispersion), prepares dispersions or test solutions in a fume hood, runs a functional test on each (catalytic/photocatalytic conversion, UV-vis/photoluminescence, film conductivity), tabulates results and ranks the variants against spec for the supervising engineer.

Particle-size / dispersion metrology comparison in an analytical lab: dilute and disperse several lots, run DLS, nanoparticle tracking, zeta potential or laser diffraction on each, and compare mean size, polydispersity, agglomeration state and surface charge across the lots; issue a comparative data sheet.

Electron-microscopy morphology comparison: prepare TEM grids or SEM stubs from several nanomaterial samples (drop-cast, dry, sputter-coat), acquire high-magnification images, measure hundreds of particles per sample, and compare size distributions, shape/aspect-ratio statistics and degree of ordering or agglomeration between samples.

Environmental-impact / EHS comparison in a tox or EHS lab: rank nanoparticle variants (size, coating, shape) by dissolution/ion release measured with ICP-MS, by cell-based or zebrafish-embryo ecotoxicity assays in microplates, or by powder dustiness/release testing; report which variant poses the lower hazard.

Application-level comparison in a materials-testing lab: fabricate coupons or devices containing different nanoparticle grades (composite bars, coated panels, electrode films, half-cells), then compare mechanical, tribological, electrical or electrochemical performance on standard test frames/cyclers and report which nanofiller size or morphology performs best.

Desk-based comparison at a lab workstation or office: compile existing batch characterization records, prior test results, supplier data and literature values for several nanomaterial grades, build comparison tables and plots of property versus particle size/shape, and write up the comparison for engineers. No new samples handled.

tasks.label: Process nanoparticles or nanostructures, using technologies such as ultraviolet radiation, microwave energy, or catalysis.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine bench-scale batch processing of a nanoparticle dispersion in an industrial or university R&D lab: weigh/dispense precursors or as-received nanoparticles into vials or flasks, seal, run a programmed microwave-reactor cycle or UV photoreactor exposure per an SOP, quench, then centrifuge/wash/redisperse the product and label it for characterization. Repeated across a batch of samples with standard labware.

Catalysis/photocatalysis process runs: load catalyst or catalyst-loaded nanoparticle suspensions into an illuminated photoreactor, or charge a packed-bed/gas-flow catalytic reactor, set light intensity, gas flows, temperature and time, run the matrix of conditions, sample the product stream and quantify by GC/UV-vis, and log results. Done in a lab or pilot facility over hours to days.

Production-fab cleanroom substrate processing at standard wafer format: a cassette/FOUP of wafers is processed through UV-cure, UV/photo patterning (e.g. UV-cured nanoimprint) or catalyst-mediated CVD/ALD nanostructure growth on qualified tools; technician dispatches lots, runs recipes and checks metrology. Fixed layout, standardized carriers, strict contamination protocol.

Shared-user research nanofabrication cleanroom: small coupons, half-wafers and odd substrates handled with tweezers, loaded into UV-ozone cleaners, mask aligners/UV exposure boxes and tube furnaces with catalyst-seeded substrates; recipes vary sample to sample and tools are older, manually loaded and shared among many users.

Commercial-scale production processing: run continuous-flow microwave or plasma nanoparticle processing equipment, or an inline UV-curing coating / roll-to-plate nanoimprint line; load feedstock or substrates, monitor and adjust process parameters against spec, pull in-process QC samples, and perform product changeovers and cleaning on the plant floor.

Non-routine work: bring up a new UV/microwave/catalytic process on unfamiliar or improvised apparatus, troubleshoot a failed or off-spec run, replace UV lamps and quartz sleeves, re-plumb gas lines or reactor fittings, and handle unusual or out-of-spec material, working with an engineer.

Field commissioning or troubleshooting of installed equipment at a customer plant, building, or job site (HVAC and refrigeration systems, pumps, compressors, conveyors, packaged machinery): take readings against rated specs, then align couplings, tension belts, balance airflow, adjust regulators or limit switches, and re-verify.

tasks.label: Conduct failure analyses, document results, and recommend corrective actions.

instances.label: Plant-floor equipment failure investigation: a production machine goes down (seized pump bearing, cracked gearbox shaft, hydraulic or conveyor failure). The technician goes to the machine, observes symptoms, locks out and partially disassembles it, inspects worn/broken parts, takes measurements (alignment, runout, clearances), reviews operator accounts and machine logs, then documents findings and recommends corrective action (realignment, lubrication change, part upgrade).

Laboratory failure analysis of a returned or broken component (fastener, weld, casting, shaft, bracket): receive and log the part, do visual/stereomicroscope examination of fracture surfaces, decide where to section, cut, mount, grind/polish and etch specimens, run hardness and dimensional checks, do SEM fractography or chemical verification, then write a report identifying root cause (fatigue, overload, embrittlement, bad heat treat) with recommended corrective actions.

Failure during durability/qualification testing on a test rig or test cell: a prototype or test article fails mid-test. The technician documents the failure event and test conditions, verifies instrumentation and fixturing were not the cause, tears down the test article, inspects the failed interface, determines whether the cause is design, manufacturing, or test setup, and recommends design change and retest.

Production quality nonconformance investigation: a recurring in-line defect or batch of rejected parts (out-of-tolerance dimensions, weld defects, misassembly). The technician inspects/measures the rejected parts, traces the defect to a process source (tool wear, fixture drift, weld parameter, misfeed), records results in the quality system (SPC/8D), and recommends the process correction.

Field or customer-site failure: equipment fails in service (installed HVAC/packaging/construction or agricultural machine). The technician travels to the site, inspects the machine in place under uncontrolled conditions and access, gathers failed parts and service history, photographs the installation, then documents findings and recommends corrective actions such as repair, retrofit, or changed maintenance practice.

instances.label: Bench test of components/specimens (coupons, brackets, fasteners, springs, seals) on standard lab machines — universal test frame, fatigue rig, hardness tester — to compare a proposed material or design change: retrieve specimens, measure dimensions, install in grips/fixtures, set parameters, run to failure or through cycles, log and reduce data. Setting: company or contract engineering test lab.

Performance test of a complete assembled unit (pump, gearbox, e-motor, small engine, compressor, HVAC unit) on a test stand or dynamometer: mount the unit, connect electrical harness, coolant/lubricant/fluid lines, attach thermocouples, pressure and torque instrumentation, sweep through operating points, record performance for a proposed improvement. Setting: instrumented test cell in an engineering facility.

Durability, life-cycle or environmental testing: fixture the unit on a shaker, servohydraulic rig, pressure-cycle stand or in a thermal/climatic chamber, wire up instrumentation, run long automated cycles under simulated operational loads, monitor for anomalies and inspect periodically to compare a baseline against a proposed change. Setting: durability/environmental test lab bay.

Vehicle or mobile-equipment testing at a proving ground, test track, or chassis dynamometer: install data acquisition, sensors and (often) driving actuation, run defined duty cycles or maneuvers, capture fuel/emissions/thermal/dynamics data to evaluate a proposed change. Setting: institution-controlled proving ground or vehicle test cell.

In-situ/field test of a proposed modification on installed equipment under real operating conditions at a plant, customer site or outdoor jobsite: rig temporary sensors and data loggers onto the running machine, run production or duty trials, watch for anomalies, troubleshoot, then de-instrument. Setting varies site to site and is not kept to a test standard.

instances.label: Engineer hands the technician a CAD model of a new or revised part (bracket, housing, fixture plate, adapter) and asks for one or a few pieces: technician picks stock/material and process, programs the CNC or slices for the printer, runs the machine in the company prototype/machine shop, deburrs and checks the part, and delivers it.

Hands-on build-up of one-off hardware in the engineering lab or model shop: assembling and wiring a prototype machine or test article from mixed purchased and fabricated parts and drawings, bonding strain gauges/thermocouples, plumbing and cabling a bespoke test rig, then fitting, shimming and reworking until it functions as the engineer intends.

Running standardized tests to a written procedure in a company test lab: tensile/flexure/impact coupons, component life and cyclic tests, load/pressure/leak checks on production or prototype units, with specimens or units loaded into an existing standard rig, the test executed, and data logged into a report.

Dimensional inspection supporting manufacture: first-article and in-process measurement of machined or molded parts against the drawing/GD&T using CMM, comparative gauge, calipers and micrometers in the shop's metrology area, recording results and flagging out-of-tolerance features.

Desk-based design support at the engineer's direction: building or revising CAD models, producing detail and assembly drawings, tolerance stack-ups and simple calculations, BOMs, and writing up test reports and change documentation.

On-site support away from the bench: installing, commissioning, adjusting or troubleshooting industrial machinery on a production floor or at a customer/field site, with unpredictable layout, access constraints and unknown fault conditions.

instances.label: Materials/parts lab: technician runs standardized coupon-level tests on prototype materials or parts using a universal testing machine (tensile, compression, flexure, hardness, fatigue/DMA), sometimes in a temperature chamber — measures the specimen, fixtures it in grips, fits the extensometer, runs the standard method, logs and reports results.

Environmental/durability lab: life-cycle, thermal or vibration testing of a prototype component or product on a dedicated rig or chamber — the article is fixtured, thermocouples/accelerometers attached, the profile programmed, and cycles run for hours or days while the technician monitors, records data and logs failures.

One-off bench setup for a novel prototype: technician improvises or fabricates fixturing from lab hardware and clamps, mounts the article, wires load cells/thermocouples/strain gauges into a DAQ, zeroes and calibrates, debugs leaks/noise/misalignment, then runs the test and records results, adapting the rig when things go wrong.

Prototype vehicle or mobile machine at a company proving ground or test track: technician instruments the prototype (sensors, telemetry, data logger), sets up the test-control gear, runs the test cycles or supervises a driving robot, and records the results.

Field test of a prototype installed at a customer plant or outdoors (e.g., prototype pump skid, HVAC unit, agricultural implement): technician rigs instrumentation onto the as-installed machine, sets up portable data acquisition, runs the test, and records results under uncontrolled site conditions.

Test lab build-up: create a one-off test setup — machine or bolt up custom fixtures and adapters, mount the DUT to a shaker head, thermal chamber rack or hydraulic actuator, plumb hydraulic/pneumatic and coolant lines, install load cells and LVDTs, align and torque, dry-run the profile, then tear the setup down afterward.

Field or proving-ground test support: instrument a vehicle, engine or machine in place for road-load data acquisition, field durability or customer-site validation — mount sensors and telemetry in cramped, dirty, weather-exposed locations, ride along or monitor remotely, troubleshoot and re-tape/re-wire failed channels between runs.

Shop fabrication of a sheet-metal or welded component for a machine modification: cut and form sheet or plate, tack and weld a bracket, guard, frame or enclosure, grind welds, and check fit against the equipment it mounts to.

Prototype lab: produce a polymer (or occasionally metal) prototype component by additive manufacturing — prepare the build file, print unattended, remove the part from the platform, remove supports and post-process, verify dimensions and fit before handing to the engineer.

Bench build of a small batch (roughly 5–20 units) of a modified mechanical subassembly for testing: kitted, fixtured parts joined by repeated operations — press/slip fits, screwdriving to torque spec, clip and connector insertion — followed by a go/no-go check.

One-off build and fit-up of a new prototype mechanism or test rig on the lab bench: press bearings, align shafts and couplings, shim and adjust clearances, route wiring and tubing, discover interferences that the drawing did not anticipate, rework parts by hand and re-fit until the mechanism runs correctly.

Modify installed machinery in place: measure an existing machine on the plant floor or at a customer site, fabricate or adapt a component to suit, then fit it in situ — drilling and tapping into existing structure, aligning, bolting, shimming, and functionally testing in cramped, as-found space around live equipment.

Field visit to inspect and monitor installed mechanical equipment at a customer or remote site (rooftop HVAC units, pump stations, substation and utility equipment, plant under construction): varied layout, weather exposure, ladders/roof hatches; visual condition check, gauge/temperature readings, thermography, leak check, written condition report.

Diagnostic troubleshooting of a malfunctioning machine: partial teardown of guards/covers/housings, inspection of internal components for wear, measuring clearances, backlash and runout with hand instruments, testing subsystems (hydraulic pressure, belt tension, bearing play) to isolate the fault, then reassembly and re-test.

instances.label: Engine / e-motor / transmission dynamometer test cell setup: mount the unit on a bedplate or pallet, align and couple the driveshaft, plumb fuel, coolant, oil, intake and exhaust connections, install dozens of thermocouples, pressure transducers and encoders at the locations called out in the test spec, wire them to the cell's automation and DAQ system, leak-check and commission the cell before the run.

Whole-vehicle test setup and instrumentation: prepare a prototype vehicle in a garage/prep bay or at a proving ground — mount DAQ boxes, GPS/IMU, wheel-force transducers, brake and exhaust thermocouples, accelerometers; route and tie wiring through the cabin and underbody; tap CAN/OBD; strap the vehicle to a chassis dyno or set up the cooling fan and emissions sampling per the drive-cycle procedure; calibrate and zero channels.

Servo-hydraulic durability / structural rig setup: bolt a component or subsystem (knuckle, control arm, seat, door, axle, subframe) into a bespoke steel fixture on a load frame or multi-axis rig, connect hydraulic actuators, hoses and manifolds, install load cells, LVDTs and strain gauges, set actuator limits, interlocks and control gains per the engineering test procedure, then tune and verify the drive file.

Electrical/electronic bench test setup for an ECU, inverter, motor controller or HIL rig: build a harness breakout, land dozens of connector pins, connect power supplies, load banks, sensor simulators and CAN/LIN/Ethernet interfaces, configure instrumentation and safety limits in accordance with the test specification.

Battery cell/module electrical test setup: place the cell or module in its fixture, land the power terminals and voltage/temperature sense leads on the cycler or impedance analyzer channel, position it in the thermal chamber, and configure the channel for the specified cycling or EIS procedure.

Specimen/coupon and small-part mechanical test setup on a universal test machine: install the correct grips or fixtures, load the coupon (metal, plastic, weld, adhesive lap shear) square in the grips, attach or align the extensometer, and configure rate, limits and data channels per the ASTM/ISO or in-house standard.
