instances.label: Office/photo lab: technician assembles an uncontrolled (index) mosaic from 10-40 overlapping aerial photo prints on a light table — matching image detail across overlaps, trimming each print along the matched line with knife and straightedge, then adhering the trimmed prints to a mounting board with spray adhesive or wax so seams butt cleanly.

Mapping office: semi-controlled/controlled mosaic laid to ground control points on a gridded base sheet at a specified scale — each print trimmed, positioned so plotted control points fall on their grid coordinates within tolerance, edges feathered, then mounted, titled and edge-labeled for reproduction.

Production/plot room: joining 2-8 large-format plotted imagery or map panels into one continuous sheet — trimming plotter margins square, butt-joining panels with tape or adhesive holding the sheet-to-sheet register, and mounting the result on foam board for a display or exhibit.

Digital-first workflow with a physical deliverable: orthomosaic produced in software, printed as tiled sheets, and the technician trims register margins and joins the tiles into a scaled wall map or presentation board, checking that scaled distances between labeled reference points survive the assembly.

Field office trailer / tailgate at a construction, mining or survey site: quick assembly or repair of a taped-together imagery mosaic or tiled plot on a folding table with a utility knife and tape, in dust, wind and poor lighting, to serve immediate field use.

instances.label: Cattle line/breed cross in a research or commercial dairy-beef herd: scientist selects the sire, detects or synchronizes estrus, thaws and loads the semen straw, restrains the cow in a headlock or chute, passes the AI gun through the cervix by transrectal manipulation, and records the mating and resulting pregnancy/calf.

Swine line cross in a nucleus or research herd: boar semen collected at the stud (mount dummy, collect, extend, dose), then gilts/sows in stalls checked for standing heat and inseminated intracervically or post-cervically with back-pressure stimulation; litters tagged and pedigreed.

Poultry pedigree line cross in a breeder house: selected males moved into single-sire pens with selected hens for natural mating, or (turkeys, heavy lines) semen collected by abdominal massage and hens caught and inseminated; pedigree eggs collected, labelled and set in pedigree trays.

Extensive pasture/range crossbreeding of beef cattle, sheep or goats: selected bulls/rams turned out with breeding groups, or animals gathered into a field handling facility for synchronization and AI; mud, weather, uneven ground, loose animals, variable site layout.

Embryo-based cross on the animal: donor female superovulated or aspirated (ultrasound-guided OPU with transrectal manipulation), and resulting crossbred embryos transferred non-surgically into recipient females restrained in a chute at a farm or clinic.

Laboratory in vitro crossing: gametes arrive at the lab (frozen semen dose from the chosen sire, oocytes from the chosen dam or abattoir ovaries); scientist matures oocytes, prepares sperm, performs fertilization/micro-injection at a micromanipulation bench and cultures embryos to blastocyst; deliverable is graded crossbred embryos.

tasks.label: Inspect food processing areas to ensure compliance with government regulations and standards for sanitation, safety, quality, and waste management.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-production GMP/sanitation walkthrough of processing and packaging rooms: QA/food scientist walks the line while it runs, checking food-contact surfaces and equipment legs/undersides for residue, condensation and drip points, standing water and drains, product exposure, allergen and glass/brittle-plastic controls, and employee hygiene practices (hairnets, jewelry, handwashing, cross-contamination behavior); records deviations on a checklist and issues corrective actions.

Pre-operational sanitation inspection after wet cleaning: inspect disassembled equipment (fillers, slicers, conveyors, hoppers) with flashlight and mirror, feel surfaces for film, look into crevices and hidden framework, verify with ATP/protein swabs, then either release the line for start-up or send areas back for re-cleaning.

Environmental monitoring / verification sampling round: collect sponge and swab samples from designated Zone 1-4 points (food-contact surfaces, equipment framework, floors, drains, wall-floor junctions), maintain aseptic technique, label and log each sample location, and deliver to the lab for indicator/pathogen testing.

Facility safety, housekeeping and condition round through processing areas: check for leaks and spills, slip/trip hazards, blocked exits or propped doors, fire extinguishers and safety signage in place, guards, lighting, overheating motors/bearings and other equipment condition issues; log findings and notify maintenance/EHS.

Waste-management, dock, warehouse and exterior grounds inspection: waste streams and segregation, compactors and dumpsters, trash rooms and floor drains, rendering/by-product handling, pest-control devices and evidence, and the condition of receiving docks and exterior grounds around the plant.

Regulatory or third-party audit walkthrough: accompany an FDA/USDA-FSIS investigator or SQF/BRC auditor through the plant, verify CCP monitoring and sanitation records against what is seen on the floor, answer questions, and respond to written observations with corrective actions.

tasks.label: Check raw ingredients for maturity or stability for processing, and finished products for safety, quality, and nutritional value.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Finished-product compositional / nutritional analysis in a QA or contract food lab: receive a retained retail unit or production sample, grind/homogenize and weigh it, run proximate analysis (moisture, fat, protein, ash), sugars and vitamin panels by Kjeldahl/Soxhlet/HPLC/NIR, then interpret against the nutrition label spec and release or hold the lot.

Finished-product safety testing in a food lab: weigh and dilute/stomach a sample, run micro indicator counts and pathogen enrichment/plating (Salmonella, Listeria, E. coli, TVC) and chemical safety screens (mycotoxins, veterinary drug residues, pesticide residues, allergens), incubate, read/enumerate, confirm and report a pass/fail disposition.

Incoming raw-ingredient lot testing with samples brought to the QA lab: raw milk (fat, protein, somatic cells, bacterial count, antibiotic screen), grain/flour (moisture, protein, mycotoxins, falling number), oils (peroxide value, FFA), fruit purees (Brix, pH) — decide whether the lot is mature/stable enough to process.

In-process checks on the plant floor: pull units off a running filling, packing or grinding line and check fill weight, density/Brix/alcohol, pH, viscosity, fat content, seal integrity, foreign material and temperature; flag drift and stop or adjust the line.

Organoleptic / sensory evaluation of raw materials and finished product: taste, smell, look at and feel samples for off-notes, rancidity, texture defects and appearance against a gold standard, either at the line or in a sensory booth, and score them.

Field, orchard or grower-site assessment of raw material maturity and condition before harvest or shipment: walk the block or the grower's shed, sample fruit/vegetables/grain as found, judge ripeness, firmness, starch index, defects and field heat, and set harvest timing or accept/reject the lot.

tasks.label: Study methods to improve aspects of foods, such as chemical composition, flavor, color, texture, nutritional value, and convenience.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench-scale formulation/ingredient screening study with instrumental endpoints in a company R&D lab: weigh powders, oils, hydrocolloids and solutions, prepare dozens of small variants across a designed matrix, measure viscosity/texture, color, solubility, moisture, emulsion stability, iterate and recommend a formulation that improves composition, texture or nutrition.

Taste-driven bench prototyping in an R&D kitchen/lab: cook or assemble prototypes of a reformulated product (reduced sugar/sodium, plant-based analogue, new flavor system), taste and assess mouthfeel with the bench team, adjust seasoning/flavor/fat systems and iterate until the prototype is accepted.

Pilot-plant process trial to improve texture, nutrient retention or convenience: set up and hook up pilot equipment (twin-screw extruder, retort, HTST/UHT, spray dryer, HPP), run a matrix of process settings with real ingredient volumes, collect hot/wet samples during runs, clean down between runs, and select improved conditions.

Analytical characterization study of experimental samples in an analytical/QA lab: extract and prepare samples, run HPLC/GC/plate-reader/proximate methods for vitamins, sugars, fat, protein or contaminants across the variants of an improvement study, and compare the options against targets.

Shelf-life / storage-stability study: package prototype variants, load controlled-temperature/humidity chambers, pull replicate samples on a schedule over weeks or months, open packages and run color, pH, oxidation, vitamin, microbiological and quick sensory checks, then model shelf life.

Sensory panel or consumer test study in a sensory facility: portion and code samples to protocol, serve them to trained panelists or consumers in booths, run the session, and analyze the ratings to judge whether a change improved flavor, texture or appearance.

sources.system: Mobile robotic chemist (KUKA mobile manipulator)
sources.title: A mobile robotic chemist - University of Liverpool Repository (Nature 583:237-241)
sources.claim: A free-roaming mobile robot autonomously ran a closed-loop, multi-component formulation optimization campaign (688 experiments over 8 days in a 10-variable space) in a chemistry laboratory, identifying mixtures six times more active than ... starting formulations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous optimization of multi-component mixtures. Transfer is partial - the loop (dispense solids/liquids, mix, measure a target property instrumentally, choose the next experiment) is the same loop used in bench formulation screening, but the materials are photocatalyst slurries in vials, not foods, and the stations were set up for robot access.

sources.system: Robotic powdered-beverage optimization platform

tasks.label: Study the structure and composition of food or the changes foods undergo in storage and processing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Analytical laboratory work-up of food samples to establish composition (moisture, fat, protein, sugars, vitamins, salt, residues): the sample is received and logged, subsampled and homogenized, weighed, extracted/cleaned up (e.g., QuEChERS/SPE), run on HPLC/GC-MS/Kjeldahl/NIR, and the chromatograms and QC checks reviewed before the result is issued.

Shelf-life / accelerated storage study: packaged product is placed in temperature- and humidity-controlled chambers at several conditions, units are pulled at set time points over weeks to months, then opened and measured for moisture, water activity, color, texture, pH, oxidation (peroxide value) and microbial load, and the trends compared against spec to fix a date code.

Pilot-plant or plant-scale processing trial: raw material is run through an extruder, retort, HTST pasteurizer, dryer, mixer or freezer at varied settings; in-process and finished samples are pulled at each condition and measured to track the changes processing causes (starch gelatinization, protein denaturation, viscosity, moisture, nutrient loss), with equipment set up, changed over and cleaned between runs.

Structure and physical-property characterization in the lab: texture profile analysis of solid foods on a texture analyser, rheology of batters and emulsions, particle sizing, and light/confocal/SEM microscopy of gels, doughs and emulsions — requiring specimens to be cut, mounted, stained or coated, imaged and interpreted.

Microbiological study of storage/process changes: 25 g portions stomached in diluent, serial dilutions prepared and plated (or Petrifilm), incubated, colonies enumerated at successive storage time points or before/after a lethality step, and spoilage/challenge results interpreted.

On the production floor during a manufacturing run: follow the line, record process conditions (equipment temperatures, times, line instrument readings, thermal profiles), observe how the product changes through the process, and take in-process and finished samples back to the lab.

instances.label: Bench-top sensory assessment of a prototype by the food technologist/development team in a pilot kitchen or sensory lab: the prototype is prepared per protocol, then tasted and judged for flavor, aroma, mouthfeel and appearance against a gold-standard control, with written descriptive notes and a keep/reformulate call.

Administering a formal descriptive or consumer sensory test in booths: preparing prototype and control samples to a fixed protocol, portioning into blind three-digit-coded cups, holding them at specified temperature, serving in randomized order, and compiling panelist scores.

Instrumental physical-property testing of prototype samples in a QA/development lab: texture profile analysis or shear/penetration tests, colorimeter L*a*b* readings, viscosity, pH, water activity, Brix, on replicate samples, with results compared to target specs.

Analytical composition testing for nutrition-label and claim compliance: homogenize/weigh the product, run proximate analysis (moisture, fat, protein, ash), minerals and vitamins by wet chemistry, ICP-MS or chromatography, and check results against label claims and regulatory rounding rules.

Food-safety and regulatory conformance testing on the new product: dilution and plating for indicator organisms/pathogens, shelf-life and challenge sampling, contaminant/residue screening, and verification that results meet government and industry standards.

In-plant pilot or first-production trial verification: pulling product from the pilot/production line, checking fill weight, package integrity, appearance/color, temperature and composition against spec, and confirming the run meets standards before release.

tasks.label: Develop new food items for production, based on consumer feedback.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: CPG manufacturer R&D lab/pilot kitchen: after central-location or home-use test feedback ('too sweet', 'not creamy enough'), the food technologist reformulates an existing SKU or line extension, weighing ingredients, making 0.5-5 kg bench batches, cooking/blending, tasting and iterating over several rounds, then documenting the revised formula and spec.

Novel product concept (e.g., plant-based or better-for-you item) driven by consumer insight: screening supplier ingredient samples, benchtop prototyping with texture/rheology and analytical checks, multiple prototype rounds presented to internal and consumer panels, in a corporate R&D laboratory and test kitchen.

Pilot-plant scale-up of a consumer-approved bench prototype: running trial batches on pilot extruder, retort, HTST/homogenizer or oven line, adjusting process parameters, pulling samples, and verifying the scaled product matches the bench gold standard.

Plant trial / first commercial production run of the new item at a manufacturing facility with operators: tuning formula and line settings to hit target sensory and quality attributes, sampling, and approving the first article for production.

Foodservice chain or small manufacturer test kitchen: developing a new menu item or private-label recipe from customer feedback using off-the-shelf ingredients, scaling the recipe for kitchen or co-packer execution, tasting and revising with the culinary team.

tasks.label: Develop new or improved ways of preserving, processing, packaging, storing, and delivering foods, using knowledge of chemistry, microbiology, and other sciences.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench-scale screening/optimization of a preservation system (antimicrobial or antioxidant blends, pH/water-activity hurdles, humectants) in liquid or semi-liquid model systems in a food R&D lab; dozens of variants are weighed, mixed, held, and assayed against instrumental endpoints (pH, aw, microbial counts, oxidation, color), and the best combination is recommended.

Bench prototype development/reformulation of an actual food product in an R&D lab or experimental kitchen, where the new preservation or processing idea changes eating quality: ingredients weighed, cooked/blended/chilled with kitchen and lab equipment, prototypes iterated against in-house tasting, texture and appearance judgment before a bench standard is signed off.

Laboratory shelf-life or microbiological challenge study on the candidate process or formula: preparing and inoculating sample sets in various food matrices, holding them at set temperatures, pulling replicates at intervals, weighing/homogenizing, plating or PCR, enumerating, measuring pH/aw/texture/color, and concluding on the achievable shelf life.

Pilot-plant trial of a new or improved process (retort, high-pressure processing, extrusion, drying, aseptic fill): rigging and setting up the line, running a parameter matrix, hot-sampling mid-run, troubleshooting fouling and hardware, cleaning between runs, and evaluating the resulting product.

Packaging development and evaluation: assembling prototype packs, running seal-integrity, barrier (OTR/WVTR) and distribution/drop testing, setting up storage trials, and selecting film, tray or closure combinations in consultation with suppliers.

Plant-scale scale-up/commercialization trial in a manufacturing facility: first production runs of the new process or pack, on-line adjustments with operators and engineers, sampling for QA, and sign-off of the production specification.

sources.system: Mobile robotic chemist (Burger et al.)

It transfers to bench-scale preservation-system screening because the physical acts are the same class (dispensing and mixing measured quantities of liquid/solid components into vessels, transferring them to an analytical station, and choosing the next formulations from the measured response), and the endpoints in that food instance are instrumental rather than sensory. It does not transfer to cooked/solid food matrices or taste-based acceptance.

instances.label: Customer visit to the supplier's applications lab / customer innovation center: the food technologist prepares prototype applications on the spot (bakes, blends, extrudes, pours beverage bases) using the client's target formulation, sets up a tasting, walks the client's R&D team through functionality, and adjusts dosage or formulation live in response to their reactions.

Demonstration meeting at the client's office or R&D kitchen: pre-made prototype samples are transported in coolers or cases, then plated, poured, warmed or otherwise presented; the scientist serves them, presents supporting analytical and sensory data, and fields technical questions.

Trade show or industry expo booth (e.g., IFT FIRST, SupplySide): repeatedly prepares and hands out bite-size or shot-size prototype samples of ingredient applications to a stream of prospective B2B customers, explains ingredient functionality (sweetening, mouthfeel, protein fortification), and captures leads.

Demonstration trial at a pilot plant or the client's processing plant: the ingredient or process is run on pilot or production equipment in front of the customer's technical team, line parameters are adjusted, output is sampled and evaluated, and performance is explained against the client's spec.

Remote/virtual demonstration: prototype samples are prepared, portioned, labelled and shipped to the client, then the scientist runs a benchtop demonstration on camera (dissolving, whipping, gelling, tasting protocol) and guides the client through evaluating the shipped samples.

tasks.label: Seek substitutes for harmful or undesirable additives, such as nitrites.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench screening of candidate replacers in liquid or model solution systems (e.g., replacing benzoate/sorbate in a beverage, replacing synthetic colors with anthocyanin extracts, antioxidant replacers in a brine): the scientist prepares dozens of small samples from stock ingredients across dose levels and pH, measures pH, color, absorbance/HPLC, oxidation markers and stability, and iterates toward a shortlist. Company or university R&D lab, standard glassware, balances and benchtop instruments.

Bench formulation of dry blends and simple mixed systems containing the candidate replacer (seasoning/cure premixes, beverage powders, bakery premixes, model emulsions): gravimetric dispensing of many powders and liquids at gram/milligram precision into replicate samples, hydration/emulsification, and instrumental readout of solubility, color and stability. R&D lab.

Bench/test-kitchen prototypes in cooked, cured or fermented matrices — e.g., 2-5 kg experimental batches of bacon, frankfurters or ham cured with cultured celery powder instead of sodium nitrite, or bread/sauce/dairy prototypes without the target additive: weighing minors, grinding and mixing meat batter, stuffing, thermal processing/smoking, chilling, slicing, then measuring cured color, residual nitrite, texture, yield and informally tasting. R&D lab and pilot kitchen.

Microbiological efficacy screening of candidate replacers: broth microdilution/MIC and agar screens of natural antimicrobials against Listeria monocytogenes, Clostridium sporogenes surrogates or spoilage organisms, plating, incubation and colony enumeration, compared against the nitrite/preservative control. Food microbiology laboratory (BSL-2).

Pilot-plant scale trial of the leading substitute: running a several-hundred-pound experimental batch on pilot processing equipment (injector/tumbler, stuffer, smokehouse, retort or filler), adjusting process parameters, sampling through the run, and assessing whether the replacer performs at scale. Institution-run pilot plant.

Formal sensory and consumer evaluation of the reformulated prototype versus the additive-containing control: preparing blinded coded samples, running a trained descriptive panel or consumer acceptance test in booths, collecting and analyzing scores to decide whether the substitute is acceptable. Sensory laboratory.

Desk scouting and documentation: literature and patent searching, ingredient-supplier technical data sheets and samples, regulatory status of the replacer (FDA GRAS, USDA-FSIS labeling of 'no nitrites added'), cost and label implications, ending in a written recommendation/spec for which substitutes to pursue. Office/workstation.

instances.label: Field plot machinery operations on a research farm: laying out and planting a replicated yield trial or breeding nursery of hundreds of small plots, each a distinct seed lot loaded in order on a plot planter, and later harvesting the same plots with a plot combine (per-plot weight and moisture, sample bagging, clean-out between plots) plus hand harvest of selected rows, ears and heads.

In-season instrumented phenotyping of field trials at a research station: repeated passes over hundreds to thousands of plots to record stand counts, plant height, canopy cover/NDVI, growth stage and stress indices, in row crops with alleys, in mud, dust, heat and variable light.

Expert visual scoring and selection walks in the nursery and trials: rating disease severity and lodging, noting flowering and maturity dates, and walking rows to select, tag and mark individual plants, ears or heads for advancement.

Pollination control and controlled crosses in field nursery or greenhouse: emasculating wheat spikes or soybean flowers, bagging and shoot-bagging maize, detasseling, transferring pollen at the right stage, tagging and recording each cross.

Post-harvest seed processing and laboratory analyses supporting selection: threshing and cleaning plot and single-plant samples, counting/weighing and packaging seed lots for the next cycle, seed sampling or chipping, DNA extraction and marker genotyping in plates, and NIR grain quality or tissue nutrient analysis.

Greenhouse or growth-chamber controlled experiments: pot-based drought, salinity, nutrient or seedling screens with imposed watering/treatment regimes and repeated measurement of growth, biomass and physiological traits on hundreds of plants.

instances.label: Controlled-environment treatment experiment on potted plants in a research greenhouse or growth chamber: sow/transplant genotypes into pots, impose and maintain treatments (water deficit to target soil weight, nutrient levels, temperature/CO2, hormone or inhibitor dosing), take repeated growth measurements over weeks, then destructively harvest for biomass and tissue.

Wet-lab mechanistic assays on harvested plant tissue and soil in a university/USDA laboratory: grind and weigh samples, nucleic-acid or metabolite extraction, qPCR, enzyme-activity and nutrient assays on microplates, read on benchtop instruments, output quality-checked data.

Replicated field experiment at a university or USDA research farm, establishment through harvest: lay out and plant randomized plots of many entries with a plot planter, impose differential treatments (fertility rates, irrigation/rain-out shelters, inoculation), manage the trial in season, then harvest plots and determine per-plot yield.

In-season data-collection campaign inside an ongoing research-station field trial: walk/drive the mapped plots collecting canopy and stand measurements, plant height/stem traits, and pulling georeferenced soil cores and tissue samples on schedule, in variable weather and mud.

Experiment sited off-station: an on-farm strip trial in a cooperating grower's field, or plots in forest, rangeland or wetland - install treatments and markers, take soil and plant samples and field measurements at sites with unmapped terrain, residue, brush and no institutional upkeep.

Specialized physiological/structural measurement experiment in a controlled-environment facility: root and shoot growth imaging of plants in rhizotrons, chlorophyll-fluorescence and photosynthesis/leaf-temperature protocols, repeated imaging of individual plants under defined light and climate.

instances.label: Order-2/order-3 soil survey mapping traverse: soil scientist walks or drives a landscape (cropland, pasture, rangeland, woodland), makes hand-auger or spade borings at many observation points, describes horizons (Munsell color, texture by feel, structure, consistence, roots, redox features, effervescence), records slope/landform/landscape position with GPS, assigns each observation to a soil series/taxonomic class and delineates map unit lines. Weather, mud, brush, fences and variable terrain are as found.

Detailed pedon characterization at a benchmark or research site: a pit is opened (spade or backhoe), the face is cleaned, horizon boundaries are marked and described in full detail, samples are taken by horizon and bagged for laboratory characterization, and the pedon is classified to family/series under Soil Taxonomy.

On-site soil evaluation for a client or regulator on a private lot or parcel: test pits or borings for septic/onsite wastewater suitability, hydric-soil/wetland determination, or land-capability classification; scientist inspects profiles for restrictive layers, depth to seasonal water table and redoximorphic features, classifies the soil and writes a signed report. Setting is a residential lot, farm yard or wooded parcel taken as found.

Laboratory characterization of collected samples in a soil testing/characterization lab: air-dry, crush and sieve to <2 mm, weigh, then run particle-size (pipette/hydrometer) analysis, pH/EC, organic carbon, CEC and related determinations, and use the results to assign textural and taxonomic classes and check field calls.

Field-scale soil property mapping for zone classification (precision-ag or research plots): dense georeferenced core collection on a grid or by zone across a production field, analysis of the samples for pH, nutrients, organic matter and texture-related properties, and delineation of the field into soil property classes/management zones.

Research lab microbiological/biochemical assays: dilution series and plate counts or MPN of soil suspensions, microplate fluorometric extracellular enzyme assays (e.g., beta-glucosidase, NAG, phosphatase), substrate-induced respiration; reagents prepared, plates incubated and read, activity computed per gram dry soil.

Commercial/service soil testing lab (agronomic or soil-health suite): receive and log hundreds of samples, dry/grind/sieve, extract (Mehlich-3/Olsen/KCl), ICP and colorimetric determination of nutrients and pH, plus a biological indicator (CO2-burst, PLFA, organic matter), report interpreted for crop nutrient management.

Molecular soil-microbiome workflow: homogenize/bead-beat soil, extract and clean up DNA (humic interference), quantify, run qPCR of functional or 16S targets, prepare amplicon sequencing libraries, normalize and pool; relate community metrics to soil chemistry and plant performance.

Field campaign at research plots or farmer fields: in-situ soil respiration flux chambers and probe/sensor readings at georeferenced points, plus collection and on-site processing (compositing, cooling) of cores for later microbial/chemical assay; variable weather, residue, and terrain.

tasks.label: Conduct experiments investigating how soil forms, changes, or interacts with land-based ecosystems or living organisms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Laboratory execution of a soil experiment: receiving/drying/sieving samples, weighing subsamples, setting up extractions or short incubations, and running chemical and physical characterization (pH/EC, extractable nutrients, loss-on-ignition, texture/particle size, C and N) in a university or service soil laboratory; output is a QC'd data table tied to sample IDs.

Greenhouse or growth-chamber pot experiment on soil-plant interaction (e.g., soil type x fertility x water treatments, inoculation with soil microbes): pots of defined soil, sowing, treatment application, controlled watering to target moisture/weight, repeated growth and stress measurements over weeks; output is a non-destructive growth/water-use dataset.

Destructive and messy experiment steps: harvesting plants from pots or field microplots, excavating and knocking out root balls, washing and separating roots from soil, hand-sectioning intact cores/monoliths, extracting fauna or aggregates, mounting/subsampling heterogeneous wet soil for downstream analysis.

Recurring soil sampling campaign at a replicated cropland field experiment (university research farm or cooperator's field): navigating to prescribed georeferenced points in each treatment plot, augering cores to specified depth, compositing, bagging, labeling and logging position/depth, and delivering samples to the lab.

Field campaign in unmanaged terrain (forest, rangeland, wetland, roadcut, burned or restored site): traversing off-road to sites, digging or describing soil pits, identifying and sampling by horizon, taking bulk-density cores and vegetation/site notes under variable weather, slope, rocks, roots and litter.

Instrumented monitoring within a running experiment: automated soil CO2/CH4 flux chambers, soil moisture/temperature profiles, weighing lysimeters, and repeated in-plot canopy/soil-surface scans over a season at a research farm or experimental station; output is a continuous, gap-checked time series.

tasks.label: Survey undisturbed or disturbed lands for classification, inventory, mapping, environmental impact assessments, environmental protection planning, conservation planning, or reclamation planning.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field soil survey and mapping of a tract of undisturbed land (rangeland, forest, pasture or cropland): traverse the tract on foot/ATV, hand-auger or dig pits at observation points, describe horizons (depth, Munsell color, texture by feel, structure, redox features, roots, coarse fragments), classify pedons to series/taxonomic class, collect horizon samples, and delineate map-unit boundaries on imagery.

Environmental impact assessment / ecological baseline survey of a proposed project parcel: lay out vegetation plots and transects, identify plant species and estimate cover, delineate wetlands using soil, hydrology and vegetation indicators, log photo points, and collect representative soil samples for the impact report.

Ground survey of disturbed land (active or closed mine, quarry, pipeline right-of-way, post-fire or construction-scarred site) for reclamation planning: characterize spoil and salvaged topsoil, test compaction and rooting depth, sample for pH/salinity/metals, map erosion features and rate revegetation success on plots.

Aerial survey flight over a tract for inventory, mapping and monitoring: fly a photogrammetric/multispectral/LiDAR mission over a mine, reclamation area, farm or forest block to produce an orthomosaic, digital terrain model, land-cover / vegetation-cover map, erosion and stockpile measurements, or a timber inventory, repeated for change monitoring.

Georeferenced grid or zone soil sampling campaign over cultivated fields for conservation and nutrient-management planning: navigate the field to hundreds of prescribed points, pull cores to a specified depth, composite and bag them by point, keep the georeference, and deliver samples to the lab for the resulting soil property maps.

tasks.label: Conduct experiments regarding causes of bee diseases or factors affecting yields of nectar or pollen.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Colony-level trial at a research apiary (university farm or cooperating beekeeper's bee yard, outdoors): assign treatment and control colonies, smoke and open standard Langstroth hives, pull and score brood frames for foulbrood/chalkbrood/deformed-wing symptoms, run alcohol-wash or sticky-board varroa counts, apply the assigned miticide or feed treatment, estimate colony strength, and log data across repeated visits through the season in variable weather with defensive bees.

Bench processing of samples brought back from experimental colonies in a university/USDA laboratory: weigh and homogenize pooled bee, brood, wax, honey or bee-bread samples, run magnetic-bead RNA/DNA extraction, set up RT-qPCR plates for viruses/Nosema/pathogens (or prepare pesticide-residue extracts), run the instrument and export quantified results.

Live-bee laboratory bioassays in a lab or environmental chamber: collect newly emerged bees, load 20-30 per cage or graft larvae into plates, dose feeders with pathogen inoculum or test compound at set concentrations, refill and weigh feeders daily, count mortality, and dissect bees for spore loads or gut/ovary scoring under a stereoscope.

Field measurement of nectar and pollen yields across treatment plots of a bee-forage or pollinated crop (orchard, field, or hedgerow): bag flowers, extract nectar with microcapillary tubes and read sugar concentration on a handheld refractometer, collect and weigh anther pollen, count open flowers per unit area, and run timed pollinator-visitation observations under changing sun, wind and bloom stage.

Establishing and maintaining the experimental planting itself: laying out and seeding/transplanting replicated small plots or greenhouse pots of nectar-producing plants, applying the assigned irrigation, fertility or pest-management treatments per plot, and taking repeated growth and bloom-phenology measurements through the trial.

tasks.label: Identify or classify species of insects or allied forms, such as mites or spiders.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scouting a commercial field, orchard or research plot: walking rows, turning leaves, beating/sweeping vegetation, and identifying the insects and mites found in situ (aphids, thrips, spider mites, beetles, borers) to species or species-group, plus checking pheromone/sticky trap catches; conditions vary by site, weather and crop stage.

Bench work in a research lab: processing bulk samples from pitfall traps, sweep nets, Malaise traps or Berlese funnels - picking specimens out of debris/ethanol with forceps under a stereomicroscope, sorting them into taxa (family/genus/morphospecies) and counting them for an experiment or survey.

Fine microscopy on very small allied forms: clearing and slide-mounting mites (phytoseiids, tetranychids, eriophyids) or springtails, examining setal patterns, shields and genitalia under compound/phase-contrast optics, and running published taxonomic keys to a species determination.

Inspection inside a greenhouse, nursery or insectary: reading yellow/blue sticky cards and examining plants to identify whiteflies, thrips, aphids, mites, fungus gnats and released biological-control agents, distinguishing pest from beneficial and recording species and counts.

Formal determination of a submitted or collected specimen in a lab or diagnostic clinic: comparing the specimen with keys and a reference collection, sometimes confirming with DNA barcoding, and issuing a recorded species identification (voucher, diagnostic report, quarantine screen).

sources.claim: DiversityScanner is a benchtop robot that autonomously detects individual small invertebrates in a mixed bulk sample, images and measures each one, and pick-and-places it into a 96-well plate for DNA barcoding - the mechanised equivalent of a technician sorting a trap sample under a scope.

sources.claim: The same robot classifies each imaged specimen into 14 mostly family-level insect classes plus an 'other' class with 91.4% average precision, and its images are labelled with DNA-barcode identifications to reach species-level (MOTU) assignments.

sources.system: BIODISCOVER machine

sources.title: Automatic image-based identification and biomass estimation of invertebrates (Methods in Ecology and Evolution)
sources.claim: BIODISCOVER is a vision-enabled robotic imaging machine that images arthropod specimens presented in an ethanol cuvette, classifies them to species, and physically sorts them via a software-controlled valve that flushes each specimen into the container chosen by the classifier; test accuracy was 98.0% over 12 insect and spider species, above the 93.9% reported for taxonomic experts on physical specimens.

sources.claim: Robotic specimen handling and imaging with the DiversityScanner remains the working pipeline for taxonomic identification of bulk-sample insects in 2026, with deep learning added to triage specimen orientation and sex from the robot's images.

sources.claim: Trapview, the most widely deployed automated field trap (motorised self-cleaning sticky roll plus camera and AI), identifies and counts target moths in orchards but reached only 66-87% count accuracy against manual counts for codling moth because of non-target insects - below the accuracy a scout's employer would accept.

tasks.label: Study physical principles of living cells or organisms and their electrical or mechanical energy, applying methods and knowledge of mathematics, physics, chemistry, or biology.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Patch-clamp electrophysiology on cultured/transfected cell lines or iPSC-derived cells in a university or pharma research lab: harvest cells, form gigaseals, run voltage/current-clamp protocols, apply compounds, extract I-V and kinetics to characterize channel biophysics.

Electrophysiology in intact tissue or living animals: acute brain slices, in vivo whole-cell/extracellular recording in head-fixed mice, cardiac or muscle preparations; targeting individual cells in heterogeneous tissue, hours-long recordings on a custom rig.

Single-molecule / single-cell force biophysics on established instrumentation: AFM nanoindentation of living cells, optical or magnetic tweezers pulling on DNA/protein tethers, smFRET; probe calibration, sample mounting, long acquisitions, force-curve fitting.

Building or adapting a bespoke apparatus/assay to measure a physical property not accessible with off-the-shelf tools: aligning a new optical path, machining a chamber, wiring electrodes, validating the new measurement before any data is taken.

Quantitative live-cell imaging and cell-physiology assays: culture and plate cells, apply perturbations (drug, CRISPR, mechanical), stain, image on an automated microscope, quantify motility, morphology, membrane potential or traction forces.

Structural/molecular biophysics: set up crystallization, harvest and cryo-cool crystals or vitrify grids, load samples, collect synchrotron X-ray or cryo-EM datasets, process to a structure/dynamics model.

tasks.label: Develop new methods to study the mechanisms of biological processes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Industry/screening-center method development with a parameterized space: a biochemist develops a new plate-based biochemical assay or reaction formulation (e.g., enzyme activity assay, cell-free expression mix) — choosing component ranges, running iterative microplate campaigns with automated fluorescence/absorbance readout, converging on validated conditions and documenting an SOP. Automated liquid handling is standard in the facility.

Academic wet-lab development of a novel biochemical/biophysical assay to probe a mechanism (e.g., FRET or coupled-enzyme readout, single-molecule or pull-down based approach): clone and purify the protein, label or modify it, assemble the readout on shared instruments, diagnose artifacts (aggregation, inner-filter effects, interference), and cross-validate against an orthogonal method before writing it up.

Development of a new instrument or physical measurement technique: modify or build optical/spectroscopic hardware (custom microscope, optical tweezers, stopped-flow, EPR/NMR probe), microfluidic chips, or electrophysiology rigs; machine or assemble parts, align and calibrate, characterize noise and resolution against standards, iterate on the design.

Optimization of a cell-culture-based procedure as method development: tuning media, timing, seeding density and supplements for a passaging/differentiation protocol, with automated imaging or plate-reader readouts, in a dedicated automated cell-culture station.

Development of a new cell-based or model-organism approach to study a pathway: engineer reporter constructs and stable lines or organoids, establish perturbation (CRISPR/drug) and live-imaging or biochemical readouts, validate specificity with controls, and package the approach as a reusable protocol.

Computational/analytical method development at a workstation: new algorithms or pipelines for MD trajectory analysis, structure determination, mass-spec or single-cell data, benchmarked against reference datasets and released with documentation.

tasks.label: Determine the three-dimensional structure of biological macromolecules.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine X-ray crystal structure of a well-behaved soluble protein in an academic or pharma structural biology lab: express and purify a construct with established conditions, set up nanolitre crystallization screens, inspect/score drops, harvest and cryo-cool a crystal, collect synchrotron data, solve by molecular replacement, refine, validate, deposit.

Novel or recalcitrant crystallography target (membrane protein, low-yield eukaryotic complex): iterative construct/detergent screening, expression troubleshooting, crystal optimization and additive screening, difficult harvesting, experimental phasing (SAD/MAD), heavy manual map interpretation and rebuilding in a lab and at a beamline.

Single-particle cryo-EM structure of a purified, well-behaved complex at a core cryo-EM facility: vitrify grids, screen grids, run multi-day automated collection on a 300 kV autoloader instrument, process (motion correction, picking, 2D/3D classification, refinement), build and refine an atomic model.

Difficult cryo-EM project: heterogeneous, scarce or detergent/nanodisc-solubilized sample requiring biochemical re-optimization, grid/support and additive screening, preferred-orientation fixes, and expert-guided classification of conformational states before a usable map and model are obtained.

High-throughput ligand/fragment complex determination in a pharma or synchrotron facility pipeline: acoustic dispensing of compounds into crystal drops, soaking, harvesting/cryo-cooling of hundreds of crystals, unattended beamline data collection, automated processing, ligand density detection and refinement of many structures.

Solution NMR structure/dynamics of a small protein, peptide or nucleic acid, or complementary low-resolution determination (BioSAXS envelope, negative-stain EM): prepare isotope-labelled or dilution-series samples in tubes/plates, run automated multi-dimensional acquisition on a spectrometer or beamline sample changer, assign, calculate and validate the model.

tasks.label: Design or build laboratory equipment needed for special research projects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Design-only: the scientist conceives a custom apparatus or instrument modification for a specific experiment (e.g., a temperature-controlled sample stage, a custom cuvette holder, a gravity-fed perfusion manifold), sketches it, produces CAD drawings/tolerances, selects catalog components, and issues a specification to the departmental machine shop or a vendor. No physical build by the scientist; output is a drawing package and parts list.

Digital fabrication of a bespoke part from an existing design: 3D-print (FDM/SLA) or CNC-machine a sample holder, adapter, flow cell, gel tray, or custom reaction vessel in the lab or a core machine shop; remove supports/deburr and finish, verify dimensions and fit.

Build or modify a bench rig: assemble a bespoke perfusion/flow chamber or purification rig from tubing, barbed and Luer fittings, gaskets, valves, a peristaltic pump and a heater; mount it onto an existing microscope stage or chromatography system with clamps and adapters; seal, prime, and leak-test until it holds under working pressure.

Build custom control electronics for an apparatus: populate and solder a small custom PCB or perfboard, wire in thermistors/photodiodes/valve drivers, mount the board in an enclosure with connectors, flash microcontroller firmware, and bench-test the finished controller against the instrument's requirements.

Build and align an optical or mechanical instrument on an optical table: bolt posts, mounts and cage components to a breadboard; install lasers, lenses, mirrors, dichroics, objective and camera for a single-molecule TIRF scope or optical trap; align the beam path, focus, and validate performance on a calibration sample.

instances.label: Single-particle cryo-EM data collection session in an institutional EM facility: clipped autogrids are transferred under LN2 into an autoloader cassette and loaded into a 200/300 kV cryo-TEM; atlases are taken, grids screened for ice/particle quality, squares and holes selected, and 24-72 h of movie acquisition run, with on-the-fly processing confirming the dataset is usable.

Cryo-EM specimen preparation at the bench: glow-discharge grids, apply a few microlitres of purified protein/complex, blot or wick, plunge-freeze into liquid ethane, and store vitrified grids under liquid nitrogen (clipping into autogrids), iterating over concentration, buffer, detergent and blot conditions to get suitable ice.

Protein crystallization and crystal harvesting in a lab: set up nanolitre sitting-drop screens in 96-well plates, incubate and inspect plates by imaging over days to weeks, judge hits, optionally soak ligands/fragments, then harvest crystals into loops/pins, cryoprotect, cryocool in LN2 and load pins into pucks for the beamline.

X-ray diffraction data collection in a synchrotron MX experimental hutch (or in-house diffractometer cabinet): pucks placed in the beamline dewar, samples mounted on the goniometer by the sample changer, crystal located and centred in the beam, diffraction characterized, strategy chosen, datasets collected and auto-processed to scaled intensities / an initial structure.

In-situ cryo-electron tomography: cells vitrified on grids, cryo-FIB milling of lamellae in a cryo-FIB/SEM, transfer of the shuttle/grids to the cryo-TEM, lamella detection and tilt-series acquisition, then tomogram reconstruction and subtomogram averaging of macromolecules in the cell.

tasks.label: Study the chemistry of living processes, such as cell development, breathing and digestion, or living energy changes, such as growth, aging, or death.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mammalian cell-culture study of cell development/growth in an academic or biotech lab: thawing and maintaining cell lines or iPSCs in a biosafety cabinet and incubator, feeding/passaging on a schedule, applying growth factors, nutrients or drug treatments, then running plate-based readouts (viability, proliferation, differentiation/pigmentation, reporter, live-cell imaging) and interpreting the result.

In vitro biochemical study of a metabolic or energy-transducing pathway: preparing buffers and substrates, purifying or lysing to obtain enzyme/protein, running kinetics or activity assays (spectrophotometer, fluorimeter, oxygen/ATP assays) across concentration series in cuvettes or microplates, and fitting the data.

Microbial or yeast study of metabolism and growth: inoculating cultures, varying media/nutrient or gene-knockout conditions in flasks, microplates or bioreactors, tracking growth curves and product/metabolite titers, and iterating conditions to test hypotheses about pathway chemistry.

Molecular readouts of the same living processes: extracting protein/RNA/DNA from cells or tissue, then running Western blots, qPCR, ELISA or sequencing library prep to quantify signaling, senescence/aging or metabolic markers, with quantification and statistics.

Analytical profiling of biological samples: extracting metabolites/lipids/peptides from plasma, cells or tissue, preparing plates or vials, queueing LC-MS/GC-MS or NMR runs, then processing spectra to quantify metabolic changes with aging, diet or drug treatment.

Whole-animal in vivo study of digestion, growth or aging (mice or rats in a vivarium): dosing or diet administration, weighing and monitoring animals, serial blood collection, then euthanasia, dissection and harvest of organs/tissues for downstream biochemical analysis.

tasks.label: Study the mutations in organisms that lead to cancer or other diseases.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cancer/disease genomics run: tumor biopsies, patient blood, or cell-line pellets arrive in a university/pharma genomics lab; the scientist extracts DNA/RNA, QCs it, builds NGS libraries (whole-genome, exome or targeted panel), loads the sequencer, and calls candidate somatic/germline mutations. Plated, barcoded samples; standard kits and liquid handlers.

Functional test of candidate mutations in cells: CRISPR knock-in/knockout or site-directed mutagenesis to install the variant in a cell line, clonal expansion and cell culture over days-weeks, then phenotypic and biochemical assays (viability, high-content imaging, reporter, western/transcriptomic readout) comparing mutant to wild type in a BSL-2 tissue-culture room.

Biophysical/structural characterization of a mutant protein: clone and express wild-type and mutant constructs in E. coli or insect/mammalian cells, purify by chromatography, then measure stability, activity or binding (DSF, ITC/SPR, enzyme kinetics) and/or determine structure by crystallography or cryo-EM to explain how the mutation alters the protein.

In vivo and primary-tissue work: maintain and genotype a genetically engineered or xenograft mouse cancer colony in the vivarium, monitor and measure tumors, perform necropsy and tissue dissection, then process fresh/FFPE tissue for histology, IHC and nucleic-acid extraction; or dissect and microdissect fresh human surgical specimens.

Desk-based mutation study: mining cohort variant databases (TCGA, COSMIC, gnomAD, ClinVar), running variant-effect prediction, structural modeling or molecular dynamics on a workstation, statistical analysis of prior sequencing data, and writing up interpretation of which mutations drive disease.

tasks.label: Research the chemical effects of substances, such as drugs, serums, hormones, or food, on tissues or vital processes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cell-based dose–response experiment: cultured human/rodent cell lines (or engineered reporter cells, spheroids/organoids) are seeded in 96/384-well plates in an institutional research lab, treated with a compound, drug, hormone or nutrient across a concentration series, incubated, and read out on a plate reader or high-content imager for viability, reporter signal or morphology.

Target-level biochemical/biophysical assay: purified enzyme, receptor or protein is combined with a test substance in plates or on a biosensor to measure inhibition, binding affinity, IC50/Kd or kinetics; includes counter-screens and hit confirmation in a standard lab or screening facility.

Molecular/analytical characterization of treated samples: lysing treated cells, extracting protein/RNA/metabolites, and running Western blot, qPCR/RNA-seq library prep, ELISA or LC-MS to quantify how the substance changed signaling, gene expression or metabolite levels.

Ex vivo primary tissue work: harvesting or receiving fresh tissue (rodent organs, surgical specimens), dissecting and preparing slices, homogenates or primary cells, applying the substance (organ bath, slice electrophysiology, perfusion), then fixing, sectioning and staining tissue for analysis.

In vivo study in a vivarium: dosing rodents with a drug, serum, hormone or dietary substance, observing and weighing animals, collecting blood/urine at timed intervals, then necropsy and harvest of target tissues for downstream assay.

tasks.label: Research transformations of substances in cells, using atomic isotopes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine 13C (or 15N/2H) stable-isotope tracer experiment in cultured mammalian cell lines: seed plates/dishes, grow to target confluence, swap to tracer-labeled medium, incubate for a timed labeling period, aspirate/wash and quench metabolism cold, extract intracellular metabolites, spin/dry/resuspend, inject on LC-MS, and compute mass-isotopologue distributions. Standard BSL-2 academic or pharma wet lab, established protocol.

13C labeling experiment in microbial cultures (E. coli, yeast, C. glutamicum) for metabolic flux analysis: cultivation in shake flasks or microbioreactor plates on labeled substrate, timed sampling, rapid quenching/extraction, GC-MS/LC-MS or NMR measurement of labeling patterns, and flux estimation. Bioprocess/metabolic-engineering lab.

Radioisotope tracer assay of cellular transformation (35S-methionine pulse-chase, 3H-thymidine or 3H-substrate incorporation, 14C-substrate oxidation, 32P/33P labeling): dispense radiolabeled medium onto cells in plates, incubate, harvest/precipitate or capture product, and read by scintillation counting or phosphorimaging, in a radiation-licensed lab with shielding, surveys and radioactive-waste segregation.

Production and measurement of isotope-enriched biomolecules for structural/quantitative work: transform and grow E. coli (or label cells by SILAC) in 15N/13C minimal or labeled medium, harvest, lyse, purify the labeled protein by chromatography, concentrate and buffer-exchange, then acquire NMR or MS spectra to follow labeling/exchange.

In vivo or ex vivo tracer study: catheterize/infuse or gavage 13C- or 2H-labeled substrate into mice (or dose a human subject), take timed blood samples, euthanize and rapidly dissect and freeze-clamp multiple tissues, then extract and analyze labeled metabolites. Vivarium or clinical research unit with live-animal/subject handling.

Exploratory method development with isotopes on non-standard preparations: new tracer workflow for organoids, primary tissue slices, isolated organelles, mixed microbial communities or plant tissue; assembling custom labeling chambers or perfusion rigs, improvising quench timing, troubleshooting unexpected artifacts, iterating on protocol design.

tasks.label: Develop or execute tests to detect diseases, genetic disorders, or other abnormalities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine high-throughput execution of established plate/tube-based detection assays (qPCR panels, ELISA/immunoassays, pathogen or biomarker panels) on batches of banked or clinical specimens in a research or clinical lab: barcoded primary tubes, kit reagents, controls and calibrators, plate reader/analyzer readout, QC review.

Nucleic-acid extraction from blood/saliva/tissue followed by NGS library preparation, pooling, and a sequencing run to detect genetic disorders (panel, exome, or genome), including QC metrics and re-prep of failed libraries, in a genomics lab.

Execution of standardized protein- or tissue-level tests on prepared specimens to detect abnormalities: western/immunoblot of lysates, electrophoretic separation, enzyme-activity assays, immunostained tissue sections, run against controls in a lab.

Optimization and validation of a detection assay on an established platform: antibody/primer titration, buffer and cycling-condition sweeps, DOE/iterative parameter search, running validation panels of known positives and negatives to characterize sensitivity and specificity.

Non-routine bench work and de-novo test development: one-off protocols on unusual specimens with improvised labware, troubleshooting unexpected failures, plus conceiving a new test (biomarker/modality choice, novel reagents, judging what evidence establishes detection) and writing it up.

Specialized biophysical or instrumental measurement to detect functional/metabolic abnormalities: automated electrophysiology on cells expressing variant channels, LC-MS/MS metabolite panels on patient specimens, binding/kinetic characterization, in an instrument lab.

tasks.label: Develop or test new drugs or medications intended for commercial distribution.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Run a screening campaign against a validated drug target in a pharma/biotech discovery lab: prepare assay reagents and compound plates, dispense nanoliter-microliter volumes into 384/1536-well plates, incubate, read (fluorescence/luminescence/imaging), QC plates and confirm hits in dose-response. Standard microplate labware, institution-controlled lab.

Medicinal-chemistry make step: synthesize a series of new analogs of a lead compound (weigh/dispense reagents and solvents, run reactions under inert/heated conditions in a fume hood, monitor by LC-MS, work up, purify by flash or prep-HPLC, confirm structure/purity by NMR/LC-MS) and deliver assay-ready material.

Cell-based potency, mechanism and cytotoxicity testing requiring aseptic mammalian cell culture: thaw/passage cells in a biosafety cabinet, count and seed plates, dose with the candidate compound over several days with media changes, then run readouts (high-content imaging, reporter assays, flow cytometry).

Analytical, biophysical and DMPK characterization of a candidate: target-binding measurements (SPR, thermal shift), solubility/stability and formulation testing, and bioanalysis of plasma or tissue samples (protein precipitation/SPE sample prep, LC-MS/MS quantitation) in an institution-controlled analytical lab.

In vivo preclinical testing in a vivarium: prepare dose formulations, handle and dose rodents (oral gavage, IP/IV), observe and weigh animals, collect serial blood samples and terminal tissues, and process samples - animals of varying temperament, IACUC-controlled animal facility.

tasks.label: Isolate, analyze, or synthesize vitamins, hormones, allergens, minerals, or enzymes and determine their effects on body functions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Recombinant expression and purification of an enzyme, hormone or binding protein for downstream study: grow/induce E. coli or mammalian cultures, harvest and lyse cells, clarify, run affinity/ion-exchange/size-exclusion chromatography, check fractions by SDS-PAGE, concentrate, buffer-exchange, quantify and freeze aliquots. Academic or industry biochemistry lab, standard benches, cold room, shared FPLC and centrifuges.

Quantitative analysis of a vitamin, hormone, allergen-specific antibody, mineral or metabolite in biological samples (serum, plasma, tissue homogenate, cell lysate, food or plant extract): sample extraction/digestion/precipitation, standard curve and QC preparation, ELISA/immunoassay, LC-MS/MS or ICP-MS run, integration and concentration calculation. Research or core analytical lab.

Enzyme or receptor characterization and screening: set up microplate kinetic or binding assays (substrate titrations, Km/Vmax, IC50/Kd), dispense compounds or ligands, incubate, read absorbance/fluorescence/luminescence, fit curves, confirm hits. Microplate-based work at a bench with plate reader and multichannel or handheld pipettes.

Synthesis of a biochemical entity: solid-phase peptide or oligonucleotide synthesis, a labeled substrate, vitamin/steroid analog, or a bioconjugate; includes cleavage/deprotection, preparative HPLC purification, MS/NMR confirmation of identity and purity, lyophilization. Synthetic bench with fume hood, synthesizer, prep HPLC.

Cell- or tissue-based functional testing of the isolated/synthesized substance: culture and plate cells (or prepare primary cells/organoids/tissue slices), dose with hormone/vitamin/enzyme across concentrations and times, then measure a physiological readout (signaling western/ELISA, reporter, qPCR, viability, imaging, electrophysiology). Tissue-culture room with biosafety cabinets and incubators.

In vivo or ex vivo determination of effects on body functions: dose rodents (gavage, injection, diet) or perfuse an isolated organ, monitor physiology, take serial blood samples, euthanize and dissect tissues, then process samples for downstream assay. Institutional vivarium and animal procedure room under IACUC protocol.

tasks.label: Examine the molecular or chemical aspects of immune system functioning.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plate-based immunoassay in a university or biotech research lab: run ELISA or multiplex cytokine/antibody panels on serum, plasma or culture supernatant — dilution series, coating/blocking, timed incubations, plate washing, substrate development, plate reading, standard-curve fitting and reporting of concentrations.

Molecular readouts of immune genes and proteins: lysate prep, SDS-PAGE/western blot of signaling proteins (e.g., NF-kB, STAT phosphorylation), RNA extraction, qPCR panels, or sequencing library prep for immune transcriptome/repertoire, run on standard bench instruments in a shared lab.

Protein biochemistry/biophysics of immune molecules: express and purify antibodies, cytokines or immune receptors; measure binding kinetics/affinity by SPR or BLI; determine or refine structures by crystallography or cryo-EM at a core facility or synchrotron.

Animal and primary-tissue immunology in a vivarium/procedure room: immunize or challenge mice, bleed, euthanize and dissect spleen/lymph nodes, prepare single-cell suspensions, fix tissue and prepare sections for immunohistochemistry.

Bespoke biophysical measurement on immune cells: assemble or reconfigure a custom rig (single-molecule force spectroscopy on TCR-pMHC, TIRF/live-cell imaging of the immune synapse, patch-clamp or microfluidic device), troubleshoot a non-standard protocol, and acquire data on samples that behave unpredictably.

tasks.label: Research how characteristics of plants or animals are carried through successive generations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wet-lab molecular/cellular genetics in a university or company biochemistry lab: extract DNA/RNA from parent and progeny material (leaf punches, tail clips, cultured cells), set up PCR/qPCR genotyping plates, run gel/QC, build NGS libraries and sequence, and run yeast/bacterial/mammalian cultures, transformations and CRISPR edits to test how alleles and their phenotypes are transmitted. Shared benches, standard SBS labware, other researchers present.

Invertebrate/fish model-organism genetics: maintain C. elegans, Drosophila or zebrafish lines in a worm/fly room, set up defined crosses, collect virgin females, score progeny under a stereoscope for markers and mutant phenotypes, and pick/transfer selected individuals to fresh plates or vials over successive generations.

Rodent colony genetics in an institutional vivarium: set up mating pairs from genotyped lines, monitor litters, wean and ear-tag pups, take tail/ear biopsies for genotyping, maintain pedigree records, and phenotype offspring across generations.

Greenhouse or growth-chamber generation advance and phenotyping of segregating plant families (F2s, RILs, mutant lines): keep line identity, water and fertilize, and repeatedly score traits (height, biomass, color, flowering time) on individually tracked plants generation after generation.

Making the crosses and collecting the materials by hand: emasculating and pollinating flowers of chosen parental lines in a greenhouse or field nursery, bagging and tagging each cross, harvesting and threshing seed plant-by-plant, and collecting tissue samples or specimens from field plots and natural populations.

Field nursery/plot phenotyping: traversing progeny rows in a breeding nursery or replicated field trial and recording stand counts, plant height, stem width and canopy traits row-by-row across seasons and generations, in weather, mud and variable canopy conditions.

instances.label: Producing a bulk drug substance batch in a GMP pilot plant / production suite: charging media and raw materials, running the bioreactor or synthesis reactor, harvest, chromatography/filtration purification, in-process sampling, and bulk fill of the purified substance. Specialty small-batch/individualized preparation for distribution: e.g., autologous cell-therapy doses or radiopharmaceutical dose dispensing into shielded syringes/vials, under short expiry pressure in a cleanroom or shielded hot-cell suite.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Analytical/bioanalytical method development in a pharma or CRO analytical lab: for a drug substance, impurity mix or chemical compound, develop and optimize an HPLC/UHPLC-MS assay (column, buffer, gradient, detection, sample prep), run specificity/forced-degradation and robustness checks, and deliver a documented, transferable method.

Formulation and storage-condition development for a drug or biologic in a formulation lab with stability chambers: screen excipients, buffers, pH and concentrations, prepare candidate formulations, stress them (temperature, agitation, freeze-thaw), measure solubility, viscosity, aggregation and potency, and select a formulation plus storage conditions.

Synthesis/process development for a compound or biologic in a synthetic chemistry lab or bioprocess development suite: iterate reaction, work-up, purification or fermentation/perfusion conditions, run the experiments, characterize products by chromatography/spectroscopy, and define a scalable processing route.

Bench-scale food or beverage processing/ingredient method development in a food science lab: vary ingredient ratios, salt/pH, heating, mixing and drying parameters, prepare samples, measure viscosity, turbidity, texture or foam, and converge on a processing recipe.

Pilot-plant scale-up and validation of a food process: run the pilot line (retort/extruder/dryer/filler), validate the thermal or preservation process, conduct microbial challenge and shelf-life storage studies, and run sensory panels before the method is accepted.

Biological method development in a cell-culture/biochemistry lab: develop protocols for using living cells, tissues or enzymes — culture and differentiation conditions, assay protocols, or cryopreservation/storage conditions — with iterative optimization judged by imaging and assay readouts.

tasks.label: Investigate the nature, composition, or expression of genes or research how genetic engineering can impact these processes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Construct building at the bench in an academic or biotech research lab: amplify/mutagenize a gene of interest, assemble it into an expression vector (Gibson/Golden Gate/restriction cloning), transform bacteria, pick colonies, miniprep and verify by sequencing; shared bench, mixed labware, multi-day.

Gene-expression profiling: extract RNA from banked samples or cultured cells, make cDNA, run RT-qPCR panels or build NGS libraries in 96-well plates, QC on a bioanalyzer, load a sequencer; protocolized, plate-based, moderate-to-high throughput.

Mammalian cell culture with CRISPR editing and functional readout: sterile hood work, passaging, transfection/nucleofection of guides, antibiotic selection and clonal expansion, then imaging/flow cytometry or reporter assay to score the effect of the edit on expression.

Express and characterize a gene product: induce recombinant protein in E. coli or a cell line, lyse, purify by affinity/size-exclusion chromatography, run SDS-PAGE, and measure activity/stability to relate sequence variants to function.

Sourcing biological material from model organisms: vivarium or greenhouse work — euthanize/dissect mice or harvest plant tissue, weigh and homogenize organ or tissue samples, preserve in RNAlater/liquid nitrogen for downstream expression analysis.

Novel assay and method development / troubleshooting: building a non-standard reporter or biophysical assay, improvising rigs and reagent handling, diagnosing failed reactions and contamination, adapting protocols to an unusual sample; ad hoc, changes day to day.

tasks.label: Produce pharmaceutically or industrially useful proteins, using recombinant DNA technology.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench-scale bacterial production of a single target protein for research/preclinical use in a university or biotech lab: gene cloned into an expression vector, transformed into E. coli, 0.5-2 L shake-flask or benchtop-fermenter culture, IPTG induction, centrifugal harvest, sonication/homogenization lysis, affinity plus size-exclusion chromatography on an FPLC, QC by SDS-PAGE/A280/MS, aliquoting and freezing of milligram quantities.

Mammalian transient expression of a therapeutic protein or antibody: plasmid prep, transfection of HEK293/Expi293 or CHO suspension cultures (30 mL-2 L) in shaker incubators, 4-7 day culture, clarification, Protein A or Ni affinity capture, buffer exchange/concentration, QC by SEC-HPLC and endotoxin testing, delivering milligrams of purified material.

High-throughput parallel production of a variant library or construct panel for screening: primer/fragment design, mutagenesis or DNA assembly, transformation or cell-free expression in 96/384-well format, small-scale expression, microscale (magnetic-bead or filter-plate) purification or clarified lysate, and activity/expression readouts feeding a design cycle.

Strain or cell-line and process development to make an industrially useful protein at scale: construct and screen production clones, run parallel benchtop bioreactors (250 mL-10 L) with feeding, induction and periodic sampling, measure titer and product quality, and select the production process.

Pilot- or manufacturing-scale production campaign in a bioprocess suite: 50-2,000 L single-use or stainless bioreactor run, harvest/clarification, capture and polish chromatography skids, ultrafiltration/diafiltration and formulation of recombinant protein under documented procedures with in-process sampling.

Difficult or novel target where the protocol must be invented: membrane proteins, toxic or insoluble products requiring inclusion-body solubilization and refolding, unusual hosts (baculovirus/insect, plant, yeast secretion), iterative hands-on troubleshooting of construct, host, media and buffer conditions until usable protein is obtained.

tasks.label: Isolate and maintain cultures of bacteria or other microorganisms in prescribed or developed media, controlling moisture, aeration, temperature, and nutrition.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Clinical/diagnostic microbiology lab: primary isolation from patient specimens (urine, liquid-based swabs, sputum, stool) — labeling plates, inoculating and streaking selective/enriched agar for isolated colonies, incubating at 35 °C under aerobic/CO2/anaerobic atmospheres with humidity control, then subculturing colonies to purity for ID/AST.

Academic/industrial research bench: picking colonies from mixed or transformant plates, inoculating broth in tubes/flasks/deep-well plates, overnight growth in shaking incubators (aeration, temperature), serial dilution and re-streaking, passaging into fresh prescribed or newly formulated media, all with aseptic technique at a bench or biosafety cabinet.

Maintenance of a strain/stock collection: periodic subculture of working stocks, purity checks, preparation of glycerol/cryovial stocks, deposit into -80 °C or LN2 storage with inventory tracking, and revival/re-streaking of archived strains on demand.

Fastidious or specialized organisms: strict anaerobes handled in an anaerobic chamber, mycobacteria/fungi with long slow incubations and humidity control, algae/phototrophs in illuminated culture vessels or photobioreactors — atmosphere, moisture and nutrient regimes tightly controlled.

Industrial/food/pharma QC and environmental microbiology lab: SOP-driven serial dilution and plating (spread, pour, spiral, membrane filtration) of product, water or environmental-monitoring samples, controlled incubation, colony enumeration, and subculture of presumptive isolates for confirmation.

tasks.label: Monitor and perform tests on water, food, and the environment to detect harmful microorganisms or to obtain information about sources of pollution, contamination, or infection.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine water microbiology in a utility or environmental testing lab: log in bottled samples, run membrane filtration or defined-substrate (Colilert/Quanti-Tray) tests for total coliforms/E. coli and heterotrophic plate counts, incubate, read and confirm, enter results and flag exceedances.

Food, beverage or ingredient QC testing in a plant or contract lab: weigh and homogenize sample, prepare serial dilutions, pour/spread or Petrifilm plate for indicator counts, set up enrichments and rapid PCR/immunoassay for Salmonella/Listeria, incubate, enumerate, confirm presumptives, report.

Scheduled viable air monitoring round in a pharmaceutical or food cleanroom: gown up, walk the mapped sampling points, run active air samplers and expose/retrieve settle plates, log locations and times, then incubate and enumerate the plates in the QC lab.

Surface and personnel environmental monitoring in a production facility (cleanroom, dairy, RTE food plant): contact plates and swabs of equipment, drains, floors, gloves and gowns, including investigational vector swabbing around a positive result, followed by enrichment/plating and identification of isolates.

Field sampling round at off-site outdoor locations: drive to streams, beaches, storm/wastewater outfalls, private wells or farm sites; collect aseptic grab samples in sterile bottles, take field readings and notes, maintain chain of custody and ice samples for return within holding time.

Continuous or in-situ monitoring of a source water body, reservoir or canal for harmful microorganisms (fecal indicators, cyanobacteria/HAB toxins): deploy and operate in-situ monitoring instrumentation, obtain repeated measurements over days to weeks, and report trends/alerts.
