tasks.label: Examine physiological, morphological, and cultural characteristics, using microscope, to identify and classify microorganisms in human, water, and food specimens.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital/clinical microbiology lab: working up incubated culture plates from human specimens (urine, screening swabs, wound, respiratory, blood-culture subcultures) - judging colony morphology, quantitation, hemolysis, chromogenic color and growth on selective media, then picking colonies for identification and classifying the organisms present.

Clinical lab: Gram-stained smear microscopy of human specimens - smearing and staining slides, then oil-immersion (1000x) reading of positive blood cultures, sputum, wound, body-fluid and CSF smears to classify cell morphology/arrangement, judge specimen adequacy (WBC/squamous cells) and describe mixed flora.

Clinical/reference parasitology: microscopic examination of stool concentrates and wet mounts (saline/iodine, trichrome, modified acid-fast) to detect, identify and classify protozoan cysts/trophozoites, helminth ova and coccidia in human specimens.

Clinical/reference mycology: KOH and calcofluor preps, lactophenol cotton-blue tease/tape mounts and slide cultures examined microscopically together with colony (cultural) characteristics to identify moulds and yeasts by conidiation, hyphal and reproductive-structure morphology.

Water/environmental microbiology lab: examining water samples and membrane filters - enumerating and identifying algae/cyanobacteria and protozoa by microscopy, and reading heterotrophic-plate-count/coliform membrane filters and chromogenic plates for colony morphology and confirmation.

Food/beverage QC microbiology lab: plating and reading enumeration and selective/chromogenic plates from food homogenates (aerobic counts, coliforms, yeast/mould, Listeria, Salmonella, E. coli), judging colony morphology against cluttered food-particle backgrounds, plus wet mounts/stains of spoilage organisms and confirmation of presumptive colonies.

instances.label: Setting up and running nucleic-acid amplification: assembling PCR/qPCR master mixes and template in tubes or 96-well plates at the bench of a research or clinical microbiology lab, sealing and spinning plates, loading the thermocycler/real-time cycler, running the program, and retrieving amplicons or curves. Electrophoresis and gel/blot imaging: casting or using precast agarose or polyacrylamide gels, pipetting 1-20 uL of sample and ladder into wells, assembling tank and buffer, running at set voltage, then imaging on a gel doc, or exposing a gel/blot to a storage-phosphor screen and scanning it on a phosphorimager. Chromatographic analysis (GC, HPLC/UPLC, LC-MS): extracting or derivatizing microbial cultures/supernatants (e.g., fatty-acid profiling for identification, metabolite or antibiotic quantitation), filling and capping autosampler vials, loading the autosampler tray, queueing the method, running the sequence, and integrating peaks. Shared instrument room in an institutional lab.

Flow cytometry / fluorescence-activated cell sorting: staining cell or microbial suspensions in tubes/plates, washing, loading the cytometer or sorter, running startup/QC and compensation, acquiring events, and for sorting, gating populations and collecting sorted cells into tubes or plates. Core-facility or lab instrument room.

Electron microscopy imaging session on already-prepared specimens: loading grids or stubs into the microscope (side-entry holder or autoloader cassette), aligning and tuning the column, finding areas of interest, and acquiring image sets or a multi-hour automated dataset on a TEM/SEM in a shared EM facility.

Prep-heavy or bespoke instrument work in non-standard formats: EM specimen preparation (fixation, resin embedding, trimming and ultrathin sectioning on an ultramicrotome, grid pickup and post-staining, negative staining of virus/bacteria grids), one-off rigs, odd sample vessels and instruments used a few times a year at the bench.

Prepares formulations and food matrices, inoculates spoilage/pathogen cocktails, holds samples across storage conditions, samples and enumerates at intervals over weeks, measures pH/water activity, revises the formulation, and issues a shelf-life/preservation recommendation.

Plate-based screening and optimization campaign inside the lab: candidate antimicrobial agents, preservative blends, or growth/recovery media conditions are screened in microtitre plates against defined panels of organisms using automated liquid handling and plate readers, with iterative rounds narrowing on the best-performing composition or condition set; deliverable is the identified/optimized composition plus the supporting growth-inhibition data.

Scale-up / in-plant trial of the new procedure at a production or pilot facility (fill-finish suite, cannery, cleanroom, CIP/SIP skid): placing biological indicators, coupons and data loggers in equipment, running trial cycles with plant staff, retrieving and culturing indicators, taking surface swabs and air samples, then revising the procedure to fit the equipment and line conditions.

sources.system: BacterAI (AI agent plus automated liquid-handling/plate platform)
sources.developer: Jensen Lab, University of Michigan / University of Illinois
sources.title: AI could run a million microbial experiments per year - Michigan Engineering News
sources.claim: BacterAI, an AI agent driving a laboratory robotic platform, autonomously designed and executed thousands of plate-based microbial growth experiments per day, changing the next day's experiments based on prior results, and derived the amino-acid requirements of two Streptococcus species with no prior data.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous closed-loop screening of medium composition for microbial growth. It uses the same objects and precision as a preservative/antimicrobial screening campaign (microtitre plates, defined media, live bacterial cultures, optical growth readouts) and the same iterative narrowing on a best-performing composition, so performance carries over to instance 3.

sources.system: BacterAI
sources.title: BacterAI maps microbial metabolism without prior knowledge | Nature Microbiology
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed report of BacterAI: the agent generated its own experiments on live streptococci and distilled the results into rules interpretable by scientists, i.e. a closed design-execute-analyse loop in microbiology.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: plate-based, live-culture, closed-loop optimization of growth conditions is the technical core of a preservative/medium screening campaign.

sources.system: Autonomous test-learn robotic cultivation platform
sources.developer: Kabisch lab, TU Darmstadt (Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology)
sources.title: Closing the loop: establishing an autonomous test-learn cycle to optimize induction of bacterial systems using a robotic platform
sources.claim: A robotic bacterial-cultivation platform was closed into an autonomous test-learn cycle that itself chose the next experimental parameters, autonomously optimizing inducer concentration for Bacillus subtilis and inducer/feed combinations for E. coli.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous optimization of culture conditions for live bacteria on a purpose-built robotic deck; the handling (plates/microbioreactors, media additions, growth readouts) and the closed-loop narrowing match a plate-based antimicrobial or medium screening campaign.

sources.system: Mobile robotic chemist (KUKA mobile manipulator)
sources.title: A mobile robotic chemist - Strathprints
sources.claim: A free-roaming mobile manipulator ran an autonomous 8-day formulation-optimization campaign (688 experiments, batched Bayesian search) inside an ordinary human chemistry laboratory, improving photocatalyst activity six-fold.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous formulation optimization in a human-standard lab. It bounds what is demonstrated at E2 — the campaign was chemistry with stable reagents and an in-line assay, with no aseptic technique, live-culture handling, incubation scheduling or colony enumeration, so it does not transfer to microbiological method development.

sources.system: Copan WASPLab / WASP DT with PhenoMATRIX
sources.title: WASPLab - Copan Diagnostics
sources.claim: Deployed clinical-microbiology total lab automation robotically plates specimens, streaks, incubates and images cultures on a conveyor track, but executes fixed validated workflows and leaves interpretation and result release to qualified human staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine culture processing in a microbiology lab. It shows deployed microbiology robots execute pre-validated procedures but do not devise or validate new ones, so it cannot substantiate completion of a development instance.

sources.system: Automated liquid handling robot for rapid lateral flow assay development
sources.developer: Academic group, Analytical and Bioanalytical Chemistry
sources.title: Automated liquid handling robot for rapid lateral flow assay development
sources.claim: A dedicated liquid-handling robot was built to run large optimization matrices for lateral-flow assay development (malaria, SARS-CoV-2, M. tuberculosis), but experimental designs, reagent choices and interpretation remain with the human developers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: detection-assay development. Cited only to characterise the state of the art — execution of human-designed optimization runs; autonomy over the development project is not established, so it cannot support a positive judgment for instance 1.

tasks.label: Conduct chemical analyses of substances such as acids, alcohols, and enzymes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Industrial/production QC lab (fermentation, food & beverage, biofuel, biopharma): quantify ethanol, organic acids, residual sugars or product titer in broth and product samples by HPLC/GC or an automated enzymatic/discrete analyzer. Samples arrive as capped tubes/vials with a worklist; calibration standards and controls are run; results reported to LIMS.

Research or biotech lab bench: enzyme activity and biochemical microplate assays (kinetic spectrophotometric enzyme assay, Bradford/BCA protein quantification, ELISA-type substrate assays) on cell lysates or culture supernatants - serial dilutions, timed reagent additions, wash steps, plate-reader read and curve fitting.

Clinical or diagnostic microbiology lab: enzymatic/biochemical characterization of isolates (colorimetric substrate panels, oxidase/catalase-type tests) and clinical chemistry measurement of enzymes and alcohols on patient specimens, run under a regulated SOP with QC materials and result review.

Academic or exploratory bench work in a shared lab: prepare reagents and buffers, weigh solids, adjust and measure pH, extract or derivatize metabolites from cultures, titrate acids, and run one-off spectrophotometric or chromatographic determinations using assorted glassware and shared instruments, with protocols that change between experiments.

Field or plant-floor work: collect grab samples at a wastewater plant, brewery/production floor, farm or environmental site and perform on-site chemical tests (pH, titratable acidity, residual analyte kits, portable meters) on uneven ground, in variable weather, around other people and traffic.

sources.system: Liverpool mobile robotic chemist (KUKA KMR iiwa)
sources.title: A mobile robotic chemist | Nature
sources.claim: A KUKA mobile robot autonomously operated analytical instruments in an ordinary wet-chemistry laboratory, running 688 experiments over 8 days of unattended 24/7 operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (photocatalyst screening) transfers: the robot performed the same physical acts this task requires - dispensing solids and liquids into vials, capping, and operating benchtop analytical instruments in a standard human wet lab.

sources.system: Autonomous mobile robots for exploratory synthetic chemistry (mobile robots + Chemspeed ISynth + UPLC-MS + benchtop NMR)
sources.developer: University of Liverpool (Dai, Vijayakrishnan, Cooper et al.)

sources.claim: Two mobile robots autonomously ran synthesis and product analysis using a shared UPLC-MS and benchtop NMR in a working university laboratory, choosing next steps from the analytical data.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (exploratory synthesis) transfers to chemical analysis: the analytical half of the workflow - sample handling into vials, LC-MS injection, NMR acquisition and data interpretation - is the same instrument work microbiologists do on broths and extracts.

sources.system: Liverpool mobile robotic chemist (2026 update)
sources.title: Self-driving labs are changing how chemists work - C&EN
sources.claim: Trade press review of self-driving labs reports the Liverpool mobile robot's data analysis matched a trained chemist's accuracy, and that by 2026 it synthesized acetaminophen, analyzed the product by UHPLC-MS and cleaned the reactor.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes worker-quality output for robot-run instrumental analysis in a normal laboratory, the quality bar this task requires.

sources.title: ambr 250 High Throughput Perfusion brochure (Sartorius)

sources.transferJustification: Related task (solubility screening) shares the physical acts of this task - gravimetric solid dispensing, solvent addition, vial handling and instrumental measurement - performed across stations in a normal laboratory.

sources.system: Unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) for water chemistry monitoring
sources.developer: Athens Water Supply and Sewerage Company (EYDAP) with research partners

sources.claim: Unmanned surface vehicles carrying water-quality sensor payloads were deployed by a water utility for routine monitoring of surface water bodies, supplementing periodic spot sampling followed by laboratory analysis.
sources.transferJustification: Closest field analogue: in-situ sensor measurement of water chemistry. It does not cover reagent-based analysis of acids, alcohols or enzymes, and the autonomy of the vehicle operations is not established.

tasks.label: Research use of bacteria and microorganisms to develop vitamins, antibiotics, amino acids, grain alcohol, sugars, and polymers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-throughput screening of engineered or mutagenized microbial strains (E. coli, C. glutamicum, yeast, Streptomyces) and of media/condition variants in 24-96 well plates in an industrial-biotech R&D lab: dispense media, inoculate from cell bank, incubate with shaking, track growth, assay product titer (amino acid, vitamin, ethanol, antibiotic activity), rank hits and pick winners for the next round.

Building the strains to be tested in a molecular biology lab: designing and assembling pathway/mutant DNA libraries, transforming host microbes, plating and picking colonies, purifying and sequence-verifying plasmids, banking verified clones as glycerol stocks.

Bench-scale fermentation runs to characterize promising strains: prepare and sterilize media, assemble/inoculate shake flasks and 0.25-5 L stirred bioreactors, control pH/DO/feeding, draw time-course samples, harvest broth, in a process-development lab.

Quantitative analysis of fermentation samples and product characterization: sample prep (dilution, centrifugation, filtration, extraction), HPLC/GC/LC-MS or plate-reader assays for the target vitamin, amino acid, sugar, alcohol, antibiotic potency or polymer property, plus data workup for the campaign report.

Exploratory, non-standard bench work: isolating and characterizing novel producer microbes from environmental samples, adapting protocols to fastidious or unfamiliar organisms, ad hoc microscopy and staining, diagnosing contamination or failed runs and improvising fixes at the bench.

Scale-up trials in a pilot plant: inoculum train preparation, sterile hose/filter connections to 50-2000 L fermenters, SIP/CIP oversight, manual aseptic sampling and inoculation transfers, downstream recovery trials on the pilot floor.

sources.system: BioAutomata on iBioFAB
sources.developer: Zhao lab, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
sources.title: Towards a fully automated algorithm driven platform for biosystems design | Nature Communications
sources.claim: BioAutomata, running on the Illinois Biological Foundry for Advanced ... () robotic platform, closed the full design-build-test-learn loop autonomously to optimize a lycopene biosynthetic pathway in E. coli: the scheduler pipetted parts, assembled plasmids by Golden Gate, cultured variants and quantified product, with a Bayesian algorithm choosing the next experiments.

sources.system: AI-powered autonomous enzyme engineering platform (iBioFAB + Thermo F5 robotic arm, Momentum scheduler)
sources.developer: Zhao lab, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
sources.title: A generalized platform for artificial intelligence-powered autonomous enzyme engineering | Nature Communications
sources.claim: A generalized autonomous protein/enzyme engineering platform on iBioFAB automated every wet-lab step of multi-round campaigns (mutagenesis PCR, DNA assembly, 96-well microbial transformation, plating, colony picking, plasmid purification, protein ... in microbes, and functional assays), integrated by a central robotic arm and a scheduler, over four rounds in four weeks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (enzyme variant engineering) uses the identical physical operations on the same microbial hosts and labware as strain construction for metabolite production: transformation, plating, colony picking, plasmid prep, culturing and product assay in 96-well format.

sources.system: Automated microbioreactor platform (BioLector-class microbioreactor + liquid handler + automated deep freezer)

sources.claim: An automated microbioreactor platform with an integrated automated deep-freezer performs autonomous strain phenotyping from cryo cell bank through cultivation to product assay, demonstrated with Corynebacterium glutamicum (the industrial amino-acid production host) secreting cutinase, including automated clean-in-place so consecutive experiments run without human interaction.

sources.system: Sartorius ambr 250 High Throughput
sources.title: Sartorius Ambr 250 - ABPDU (Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory)
sources.claim: The commercial Sartorius ambr 250 High Throughput system runs parallel 100-250 mL microbial fermentations with a fully automated liquid-handling robot and automated control of sampling, feeding and process parameters; it is installed and used in bioprocess development facilities such as LBNL's ABPDU.

sources.system: BioLector XT microbioreactor + Biomek i5 liquid handler (RoboLector-type integration)
sources.title: BioLector XT Microbioreactor & Biomek i5 Liquid Handler Integration
sources.claim: The commercial BioLector XT microbioreactor integrated with a Biomek i5 liquid handler executes inoculation, feeding/induction dosing and sampling of individual culture wells automatically, triggered by real-time online biomass, pH and dissolved-oxygen signals from the cultures.

sources.system: Robot Scientist Adam
sources.title: The automation of science - PubMed (Science 2009)
sources.claim: Robot Scientist Adam, a purpose-built integrated laboratory robotic system, autonomously generated hypotheses about yeast gene function, designed and executed the microbial growth experiments (media preparation, inoculation, incubation, optical-density measurement) and interpreted the results, which were later confirmed by manual experiments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (functional genomics of yeast) is executed with the same physical operations as applied-microbiology screening: automated media dispensing, inoculation of microbial cultures in microplates, incubation and growth/product readout in a purpose-built robotic lab.

sources.system: Robot Scientist Eve
sources.developer: Universities of Manchester, Aberystwyth and Cambridge
sources.title: AI 'scientist' finds that toothpaste ingredient may help fight drug-resistant malaria | EurekAlert!
sources.claim: Robot Scientist Eve automates hypothesis generation, execution of high-throughput compound screens against cultured cells/parasites using laboratory robotics, and interpretation; it was used to identify triclosan as an inhibitor of Plasmodium DHFR, an antimicrobial-drug discovery result.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (antiparasitic/antimicrobial compound screening) matches the antibiotic-development element of this task: robotic plate handling, dosing of microbial/parasite cultures and assay readout in a purpose-built screening cell.

sources.system: BD Kiestra TLA / Copan WASP-WASPLab
sources.title: Total Laboratory Automation for Rapid Detection and Identification of Microorganisms and Their Antimicrobial Resistance Profiles | Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology
sources.claim: Total laboratory automation systems for culture-based microbiology (BD Kiestra, Copan WASPLab) are commercially installed in routine clinical laboratories, where track-based robotics inoculate specimens onto culture plates, transport plates to automated incubators, and image colony growth at set intervals; hundreds of processors and dozens of full automation lines have been installed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (clinical culture processing) demonstrates production-reliability robotic handling of the same physical objects as research microbiology - agar plates, inoculation loops, incubators, colony imaging - on purpose-built conveyor track lines inside institutional labs.

sources.system: Robotic liquid-handling sample-preparation platforms for LC-MS bioanalysis
sources.developer: multiple vendors (e.g., Hamilton, Tecan, Agilent) as reviewed in LCGC
sources.title: Bioanalytical Analysis of Small-Molecule Drugs and Metabolites in Physiological Samples by LC-MS, Part 2: Sample Preparation | LCGC International
sources.claim: Fully automated robotic liquid-handling sample-preparation platforms feeding LC-MS quantification are routine in high-throughput analytical laboratories and can be programmed for hands-free sample preparation of biological matrices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (bioanalytical sample prep of plasma for LC-MS) uses the same labware, extraction/filtration steps and precision as preparing fermentation broth samples for HPLC/LC-MS quantification of amino acids, vitamins, alcohols or antibiotics.

sources.system: Mobile robotic chemist
sources.title: A mobile robotic chemist (Nature 2020) - Strathprints
sources.claim: A mobile robot with a manipulator operated autonomously for eight days in a chemistry laboratory, performing 688 experiments driven by a Bayesian search algorithm and using human-scale instruments - the closest evidence to robotic experimentation in an ordinary human-designed lab, but in synthetic chemistry rather than sterile microbiology.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only to bound the E2 question: it shows autonomous mobile experimentation in a human-scale lab for solid/liquid dispensing and analysis, but does not demonstrate aseptic microbial culture work, so it cannot substantiate completion of these microbiology instances at E2.

sources.system: Ginkgo Bioworks Foundry
sources.title: Ginkgo's Synthetic Biology platform - automated Foundry (IARPA capabilities profile)
sources.claim: Ginkgo Bioworks operates a large commercial automated foundry (>290,000 sq ft, BSL2) that runs standardized, heavily automated organism-engineering workflows at industrial scale; humans work alongside the automation, so end-to-end autonomy is not established.
sources.transferJustification: Context only for the commercial scale of purpose-built biofoundries; autonomy unclear, so not used to support any positive judgment.

emergingTasks.label: Perform tests on water, food, and the environment to detect harmful microorganisms or to obtain information about sources of pollution, contamination, or infection and interpret the results.
emergingTasks.status: Proposed for future data collection; not treated as established task evidence

roles.title: Zoologists and Wildlife Biologists
roles.description: Study the origins, behavior, diseases, genetics, and life processes of animals and wildlife. May specialize in wildlife research and management. May collect and analyze biological data to determine the environmental effects of present and potential use of land and water habitats.

tasks.label: Inventory or estimate plant and wildlife populations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Aerial count of large or colonial wildlife over open or winter-forested landscapes: flying planned transects/grids over a refuge, reservation, wetland or haul-out and counting ungulates (thermal), waterfowl, seabirds or pinnipeds to produce a density/abundance estimate for management.

Ground-based observer surveys on foot in forest, shrubland or wetland: breeding-bird point counts and aural species identification, amphibian call surveys, herp visual-encounter transects, pellet-group and track/sign transects, nest searches; done at dawn/dusk in variable weather off-trail.

Deploying, servicing and retrieving passive monitoring gear across a grid of remote sites: mounting camera traps and acoustic/bat recorders on trees and posts, setting hair snares or eDNA samplers, swapping cards and batteries, hiking or driving between scattered points, then compiling detections into an occupancy/abundance estimate.

Capture-based sampling and mark-recapture: setting and checking small-mammal trap grids, mist nets, bat nets, funnel/pitfall traps or nets and electrofishing runs; handling, measuring, marking/banding/tagging and releasing live animals, with permits and animal-welfare constraints.

Plant/vegetation inventory in habitat plots: fixed-radius or belt plots for tree counts, DBH and stem density, shrub canopy cover, and quadrat/line-intercept species composition used to characterize habitat and plant populations.

Fish and aquatic population surveys on large water bodies: running acoustic (hydroacoustic) abundance transects across a shelf, lake or bay and photographic/benthic visual census of fish and invertebrates over rugged bottom, producing an abundance index used in stock or population assessment.

sources.system: Thermal-infrared survey drones (MassDOT Aeronautics Division / Massachusetts DCR deer density survey)

tasks.label: Disseminate information by writing reports and scientific papers or journal articles, and by making presentations and giving talks for schools, clubs, interest groups and park interpretive programs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Develop, or make recommendations on, management systems and plans for wildlife populations and habitat, consulting with stakeholders and the public at large to explore options.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Study animals in their natural habitats, assessing effects of environment and industry on animals, interpreting findings and recommending alternative operating conditions for industry.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ground-based field survey/observation in terrestrial habitat: walking transects, point counts, nest/den/sign searches, behavioral observation and habitat plots on a proposed or operating industrial footprint (wind, solar, pipeline, timber, mining); off-trail terrain, brush, variable weather, cryptic species identification, data logged for an impact analysis.

Deploying, servicing and retrieving remote field instruments across dispersed sites reached by truck/ATV/on foot: mounting and aiming camera traps and acoustic recorders on trees/posts, swapping cards and batteries, setting telemetry receivers, hair snares and habitat/water samplers, seasonal retrieval.

Live capture, handling, marking and biological sampling of wild animals: mist nets, small-mammal or fish traps, electrofishing, darting/net-gunning; then measuring, banding/collaring/tagging, taking blood or tissue, and releasing the animal unharmed.

Radio/GPS telemetry work: relocating tagged individuals across a landscape with a handheld VHF antenna on foot or from a vehicle (occasionally aircraft), homing on dens/roosts/mortality signals, logging fixes to build home-range and disturbance-response data near industrial activity.

Large-area survey from a platform: aerial counts of ungulates, waterfowl or nesting colonies; vessel-based marine mammal, seabird or acoustic fish surveys over an offshore lease or fishery, producing abundance/distribution data used in industry impact assessment.

Monitoring animals at or around an operating industrial site controlled by the operator: protected-species observer duty during offshore construction/seismic work, eagle and raptor watch at a wind facility, or fish-passage monitoring at a hydro project, with real-time calls to shut down or alter operations.

sources.claim: The AutoFish System, a computer-operated automated marking trailer used by USFWS and Pacific Northwest agencies, sorts juvenile salmon by length, clips adipose fins and injects coded-wire tags at high rates with placement accuracy superior to manual crews.

sources.system: ANYmal legged robot forest inventory system (DigiForest)
sources.developer: Oxford Dynamic Robot Systems Group / ETH Zurich / ANYbotics
sources.title: Building Forest Inventories with Autonomous Legged Robots — System, Lessons, and Challenges Ahead
sources.claim: An ANYmal quadruped autonomously navigated natural forests in Finland, the UK ... seasons to build forest inventories up to 1 ha in under 30 minutes; the data collected are tree structure, not animal observations.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound terrestrial capability: the most advanced autonomous field robots in wild terrain collect tree-inventory data on short pre-planned missions, not wildlife detection, identification and counting, nor installation of field instruments.

sources.system: RangerBot / COTSbot AUV
sources.developer: Queensland University of Technology (Dunbabin et al.), with Google
sources.title: Eliminating invasive reef species - COTSbot and RangerBot | QUT Reef Research
sources.claim: RangerBot/COTSbot autonomous underwater vehicles run untethered reef missions with onboard real-time computer vision that identifies crown-of-thorns starfish and delivers lethal injections while monitoring reef health on the Great Barrier Reef.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-habitat detection and identification of a target animal species. Same environment class (natural reef taken as found) and same requirement to find and correctly identify animals in situ, supporting autonomous animal survey work in unstructured aquatic habitat.

tasks.label: Study characteristics of animals, such as origin, interrelationships, classification, life histories, diseases, development, genetics, and distribution.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hands-on field study of a wild population to document life history and distribution: setting and checking traps/nets/nest boxes on public or private land, capturing and restraining animals, taking morphometrics and blood/tissue samples, applying bands or collars, walking ground transects and point counts in forest, wetland or rangeland, in variable weather and terrain.

Broad-scale remote survey of a species' distribution and abundance over water or open landscape: running standardized acoustic/imaging/water-sampling transects across a defined survey area (e.g., an eastern Bering Sea fish survey, a colony or herd count, an eDNA time series) and delivering the survey observations the agency's assessment relies on.

Desk study: compiling field, harvest, museum and database records; running statistical, phylogenetic and species-distribution analyses; comparing results to the literature; interpreting what they say about classification, interrelationships or origin; and writing the findings up in an office.

Molecular laboratory work on collected samples in a university, agency or diagnostic lab: DNA/RNA extraction from tissue, scat, blood or swabs, PCR/barcoding, sequencing-library preparation and genotyping or disease assays (e.g., ELISA/qPCR panels), with samples arriving racked and labeled in plates or tubes.

Bench study of specimens and small model animals: sorting bulk trap or benthic samples, imaging and measuring specimens, keying and classifying them, preparing/reading slides, and phenotyping larvae or lab organisms for development and genetics studies, on a lab or museum bench.

Gross examination of animals for disease and development: necropsy of carcasses at a wildlife health lab or in the field, organ inspection and tissue collection (e.g., cervid lymph nodes at a check station), plus hands-on exams and observation of captive animals at a zoo, hatchery or vivarium.

sources.system: Saildrone USVs with Simrad EK80 echosounders (NOAA Alaska Fisheries Science Center pollock survey)

sources.title: Ocean-Going Robots Effective At Surveying Pollock | NOAA Fisheries
sources.claim: Three Saildrone uncrewed surface vehicles autonomously sailed the eastern Bering Sea pollock survey area for ~5 months in 2020, collecting acoustic data from which NOAA scientists derived a midwater pollock abundance estimate used in the stock assessment; the article also notes trawl verification samples cannot be gathered by the vehicles.

sources.system: Environmental Sample Processor (2G and 3G ESP) with long-range AUV

sources.system: WildWing autonomous UAS

sources.claim: WildWing is an autonomous, low-cost UAS that navigates to follow animal groups and record 4K behaviour video without manual piloting; it was validated in outdoor field deployments on zebras, giraffes and Przewalski's horses.

sources.system: DiversityScanner sorting robot
sources.developer: Wührl, Meier et al. (National University of Singapore / Museum für Naturkunde collaborators)
sources.title: DiversityScanner: Robotic discovery of small invertebrates with machine learning methods (bioRxiv; published in Molecular Ecology Resources 2022)
sources.claim: The DiversityScanner is a fully automated benchtop robot that detects, images, measures and moves individual invertebrates from a bulk sample into 96-well plates for DNA barcoding, with a CNN assigning specimens to family-level classes at 91.4% average precision.

sources.system: flowbot ONE liquid handler running automated Illumina DNA library preparation
sources.developer: Flow Robotics (validation by hospital/research genomics laboratory, Scientific Reports)
sources.title: Automating the Illumina DNA library preparation kit for whole genome sequencing applications on the flowbot ONE liquid handler robot
sources.claim: A flowbot ONE liquid-handling robot programmed to run Illumina DNA Prep produced sequencing libraries matching manual preparation in yield, assembly quality and 100% concordant typing results, cutting hands-on time from 125 to 25 minutes.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class as wildlife/animal genetics benchwork: nucleic-acid extraction and sequencing-library preparation on plated samples, identical labware, volumes and precision; the sample source (deer, fish, insect tissue) does not change the robotic manipulation.

sources.system: Robot Scientist Adam
sources.title: The Automation of Science | Science
sources.claim: Robot Scientist 'Adam' autonomously generated functional-genomics hypotheses about yeast and tested them with laboratory automation, selecting strains, inoculating microtitre plates and interpreting growth data; the conclusions were confirmed by manual experiments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous genetics study of a model organism. It shows an enclosed, purpose-built automated lab completing the whole loop from sample handling through assay to interpreted genetic conclusion, the same plate-based workflow zoologists use for animal genotyping and disease assays.

sources.system: VAST BioImager (Vertebrate Automated Screen Technology)
sources.title: Tools for automating the imaging of zebrafish larvae - PubMed

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling and imaging of live animals to score development and genotype-phenotype effects, which is the bench form of studying development and genetics in this task; objects (mm-scale vertebrate larvae) and precision match.

tasks.label: Organize and conduct experimental studies with live animals in controlled or natural surroundings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Laboratory experiment with captive small model animals (mice/rats, zebrafish, insects) in an institutional animal facility: set up apparatus in a procedure room, retrieve and handle animals from standard racked cages/tanks, run behavioral or physiological trials over days to weeks, score responses, monitor welfare, and produce a clean dataset.

Experiment on larger captive animals held in controlled housing at a research station, zoo, aquarium, aviary, or research barn/mesocosm: apply a treatment (diet, temperature, stimulus, enrichment, dosing) to identified individuals, measure intake/growth/behavior over weeks, and check animal condition daily.

Manipulative field experiment on free-ranging wildlife: hike/drive to sites in forest, grassland or wetland, install and maintain apparatus (feeders, puzzle/operant boxes, playback speakers, decoys, exclosures), deliver the treatment, observe or log responses over weeks in weather, and retrieve data and gear.

Field capture-and-instrument study of terrestrial wildlife: set and check live traps or mist nets, restrain the captured bird or mammal, take morphometrics and blood/tissue samples, band/ear-tag or fit a radio/GPS collar, release the animal, then relocate and monitor it over the season.

Aquatic experimental/mark-recapture study: capture fish by electrofishing, netting, or hatchery raceway crowding; anesthetize, measure, clip a fin, insert a PIT or coded-wire tag; release marked cohorts and monitor recaptures/detections in streams, lakes, or coastal waters.

sources.system: IntelliCage
sources.title: IntelliCage: the development and perspectives of a mouse- and user-friendly automated behavioral test system

sources.system: VAST BioImager (Vertebrate Automated Screening Technology)
sources.title: Tools for automating the imaging of zebrafish larvae - PubMed
sources.claim: The VAST BioImager robotically aspirates, loads, positions and rotates individual live zebrafish larvae in a capillary for imaging, replacing manual manipulation of each animal in screening experiments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling and precise positioning of live vertebrate subjects for experimental measurement - the physical animal-handling step of a laboratory experiment, with the same organisms and precision demands as zoological lab trials.

tasks.label: Analyze characteristics of animals to identify and classify them.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field survey identification: a wildlife biologist walking transects or working from a boat/vehicle identifies and classifies animals to species (and often age/sex) from plumage, pelage, size, silhouette, flight pattern, tracks, scat, or vocalizations, recording the determination on a datasheet or app.

Review of remotely collected media: the biologist sorts camera-trap photo sets, drone/aerial imagery, or bioacoustic recordings and assigns species, age class, or individual identity to each detection, resolving ambiguous images against reference material.

Laboratory or museum specimen work: examining a carcass, skull, pelt, feather, otolith, or preserved invertebrate under a dissecting scope, taking morphometric measurements with calipers, and working through a dichotomous key or comparing against a reference collection to assign a taxon.

Molecular and genomic identification: analyzing DNA barcode sequences, eDNA metabarcoding reads, or microsatellite/SNP genotypes against reference databases (e.g., BOLD, GenBank) to determine species, hybrid status, or population of origin, and writing up the determination.

Systematic/taxonomic analysis: building character matrices from morphological and molecular data, running phylogenetic analyses, comparing candidate material to type descriptions and literature, and formally classifying a population as a known taxon or describing/revising a taxon.

tasks.label: Prepare collections of preserved specimens or microscopic slides for species identification and study of development or disease.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Paraffin histology slide sets from wildlife or fish tissues (gonads for maturity/development staging, organs for disease work): formalin-fixed tissue trimmed into cassettes, dehydrated/infiltrated, embedded and oriented in paraffin, sectioned on a microtome, floated and mounted on labeled slides, H&E-stained and coverslipped, in an agency or university lab.

Blood smear and liquid-fixed cytology/imprint slides for hemoparasite and pathogen screening: blood from captured or necropsied animals spread, air-dried, fixed, Giemsa/Wright-stained, labeled and archived as a reference slide set in an institutional or field-station lab.

Vertebrate voucher specimens for a research collection: skinning a bird or small mammal, cleaning and stuffing a study skin, arranging and drying it, cleaning the skull/skeleton, attaching field tags and entering catalog data, in a museum prep lab.

Fluid-preserved whole specimens (fish, larvae, amphibians, reptiles, endoparasites): formalin fixation, water rinse, graded transfer to ethanol, placing specimens with printed tags into jars/vials, topping off, sealing, shelving and cataloging into the wet collection.

Hand-made mounts for identification or diagnosis prepared under a stereomicroscope: parasite/mite/nematode whole mounts cleared and mounted in medium with a coverslip, fecal flotation and wet mounts, hair and plant-fragment microhistology reference slides, and otolith/scale/tooth aging preparations (embedded, sawn or sectioned, polished, mounted).

Insect and other invertebrate collection preparation: sorting bulk Malaise/pitfall/plankton samples under a scope, pinning, pointing or spreading specimens, mounting micro-invertebrates, and attaching locality/determination labels for a curated collection.

sources.transferJustification: Cited as the state of the art for robotic handling of pinned entomological specimens; it demonstrates perception only, so it cannot support completion of pinning/mounting work.

tasks.label: Collect and dissect animal specimens and examine specimens under microscope.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field collection of vertebrate specimens: setting and checking Sherman/pitfall traps, mist nets, minnow traps or electrofishing gear at remote field sites; extracting, handling, identifying and measuring captured animals; euthanizing/preserving voucher specimens or taking tissue samples; also retrieving carcasses. Variable terrain, weather, vegetation, live struggling animals.

Water-column plankton / micro-organism sampling at a coastal station, dock or from a small vessel: taking water or net samples and then enumerating and identifying the small organisms in them microscopically to produce counts by taxon.

Gross necropsy / dissection of a vertebrate specimen (bird, fish, small mammal) on a lab bench or necropsy table: opening the carcass, examining and removing organs, assessing lesions, determining sex, age and reproductive condition, collecting labelled tissue/stomach samples and recording findings.

High-volume standardized micro-dissection of many same-species small specimens in a lab — e.g. removing heads/salivary glands or midguts from hundreds of insect vectors for pathogen or parasite screening, one repeated cut per specimen.

Varied fine dissection under a stereomicroscope with forceps and micro-scissors: extracting otoliths from fish of assorted sizes, staging gonads, recovering parasites from host tissue, sorting stomach contents, dissecting invertebrate genitalia for identification.

Routine microscopic examination of prepared material in an institutional lab: scanning slide-mounted tissue sections, blood smears, fecal flotations, or fixed sample aliquots, and counting/classifying the organisms or cells present to produce a recorded result.

A zoologist's routine microscopy of parasite or cell preparations involves the same objects (glass-slide preparations, eggs/cysts at 10-40x), the same stage/focus precision, and the same lab bench setting.

sources.claim: A collaborative robot arm was integrated with a stainer, coverslipper and whole-slide scanner to run the slide-handling steps of a pathology laboratory workflow autonomously, moving slides and magazines between benchtop instruments as a technician would.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the material handling around microscope examination in a human-scale laboratory (picking up slides and magazines, loading instruments), showing the surrounding steps of slide microscopy can be done by a robot in an ordinary lab rather than only inside a closed instrument.

instances.label: Routine nucleic acid extraction/purification in an academic or industry molecular biology lab: 8–96 cultured-cell, blood, or tissue samples processed with a commercial spin-column or magnetic-bead kit (lyse, bind, wash, elute), then quantified and stored. Standard tubes/plates, standard reagents, kit protocol followed as written.

PCR/qPCR reaction setup followed by agarose gel electrophoresis for product check or genotyping: pour/handle a gel, load 10–30 microliter-scale samples plus a ladder, run, image, and read sizes/integrity; occasionally excise a band for size selection or gel purification.

Molecular cloning run: restriction digest or Gibson/Golden-Gate assembly, ligation, transformation of competent E. coli, plating and overnight growth, picking colonies into culture, plasmid miniprep, and verification by digest or sequencing.

DNA sequencing work: NGS library preparation (fragmentation, adapter ligation, indexing, bead cleanup), library QC and normalization/pooling, loading and running the sequencer; or Sanger reaction setup and capillary run/submission.

Non-routine bench work in the same lab: limited or precious primary material (dissected tissue, sorted or single cells, organoids, clinical biopsies), in-house or newly adapted protocols not available as automation kits, odd labware and improvised steps, plus troubleshooting and re-running failed preparations.

Non-routine work: developing or troubleshooting a new assay, dissecting primary tissue and handling organoids, microinjection/patch-clamp/electroporation of delicate samples, building one-off setups, and improvising when a protocol fails. instances.label: Setting up and running PCR/qPCR: pipetting master mix and template into tubes/plates at the bench in a university or biotech molecular biology lab, sealing and spinning the plate, loading the block of a benchtop thermocycler/qPCR instrument, programming or selecting the cycling protocol, starting the run, and retrieving plate and amplification data.

Electrophoresis: casting or unwrapping an agarose or SDS-PAGE gel, filling the tank with buffer, pipetting 1-20 uL samples and ladder into wells, connecting leads and setting voltage/time, monitoring dye front, then transferring the gel/blot to a gel doc, phosphorimager or scanner and capturing the image.

Chromatography: preparing and capping sample vials, placing them in the autosampler tray of an HPLC/UPLC, FPLC or GC (or a coupled LC-MS), selecting the method and column, purging/equilibrating, starting the sequence, watching pressure and chromatogram traces during the run, and collecting fractions or exporting integrated results.

Flow cytometry / FACS: bringing stained cell suspensions in tubes or plates to a benchtop analyzer or cell sorter in a lab or shared core facility, loading samples, running compensation and setting gates, acquiring events or sorting target populations into collection tubes/plates, and unloading the sorted output.

Readout instruments: loading microplates, cuvettes, blots, or storage-phosphor screens into plate readers, spectrophotometers, phosphorimagers/laser scanners or imaging systems in the lab, selecting the read protocol (absorbance/fluorescence/luminescence/scan), running it, and retrieving the plate and data file.

Hands-on instrument upkeep and troubleshooting: preparing and degassing mobile phases and buffers, swapping HPLC columns, guard cartridges and lamps, priming/purging pumps and fixing leaks, cleaning cytometer fluidics and clearing a clogged sort nozzle, replacing thermocycler seals, running calibration beads/standards and QC checks, and logging maintenance.

instances.label: A new lot or new vendor of a critical reagent arrives (primary antibody, enzyme/master mix, kit, serum or media). The biologist runs a side-by-side functional test against the current reference lot on standard bench instruments (qPCR/thermocycler, plate reader, western/ELISA, or a cell-growth comparison), compares the data to acceptance criteria, and releases or rejects the lot for lab use.

A candidate consumable for pipetting/plate workflows is trialed (new filter-tip brand, microplate type, tube, plate seal). The biologist checks that it seats on the pipettes/liquid-handler deck and fits the reader/cycler, then runs a small dispense-performance check (volume accuracy/precision, no leaks or clogs) before switching the lab over.

Miscellaneous new supplies and bench hardware arrive (racks, culture flasks, cryovials, bottle-top filters, tubing, magnetic stands, gloves). The biologist unpacks them and does a hands-on check that they physically fit the lab's centrifuges, incubators, racks and instruments and handle acceptably, then approves stocking them.

A new benchtop instrument is delivered (thermocycler, plate reader, microcentrifuge, microscope camera, set of pipettes). The biologist unpacks and sites it on the bench, connects power/data, installs software and drivers, runs the manufacturer's self-test/calibration plus a lab-specific test sample, and accepts, requests service, or returns it.

A major or shared instrument/automation platform is evaluated (confocal microscope, flow cytometer, sequencer, liquid-handling platform) at a vendor demo or on-site trial using the lab's own samples, together with a facility-fit check of bench/room space, power, vibration, venting and software integration, ending in a written recommendation.

Protein biochemistry on complexes: recombinant expression in bacteria/insect/mammalian cells, lysis and chromatographic purification, co-IP/pull-down of protein complexes, western blots and binding/interaction assays (BLI/SPR), plus sample prep for structural work (crystallization trays, cryo-EM grid vitrification).

Model-organism experiments in a vivarium/organism facility: mouse colony breeding and weaning, tail/ear biopsy collection and genotyping, treatments, then euthanasia, dissection and tissue harvest for expression analysis; or fly/zebrafish/worm husbandry, crosses, embryo microinjection and phenotype scoring.

Microbial/yeast systems-biology campaign to map gene function and metabolic networks: strain construction and transformation, plating and microplate growth/metabolite screens with defined media, plate-reader phenotyping, and iterative rounds in which results drive the next set of gene-condition combinations.

instances.label: Clinical/medical geneticist reviews exome or genome sequencing output plus family pedigree and phenotype notes for a patient with a suspected inherited disorder, determines which variant(s) are causal for the trait/condition, and outlines approaches for modifying its expression (e.g., candidacy for gene-replacement or ASO therapy, carrier/reproductive options). Output is an interpretation and a written plan.

Academic molecular geneticist working in a model organism (mouse, zebrafish, Drosophila, Arabidopsis, yeast) interprets mapping, knockout, RNA-seq and complementation data to pin down which loci/alleles control a specific phenotype, then designs a CRISPR/base-editing or transgene strategy (guide choice, donor template, allele series) to alter or create the trait. Output is a conclusion plus an experimental design/protocol.

Plant or livestock breeding geneticist analyzes QTL/GWAS marker-trait association results from multi-location trial and genotyping data to identify determinants of yield, disease resistance or milk trait, and devises an introgression scheme: marker-assisted or genomic selection plan, cross design, or gene-edit/transgene target list. Output is a written breeding/edit strategy.

Industrial microbial or cell-line strain-engineering geneticist mines genotype–phenotype data from strain libraries and screens to identify the genetic determinants of a production phenotype (titer, tolerance, growth) and specifies the next round of edit designs (promoter swaps, knockouts, pathway insertions) to produce the new trait. Output is a design specification handed to a foundry or bench team.

Population/statistical geneticist analyzes biobank or cohort data (GWAS, heritability partitioning, fine-mapping, Mendelian randomization) to identify determinants of a complex inherited trait and proposes routes for altering trait outcomes (target genes for modulation, polygenic screening approaches). Output is statistical findings and a proposed method, written up in a report or manuscript.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine nucleic acid extraction in an academic/biotech research lab: 8-48 samples (whole blood, saliva, cultured cells, bacterial pellets) lysed, purified by spin column or magnetic bead, eluted, quantified on a spectrophotometer/fluorometer, then labeled and frozen. Standard labware, benchtop centrifuges, kit reagents.

PCR/qPCR set-up and run in a research lab: calculating and pipetting master mix, primers and template into 96-well plates or strip tubes (microlitre volumes), sealing, loading a thermal cycler, running the program, and reviewing amplification/melt curves or products, with no-template and positive controls.

Agarose gel electrophoresis to check PCR products, restriction digests or genotyping bands: pouring/obtaining a gel, loading 5-20 uL samples plus ladder into wells, running the rig, imaging on a transilluminator, sizing and interpreting bands, sometimes excising a band for gel purification.

Clinical/CLIA molecular diagnostic testing on validated platforms: batches of accessioned patient specimens (swabs, EDTA blood, plasma) taken through extraction plus real-time PCR to a reportable result with QC/controls, on a high-throughput molecular analyser in a hospital or reference laboratory.

DNA extraction from difficult or non-standard specimens: FFPE curls, solid tissue, plant/insect material, buccal swabs or degraded forensic trace evidence, requiring dissection/homogenization, proteinase K digestion, extended lysis and clean-up, followed by yield/quality checks.

Southern blot analysis (e.g., repeat-expansion or rearrangement sizing): restriction digest of genomic DNA, long agarose gel run, depurination/denaturation soaks, capillary or vacuum transfer to a nylon membrane, UV crosslinking, overnight probe hybridization, stringency washes and chemiluminescent/radiographic detection over 2-4 days.

instances.label: Research genetics lab: improving an existing plate-format molecular technique (PCR/qPCR conditions, cloning or DNA-assembly reactions, library-prep or transfection/reaction chemistry). Worker runs iterative condition-testing experiments in tubes/microplates with standard reagents and thermocyclers, reads out yield/specificity/efficiency, converges on and writes up an improved protocol.

Clinical/diagnostic molecular genetics or cytogenetics lab: incorporating a new diagnostic procedure (new NGS panel, added genes, new chemistry or CNV method) under CLIA/CAP. Worker designs the validation, runs reference materials and banked patient specimens through the whole workflow, establishes accuracy/precision/reportable range and QC thresholds, writes the SOP and validation summary for director sign-off.

Adapting a genetic technique to a difficult or novel specimen type: FFPE or degraded tissue, single-cell/nuclei prep from a new tissue, blood spots, plant or non-model animal material. Involves hands-on specimen assessment, dissection/homogenization, variable input quality, and iterative troubleshooting before a protocol is fixed.

Bringing a new instrument or platform on line and folding it into lab workflow (long-read sequencer, digital PCR, optical genome mapping, automated extractor): siting and setup, calibration and verification runs with known samples, adjusting upstream/downstream steps, writing operating protocol and training staff.

Developing or revising the analysis/interpretation portion of a protocol (variant-calling pipeline parameters, QC metric thresholds, interpretation criteria) plus the written SOP, verified by running control/reference DNA through the assay and checking concordance.

Field or point-of-collection protocol development for population, agricultural, or veterinary genetics: designing and testing sampling, preservation, and on-site genotyping procedures at farms, field sites, or clinic bedside, where material and conditions vary site to site.

Laboratory and controlled-facility work on collected material: sort and identify preserved bulk samples under a scope, run DNA extraction/PCR/metabarcoding on eDNA or specimens, run chemical and physiological assays, and run greenhouse/growth-chamber/mesocosm/aquarium experiments recording organism responses to environmental treatments; then compile and statistically analyze the resulting data.

instances.label: Classroom instruction: a faculty biologist delivers lecture/discussion sessions of an undergraduate or graduate course (genetics, ecology, cell biology) in a university lecture hall or seminar room — presenting material, fielding unscripted student questions, running demonstrations and exams, adjusting pace to the class. Institution-controlled premises, fixed layout, standard AV equipment.

Supervising and mentoring trainees: leading lab meetings, reviewing graduate students' and postdocs' raw data and figures, shaping project direction, demonstrating and correcting bench technique at the bench, and overseeing undergraduate teaching-lab or field-course sections (setting out materials, circulating among benches, correcting pipetting/dissection/microscope technique, enforcing safety). University research lab, teaching lab, and office.

Well-defined, repetitive experimental work within the PI's own research program: maintaining cell or microbial cultures, plate-based assays and screens, PCR/library prep, protocol or condition optimization sweeps, sample preparation and plate readouts, with results fed back to choose the next conditions. Standard university wet lab, standard consumables and instruments.

Exploratory, varied bench and specimen work in the PI's research: setting up a protocol never run in the lab before, troubleshooting failed experiments, dissection and tissue handling, animal or plant husbandry and phenotyping, delicate microscopy and imaging of irregular specimens, improvising fixtures and workarounds. University research lab and vivarium/greenhouse.

Field research data collection by remote survey: counting or filming wildlife populations and behavior, aerial habitat/vegetation mapping, or deploying environmental sensing over a field site (rangeland, wetland, forest edge) in variable weather and terrain, often with a student assistant present.

Hands-on field research: hiking to sites chosen on the day, netting/trapping/collecting organisms, taking soil, water or plant samples, tagging and measuring animals, labeling and preserving specimens for transport, while directing student field assistants. Terrain, weather and biota taken as found.

instances.label: Aerial or vessel-based population survey/count over wildland or open water: flying transects or grids to count deer, elk, waterfowl, seals or seabird colonies, or running acoustic/visual transects for a fish stock assessment, in variable weather and terrain, producing a defensible abundance/density estimate for management.

Ground-based field monitoring: hiking off-trail to establish and service camera-trap grids, acoustic recorders, hair snares and telemetry receivers (mount, aim, bait, swap batteries/cards, retrieve), walking transects, and collecting scat/hair/pellet samples in forest, brush or wetland.

Repeat water-sample collection at fixed aquatic monitoring stations (streams, lakes, coastal sites) for eDNA/occupancy monitoring of fish, amphibians or invasive aquatic species, requiring frequent samples over a season with field QC (rinse, preserve, label).

Live capture, restraint, handling, measurement, marking/tagging (bands, ear tags, PIT/CWT tags, GPS collars) and biological sampling (blood, fin clip, hair, swab) of wild animals, then release: mist-netting birds, box/foothold trapping mammals, helicopter net-gunning or darting ungulates, electrofishing or netting fish.

In-situ population management intervention in wild habitat: culling or removing overabundant/invasive animals (pest trapping networks, invasive marine or terrestrial species removal), delivering baits or vaccines, or hazing/exclusion, sustained over an area and documented with take records.

Institutional lab processing of population samples: accessioning heterogeneous field samples (hair off snag barbs, scat vials, fin clips, teeth/otoliths), subsampling, DNA extraction and genotyping for genetic mark-recapture or stock ID, or sectioning/reading aging structures, with QC feeding the population model.

instances.label: Wadeable stream, creek or wetland survey: biologist hikes/wades to several sites taken as found (brush, canopy, riffles, soft banks), takes in-situ handheld readings (pH, conductivity/salinity, DO, temperature, light/turbidity, Secchi) at defined points alongside fish/macroinvertebrate sampling, and logs habitat conditions.

Boat-based station work on a lake, reservoir, estuary or nearshore coastal water: run a small vessel to fixed stations, lower a multiparameter sonde/CTD for depth profiles of salinity, pH, DO, chlorophyll and PAR/Secchi light, and relate profiles to plankton, fish or algal bloom observations.

Laboratory bench analysis of water samples returned from the field: benchtop pH/conductivity meters, salinity by conductivity or refractometer, Winkler titration or optical DO, spectrophotometric nutrient/chlorophyll analysis, calibration standards and QA replicates in a research lab.

Controlled facility water measurement: hatchery raceways, aquaria, recirculating systems, experimental ponds or mesocosms holding study organisms; take routine salinity, pH, DO and light readings in each tank/unit and record against organism condition.

Deploying, retrieving and servicing continuous monitoring instrumentation at field sites: install moored sondes/buoys/light loggers, clean biofouled sensors, swap batteries, recalibrate, download data and redeploy from a boat or shoreline.

Offshore research-vessel work: CTD-rosette casts with oxygen, pH and irradiance sensors plus bottle sampling on transects in open ocean or large lake, underway flow-through salinity/fluorescence, paired with net tows or acoustic biological surveys.

instances.label: Bench development of a sample handling/preservation protocol in the research lab: splitting test material, comparing fixatives, buffers, filter types, corer liners or extraction kits across replicates, running yield/quality assays on lab instruments, iterating on conditions, and writing the validated SOP for collecting representative subsamples.

Designing and building a prototype sampling apparatus in the lab/shop: sketching or CAD of a modified soil corer, sediment grab, plankton net, insect or live trap, or water/eDNA filtration rig; machining, 3D printing or improvising parts from stock; assembling, bench/tank testing recovery and leakage, and reworking the device over several iterations.

Field trial and refinement of the new method/apparatus at a study site (forest, wetland, stream bank, rangeland plot): carrying gear over uneven terrain, laying out plots or transects, deploying against real substrate and biota, judging whether recovered material is representative, adjusting depth/mesh/timing on the spot, and documenting the revised procedure.

Aquatic method development from a research vessel or dock: rigging and trialing a Niskin rosette, benthic grab, tow net or eDNA filtration rig, tuning deployment depth, tow speed, filtration volume and on-deck sample handling and preservation in wind and swell, then codifying the procedure.

Developing a standardized sampling procedure inside a controlled facility (greenhouse, growth chamber, animal colony, aquaculture room): trialing leaf punches, root/soil cores from pots, swabs or blood draws on live organisms of varying size and morphology, checking representativeness and organism condition, and drafting the SOP for facility staff.

tasks.label: Monitor projects during or after construction to ensure projects conform to design specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Post-construction 'check-out' of an earthwork conservation practice on private farmland (grassed waterway, terrace, water-and-sediment control basin, diversion, pond excavation): locate the practice, measure length/area/cross-section/grades against the engineering design and NRCS standard, document as-built dimensions, and certify conformance for cost-share payment. Bare or freshly seeded earth, open field, drivable access.

Critical-stage inspection during construction of a structural practice (pond dam core trench and foundation, buried pipeline/principal spillway riser and anti-seep collars, concrete or geotextile placement, lift thickness and compaction): observe contractor work as it is covered up, spot-check materials and compaction, and direct corrections before the work is buried.

Check-out of a non-earthwork installed facility against spec (livestock fence, watering facility and trough, buried pipeline, heavy-use area protection pad, stream crossing, culvert): verify materials, dimensions, post/brace assemblies, pad thickness, and workmanship at close range, often with the landowner or contractor present.

Compliance walk-through of erosion and sediment control measures on an active construction site or timber harvest (silt fence installation and outlets, water bars, inlet protection, sediment basin risers, temporary stabilization/seeding within required timeframes): identify each noncompliant item, photograph it, and issue corrective directives.

Monitoring a stream, riparian, or wetland restoration project during and after construction: in-channel grade control and rock/log structures, bank grading and toe protection, hydrologic connection, planting layout — much of it in flowing water, under riparian canopy, or on soft unstable ground.

Post-construction vegetation establishment check on a revegetated or planted area (tree/shrub planting rows or pits in a windbreak, buffer, or reclamation area): count survival and stocking, map failed areas, and compare to the planting specification, typically one or more growing seasons later.

instances.label: Nutrient management (NRCS 590) on row-crop cropland: pull grid/zone soil cores across whole fields, get them to the lab, turn results into a variable-rate prescription and see the fertilizer applied per plan, with records. Open, machine-accessible fields; seasonal weather and mud.

Establishing herbaceous cover per plan on machine-accessible ground: seedbed prep and seeding of grass filter strips, field-border buffers, grassed-waterway cover, critical-area seedings and cover crops, plus first-year weed control and mowing. Farm fields and field edges.

Woody riparian buffer and streambank work: hand-planting bare-root tree/shrub seedlings on spacing, installing tree shelters and mats, live stakes/willow posts, coir logs and toe protection along an eroding stream corridor with steep, soft, brushy banks.

Structural soil/water practices: survey and stake a terrace, grassed waterway, sediment basin, water-and-sediment control basin or gully repair; direct the earthmoving contractor, handle topsoil, set inlet/outlet pipe or a water-control structure, then check as-built grade and certify to spec on a working farm.

Erosion and sediment control on disturbed/critical areas: trench and install silt fence, roll and staple erosion-control blankets, build rock or wattle check dams, install water bars and hand-mulch small bare areas on irregular, steep or rutted ground; repair failures after storms.

Livestock and water-management installations: build livestock exclusion fence and stream crossings, set off-stream tanks and buried pipeline on rangeland, install/adjust drainage water-control structures, and set up irrigation water management (soil moisture sensors, flow checks) on farms and ranches.

tasks.label: Revisit land users to view implemented land use practices or plans.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Follow-up visit to a working row-crop farm (soil conservationist / district conservationist): drive out, meet the producer, walk or drive fields to see whether cover crops, residue management/no-till, nutrient and pest management, and field-border practices were installed as planned; photograph, take GPS points, note deficiencies, and complete a practice status review/certification.

Revisit to a ranch or pasture operation to check implementation of a prescribed grazing plan: traverse pastures/rangeland on foot or ATV over rough, uneven, vegetated terrain; verify cross-fencing and stock-water developments were installed, look at forage utilization, stubble height and re-growth in each paddock, and talk through stocking and rotation with the rancher.

Inspection revisit for installed structural practices: terraces, grassed waterways, diversions, ponds/embankments, sediment basins, streambank stabilization or livestock exclusion fencing. Walk the structure, look for rills, gullies, settling, blocked outlets, damaged fence; take measurements/photos and write up condition and needed maintenance against the design.

Revisit to check establishment of vegetative/woody practices: tree and shrub plantings, riparian forest buffers, filter strips, pollinator or wildlife habitat seedings. Count seedling survival, judge stand density and weed/invasive competition, check buffer width and species, over brushy, wet or wooded ground.

Revisit centered on the land user rather than a single field: meet at the farmstead or shop, review the conservation plan and the operator's records of what was applied and when, walk around the headquarters area (barnyard, waste storage, heavy-use area, irrigation setup), answer questions and agree on adjustments or the next phase of the plan.

sources.system: Solix (Solinftec, ALICE AI)
sources.title: Solinftec Expands U.S. Footprint 243%, Deploys 100+ Autonomous Robots as It Showcases Next-Generation Solix System at Commodity Classic 2026
sources.claim: Solinftec's Solix is an autonomous, solar-powered field robot commercially deployed on US farms (100+ robots, 243% acreage growth) that continuously monitors crops with onboard AI and cameras, generating field-level intelligence on emergence, stand gaps, weed density and crop stage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous crop scouting. It shows a machine can traverse a working crop field unattended and report the vegetative condition of the field (emergence, stand gaps, weed pressure) — the same perception used when a conservation planner revisits a field to see whether a cover-crop or residue practice was established. It does not itself render a practice-compliance determination or meet the producer.

sources.system: Percepto AIM / Percepto Air drone-in-a-box
sources.title: Autonomous inspection rounds with AIM - Percepto
sources.claim: Percepto's AIM platform runs fully autonomous, scheduled inspection rounds with resident drone-in-a-box and ground robots at institution-controlled industrial, mining, utility and solar sites, producing daily AI reports on anomalies, environmental infractions and volumetric measurements; at ICL Dead Sea previously manual site inspections now run with no human involvement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: recurring autonomous site inspection rounds. Like a conservation revisit, the system returns to the same site on a schedule, views installed assets and earthworks (piles, tailings dams, pipes, vegetation), detects change or deviation, and issues a documented condition report — but only inside premises an institution controls and where the robot is resident.

sources.system: Spot + FieldAI Field Foundation Models

sources.claim: FieldAI's Field Foundation Models running on Boston Dynamics' Spot let the robot carry out inspection, mapping and monitoring job walks on constantly changing construction sites without prior maps, GPS or pre-planned routes, feeding progress tracking, quality verification and ...; deployed with major contractors across three continents over two years.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: as-built documentation and deviation analysis against a plan on an unstructured, changing site — conceptually the same act as revisiting a site to see whether work was implemented per plan. Transfer is limited to hard, walkable jobsite ground; it has not been shown on soft cropland, tall pasture, gullies or stream crossings, nor at field scale.

sources.system: SwagBot

sources.claim: SwagBot, an autonomous four-wheeled ground robot developed at the University of Sydney, determines pasture health, type and density and monitors livestock on grazing land, using the data to move cattle before overgrazing occurs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous pasture condition assessment on grazing land. Judging forage condition and grazing pressure is the core observation a conservation scientist makes when revisiting a prescribed-grazing plan; the robot has not been shown checking fences, pipelines and stock-water developments or reporting plan compliance.
