Counting and measuring trees under canopy is the same perception a planner uses for seedling survival counts and buffer stocking checks, though the demonstrated work is merchantable-timber inventory on managed timberland, not establishment/competition judgments on newly planted conservation sites.

tasks.label: Visit areas affected by erosion problems to identify causes or determine solutions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cropland site visit: conservation scientist drives to a farm with reported sheet, rill or ephemeral gully erosion, walks the field, digs/probes soil to check texture, compaction and topsoil loss, measures gully dimensions, reads slope and concentrated-flow paths, notes tillage, residue and drainage, interviews the operator, and determines causes and remedies (contour farming, cover crop, grassed waterway, terrace).

Streambank / riparian erosion visit: walks a stream reach on private or public land, wades or descends banks, assesses undercutting, bank height ratio, toe scour, vegetation, upstream hydrologic changes and livestock access, and determines cause and stabilization options (fencing, bioengineering, grade control).

Construction or other disturbed-site erosion and sediment control visit, often after a storm: inspects rills on stockpiles and slopes, silt fences, inlet protection, sediment basins and outfalls on an active, cluttered, muddy jobsite; determines why controls failed and what corrective action is required.

Rangeland/pasture visit: drives and walks a grazing unit or ranch two-track, assesses headcuts, hoof shear at water points, road-and-trail erosion, cover and utilization; determines whether the cause is stocking rate, water placement, road drainage, or drought, and recommends changes.

Remote or steep terrain visit: post-fire hillslope, forest road failure, landslide scarp or badly eroded ditch/culvert in brushy, steep, sometimes wet terrain reached on foot or ATV; determines the failure mechanism and treatment (water bars, mulching, seeding, culvert resizing).

sources.system: UAV/drone photogrammetry erosion monitoring (generic RGB/LiDAR/multispectral UAS)
sources.title: UAV-Based Soil Water Erosion Monitoring: Current Status and Trends
sources.claim: UAV photogrammetry is widely used to map and monitor soil erosion features (gullies, rills) at centimetre scale, but the reviewed workflows are data-collection pipelines flown on planned missions with human analysts interpreting results, not autonomous end-to-end site diagnosis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aerial survey and measurement of eroded ground. It supplies terrain data comparable to part of what a scientist observes, but the cited work stops at detection/measurement and does not establish autonomous determination of erosion causes or of remedial practices on site.

sources.system: Rogo SmartCore autonomous soil sampling robot
sources.date: 2019-11 (commercial service; fleet and acreage expanded through 2025)
sources.title: Autonomous soil sampling: Robo sampling improves accuracy — Top Crop Manager
sources.claim: Rogo's SmartCore robots autonomously navigate ordinary crop fields and pull soil cores on a pre-programmed grid as a commercial service across the Midwest; they collect samples but perform no site diagnosis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous traverse of an as-found farm field plus physical soil sampling — the mobility and sampling half of an erosion site visit. It does not substantiate the diagnostic half (reading flow paths, attributing cause, prescribing conservation practices), so it cannot support completion of this task.

sources.system: Percepto Air / Percepto AIM
sources.title: Autonomous Mining Inspection and Monitoring – Percepto
sources.claim: Percepto's drone-in-a-box systems fly scheduled autonomous inspection missions at institution-controlled industrial and mining sites and run AI change detection on the imagery; outputs are anomaly flags and reports rather than professional determinations of erosion cause and remedy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: recurring autonomous visual inspection and change detection of outdoor industrial ground (stockpiles, dams, haul roads) at an E2 facility. It shows a robot can get sensors onto eroding ground unattended, but no cited output includes causal diagnosis or a conservation solution accepted in place of a scientist's.

sources.claim: A UAV plus deep-learning pipeline automatically detected and classified slope anomalies such as cracks and failures at soil and water conservation sites, demonstrating automated feature detection from aerial imagery in a research setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated detection of erosion and slope-failure features at conservation sites. It substantiates image-based feature detection only; the study is a research demonstration and shows no autonomous ground inspection, cause attribution, or treatment recommendation.

instances.label: Conservation-planning resource inventory walkover of a private farm or ranch: the scientist walks the operation with the landowner, records current land uses and resource concerns (sheet/rill and gully erosion, compaction, overgrazing, streambank damage), checks soil map units with a spade or hand auger and texture-by-feel, takes georeferenced photos and field notes, and writes the inventory findings that drive the corrective conservation plan. Fenced pastures, livestock, mud, brush, no fixed layout.

Rangeland or pasture monitoring at permanent transects/plots on grazing land: line-point intercept or Daubenmire cover, species composition by weight or cover, clipped production, utilization/residual dry matter, plus soil-surface rangeland-health indicators (pedestals, rills, litter movement); results feed stocking-rate and grazing-plan corrections.

Aerial mapping survey of land use, land cover, erosion features and topography over a field, ranch parcel or small watershed: a pre-planned UAS photogrammetry/LiDAR mission producing an orthomosaic, digital elevation model, cover and gully/rill feature maps and change detection against prior flights, delivered as the survey record supporting a corrective plan.

Georeferenced soil sampling campaign across cropland fields for a soil-health, nutrient-loss or erosion investigation: cores pulled to a set depth on a grid or by management zone, composited, bagged and labeled for the lab, with locations recorded for repeat sampling.

Stream corridor, riparian or wetland investigation on land taken as found: channel cross-sections and bed elevations, bank-erosion measurement, riparian vegetation condition rating, and wetland indicators requiring soil pits and hydrology observation, to support a corrective streambank/buffer or restoration plan.

Status/compliance review of installed practices or a reclamation area on institution-controlled premises (mine reclamation area, landfill cap, utility right-of-way, agency project site or research farm): repeat site survey to verify vegetative cover establishment, erosion, drainage and practice condition, documenting change since the last visit for corrective action.

tasks.label: Develop soil maps.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Conservation-plan soil map for a farm or ranch tract: pull SSURGO/Web Soil Survey data into GIS, then walk/drive the property to verify map units on the ground with a hand probe or spade (texture by feel, depth to restrictive layer, wetness, eroded phases), adjust delineations, and produce the plan map and soils report. Setting: privately owned fields, pastures, fence rows, gates, mud, crop residue, livestock.

Original or update field soil survey mapping over a landscape (order-2): traverse by truck and on foot along transects, hand-auger borings to ~1.5 m at judgment-selected points, describe horizons (Munsell color, texture, structure, redoximorphic features), classify to series, place map unit boundaries using landform/lidar/imagery cues, then digitize and correlate delineations. Setting: mixed cropland, woodland, steep pasture, roadside cuts.

Site-specific soil investigation map for a parcel (hydric-soil/wetland delineation, septic or building suitability, mine reclamation or spoil mapping): 10-40 probe borings plus one or more excavated pits, profile descriptions and sampling, boundary flagging with GPS, and a parcel-scale soil map with report. Setting: brushy, wet or disturbed ground on private or municipal parcels.

Rangeland or forest soil and ecological-site inventory mapping in remote, rough terrain: off-road/off-trail traverses, backpack auger or spade pits at representative sites, soil-vegetation map unit delineation over thousands of acres. Setting: steep slopes, rock, brush, no roads, variable weather.

Farm-scale soil property mapping from dense sampling or sensing: lay out a grid or management zones, collect georeferenced cores at prescribed points (and/or run an EC/gamma sensor pass) across trafficable crop fields, send samples to a lab, and interpolate results into soil fertility, carbon or texture maps. Setting: production crop fields post-harvest, stubble, ruts, mud.

sources.system: ROGO SmartCore autonomous soil sampling robot
sources.developer: Rogo Ag LLC (with Central Valley Ag as service partner)

instances.label: Plant materials field trial at an NRCS Plant Materials Center or university research farm: prepare and seed replicated small plots of native grass/forb accessions, maintain them (weed control, irrigation), and record establishment counts, vigor ratings, height/biomass and seed set over one or more seasons. Institution-run research farm with surveyed plot layout and standard farm equipment.

Greenhouse or nursery screening trial of plant materials: pot up accessions, impose treatments (drought, salinity, fertility, inoculation), and take repeated germination, growth, biomass and condition measurements on hundreds of containers under controlled conditions.

Field vegetation and habitat condition survey for a wildlife habitat impact study on rangeland, forest, riparian or wetland ground: hike off-road to plots, run line-point intercept or Daubenmire transects, identify grass/forb/shrub species, measure shrub and tree density and canopy cover, rate soil-surface and disturbance indicators, take photo points, in variable terrain, brush and weather.

Wildlife survey component of a habitat impact study: site and deploy camera traps and acoustic recorders and later retrieve them, run point counts or track/scat/pellet transects, and occasionally do aerial or open-country counts across a project area of scattered, hard-to-reach sites.

Soil sampling campaign for an on-farm soil health, carbon or erosion study: drive a georeferenced grid or zone plan across cooperator crop fields, extract cores to a specified depth (including deeper bulk-density cores), label/track each sample and ship to the lab.

Develop the study and deliver its results: set objectives with landowners/agency partners, design the sampling scheme and protocols, secure permits and cooperator agreements, compile and analyze the data (statistics, GIS), and write the findings and management recommendations. Desk work in an office.

This is the same measurement work that constitutes the data-collection core of a plant material field trial (same objects: plots of sown plants; same traits: emergence, height, cover, canopy condition).

instances.label: Broadcast herbicide treatment of invasive brush and weeds (mesquite, prickly pear, juniper, noxious forbs) over tens to hundreds of acres of pasture/range unit: prescription rate, mix, and application over open, uneven, brushy ground with drift and buffer constraints.

Targeted spot/patch herbicide treatment of mapped weed or brush patches that are reachable from the air (scattered thickets, invasive annual grass patches, treatment blocks around drainages) on range and pasture land.

Ground-contact individual-plant treatment of scattered noxious weeds and woody plants: backpack sprayer, basal bark, cut-stump and wick applications along fencelines, roads, steep slopes, and riparian ground where non-target vegetation must be avoided.

Implementing a prescribed burn on a range unit to remove decadent forage/woody encroachment: prepping firelines, go/no-go on weather and fuel moisture, ignition (drip torch, ATV torch, or aerial), holding the perimeter, patrolling and mop-up, and post-burn security.
Revegetation by aerial/broadcast seeding of a native seed mix on burned, steep, rocky, or otherwise inaccessible rangeland where ground equipment cannot travel.

Revegetation by ground methods: rangeland drill seeding, seedbed prep (harrow, imprinter, chaining), and hand-transplanting shrub/sagebrush seedlings, plus protective measures such as temporary fencing on rough, rocky range sites.

instances.label: Quantitative ground plot monitoring on a grazing allotment (BLM/NRCS/Forest Service AIM- or Daubenmire-style): hike/drive to a randomly located plot in sagebrush steppe or desert grassland, lay three transect tapes, record line-point-intercept hits identified to plant species, canopy gap intercept, plant heights, a species inventory of the plot, a soil aggregate-stability test, and repeat photo points; enter data into the agency database.

Forage production and utilization sampling on a pasture or allotment: clip, bag, dry and weigh vegetation in quadrats (or double-sample estimated vs clipped weights), measure stubble heights and grazed-class utilization on key forage species, and compute pounds/acre and percent use to support stocking-rate and monitoring reports.

Special-status plant and noxious/invasive weed inventory for a biological assessment or EIS: walk meander or belt transects across a project footprint (pipeline, transmission line, solar site, allotment), identify plants to species including small forbs and grasses at various phenological stages, GPS-map occurrences and infestation boundaries, and document habitat.

Pasture- or allotment-scale quantitative assessment of vegetation cover, bare ground, canopy gaps, vegetation height/volume and standing crop or utilization across whole pastures, delivered as imagery-derived indicator maps and photo transects for a rangeland monitoring program or project baseline.

Qualitative condition-and-trend / rangeland health evaluation at key areas during an allotment inspection: ocular cover and species-composition estimates, comparison with the ecological site description, rating of soil-surface indicators (pedestalling, litter movement, erosion), and repeat photography, all recorded on standard field forms.

tasks.label: Plan and implement revegetation of disturbed sites.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Post-fire emergency stabilization and rehabilitation on burned rangeland: manager writes the seed prescription (species mix, PLS rates, timing) and the site is then broadcast-seeded from the air over a few hundred to a few thousand acres of open burn scar, in a narrow fall/winter window, with rough terrain, ash, and no ground access.

Revegetation of reshaped industrial disturbance — oil/gas pads, pipeline and utility corridors, two-track roads, mine benches and backfill slopes, including small remote parcels — where earthwork/grading is already signed off and the job is applying an approved native seed mix at rate over the surface with as-applied documentation.

Ground-mechanical seeding of a disturbed rangeland site: tractor-drawn rangeland drill, harrow, or imprinter over burned or brush-treated ground that is rocky, hummocky, stump- and sagebrush-studded, with slopes, washes and fences; includes drill calibration and seeding to prescribed depth and rate.

Disturbed sites requiring surface protection in addition to seed: steep cut slopes, severe-burn hillsides, stream crossings — straw mulch and crimping, hydromulch/tackifier, erosion control blankets, wattles and silt fence installed with the seeding.

Small localized disturbances under about five acres — water developments, corrals, staging areas, fire/dozer lines, campsites, fence lines — hand-broadcast seeding, hand raking/scarifying, spot mulching, planting sagebrush or forb plugs, and installing protective cages or temporary exclosure fencing.

Riparian, wetland and woody revegetation: installing willow and cottonwood cuttings into wet, muddy, uneven banks, planting containerized shrubs and seedlings across a burn, and fitting browse-protection cages, often in dense brush and on unstable footing.

tasks.label: Provide care for park program animals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily husbandry round in a nature-center animal room / exhibit hall for reptiles, amphibians and display fish: prepare and offer varied diets (live crickets and worms, thawed rodents by tongs, greens), refresh water bowls, mist tanks, spot-clean feces and shed skin, verify heat/UVB/humidity, observe each animal for illness, and log records.

Periodic deep clean of enclosures: temporarily move the animal to a holding tub, strip and replace substrate, scrub and disinfect glass, rocks, branches and water features, wash bowls, carriers and program equipment, reassemble the habitat, and return the animal.

Care of resident raptors or other ambassador birds in outdoor mews at a park visitor center: cut and offer whole-prey diets, weigh the bird, inspect feet, plumage and falconry equipment, rake/clean mews and perches, and handle the bird on the glove for conditioning.

Health monitoring and treatment of program animals: spot signs of illness or injury, administer medications, soaks or wound care, manage quarantine of new or sick animals, and crate and transport an animal to a veterinarian.

Care of small mammals and invertebrates (rabbit, guinea pig, tarantula, hissing cockroaches, observation beehive): feed and water, change bedding, provide enrichment, maintain colony/breeding feeder cultures.

Living-history farm or heritage-breed park site: daily care of livestock program animals (goats, sheep, chickens) — hay and grain feeding, watering, mucking and re-bedding pens, egg collection, and daily individual health checks.

sources.system: Tecniplast / IWT vivarium automation (robotic cage and bottle processing lines)

It is the closest deployed analogue to cleaning program-animal enclosures, but it works only on uniform, animal-free plastic cages delivered by conveyor, not heterogeneous furnished terrariums or mews with live animals in them, so it does not carry over to the whole instance.

instances.label: Scheduled guided nature walk on an established park trail for drop-in general public (mixed ages, families): the naturalist gathers the group at a trailhead, sets pace, stops at viewpoints, and narrates plant, wildlife, and geologic features, answering questions along the way.

School or youth group field trip at a state park or nature center: the naturalist leads students along a trail or to a pond/meadow station, explains ecological concepts tied to curriculum, sometimes showing a specimen, pelt, or net sample while talking, and keeps the group oriented and on task.

Guided walking tour of a historic site (fort, battlefield, historic house grounds, or cultural landscape): the naturalist/interpreter walks visitors between fixed stops on paths and lawns, narrating events and pointing out structures, monuments, and landscape features.

Specialty interpretive outing under demanding conditions: night sky or owl-prowl walk, dawn birding hike, snowshoe or tidepool walk, or cave/lava-tube tour, with uneven terrain, low light, weather exposure, and safety briefing plus headcount management.

Vehicle- or vessel-based interpretive trip (tram, pontoon boat, canoe float, or bus tour) where the naturalist narrates passing scientific, historic, and natural features and answers visitor questions en route.

instances.label: Staffing the visitor center information desk / contact station for a shift: greeting arrivals, orienting them to the park, answering varied questions (trail and road conditions, wildlife, weather, closures), issuing backcountry or fishing permits and Junior Ranger booklets, running the cooperating-association bookstore register (cash/card, bagging, receipts), answering the phone and the radio.

Daily opening and closing / readiness rounds of the building: unlocking doors, disarming and arming the alarm, switching on lighting and exhibit AV and the orientation film, putting out sandwich-board signs and the flag, updating the trail-conditions board, walking the building at close to clear visitors, counting and reconciling the cash drawer, shutting down equipment, locking up.

Floor care of the public spaces: scrubbing/mopping the hard-floor lobby and exhibit hall, vacuuming carpeted areas of the auditorium and hallways, spot-cleaning tracked-in mud and snowmelt at the entry during operating hours with visitors moving through.

Servicing the public restrooms and waste: cleaning toilets, urinals, sinks and mirrors, mopping restroom floors, restocking paper towels, toilet paper and ... dispensers, emptying interior and entry-plaza trash and recycling bins and hauling bags to the dumpster.

Restocking and supply handling: refilling brochure, map and site-bulletin racks, shelving and facing bookstore merchandise, receiving a delivery of cartons at the back door, moving them to the storeroom, unpacking and shelving stock, and topping up desk supplies (permits, junior ranger badges, forms).

Exhibit and program-space upkeep plus incidental facility responses: wiping exhibit case glass and touch tables, replacing burnt-out display bulbs and rebooting a stuck AV kiosk, changing bulletin-board panels, setting out chairs, table and projector for an evening program and re-stacking them after, plus incidents such as a spilled drink, a lost-and-found item, a bat or wasp in the lobby, or a minor first-aid request.

tasks.label: Perform emergency duties to protect human life, government property, and natural features of park.

instances.label: First-responder medical care in a developed park area: a visitor at the visitor center, campground, amphitheater or trailhead parking lot collapses, is stung, cut, heat-sick, or in cardiac arrest. The naturalist stops the program, assesses the patient, provides first aid/CPR/AED, controls bleeding, calms bystanders, radios dispatch, and hands off to arriving EMS.

Backcountry medical/rescue response: hiking or paddling to a reported injured or hypothermic visitor on a trail, cliff, riverbank or cave route; assessing, splinting/bandaging, packaging the patient, and assisting or litter-carrying them out over rough, unimproved terrain with a small team.

Search for an overdue or missing visitor (child separated from family, hiker off-trail at dusk): sweeping assigned sectors of forest, dunes or canyon on foot, calling and listening, checking hazards such as water and drop-offs, then locating the person, checking their condition and escorting them out.

Fire and hazardous-condition response: spotting smoke on patrol, extinguishing an unattended or escaped campfire (drown, stir, feel for heat), initial attack on a small grass/brush ignition with hand tools or a backpack pump, and clearing visitors from the area until suppression crews arrive.

Emergency evacuation of a developed use area during flash flood, severe thunderstorm, hazmat or wildlife incident: sweeping the beach/campground/exhibit building, warning and directing visitors out, assisting the mobility-impaired, closing and barricading gates and trailheads, and accounting for people.

Protecting property and natural features after storms or incidents: clearing or taping off downed limbs and washed-out trail sections, securing a damaged historic structure or exhibit, hazing a bear out of a campground, and guarding a damaged sensitive resource until repair crews arrive.

It covers only the detection sub-step of the naturalist's search-and-rescue instance; the drone cannot travel to the person on foot, assess their condition, or escort/carry them out, so it does not complete the instance.

tasks.label: Survey park to determine forest conditions and distribution and abundance of fauna and flora.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Forest stand-structure inventory in wooded park land: the naturalist walks to fixed plots or transects off-trail, measures tree diameters at breast height, heights and stem density, tallies standing dead and downed wood, and compiles stand structure data for the park's resource records.

Landscape-scale forest condition mapping over large park blocks: assessing extent of canopy mortality, storm blowdown, insect/disease damage or fuel loading across hundreds to thousands of acres, producing a map or extent estimate for management and interpretive reporting.

On-foot forest ecological condition and ground-flora inventory: recording overstory and understory species composition, regeneration and deer-browse impacts, insect and disease symptoms on individual trees, hazard trees, scattered understory invasive shrubs and herbs, and rare-plant occurrences, in dense brushy forest interior.

Ground-level fauna surveys: breeding-bird point counts identified by sight and ear, frog and toad call surveys at wetlands at night, cover-board and turtle/salamander checks, butterfly and dragonfly counts, stream macroinvertebrate kick-net sampling, and deploying/servicing camera and acoustic stations off-trail.

Broad-area abundance counts of large warm-bodied wildlife: deer density estimation across a whole park unit (often at night in winter), waterfowl or colonial nesting bird colony counts across open water and marsh, to justify management actions.

Flora distribution mapping over open, canopy-visible habitats: delineating wetland Phragmites or cattail stands, meadow and grassland invasive patches, and mapping dominance of vegetation types across marsh or prairie units of the park.

tasks.label: Construct historical, scientific, and nature visitor-center displays.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Visitor-center lobby/exhibit alcove: naturalist builds a small changeable interpretive display — prints text and photo panels, trims and mounts them on foam core or matboard with spray adhesive, arranges natural objects (skull, cones, rock samples, pressed plants) with hand-made labels in a case or on a display table.

Seasonal rotation/refresh of an existing nature display or hands-on touch table: swap in new specimens (pelts, mounted birds, antlers, feathers, shells), reposition and re-secure fragile mounts, replace labels and captions, clean and re-close the case.

Exhibit workroom of a park: build a habitat diorama or 3-D case — cut and paint a backdrop, shape terrain from foam/plaster, glue down substrate (sand, duff, gravel), position taxidermy mounts and props, run small lighting, fit the case front.

Fabricate framed graphic panels or a bulletin-style display and mount them in the visitor center: cut mats and frame stock, mount printed graphics into frames with glue/fasteners and press, then measure, level, drill and hang the finished panels on the interior wall.

Historical artifact case: fabricate custom mounts/cradles for fragile historic objects (tools, documents, uniform parts), arrange and secure them per conservation practice, install label rails and the acrylic/glass cover.

Outdoor wayside or trailside display just outside the visitor center: set the frame or posts in uneven ground, bolt on the fabricated interpretive panel, level and secure it in weather and on a public, uncontrolled trail edge.

sources.claim: A commercial four-robot, vision-guided assembly line built by Midwest Engineered Systems assembles picture frames of many different styles and sizes, automating glue application, material insertion and press operations without custom fixturing per size.

Objects (frame stock, glazing, backing, printed sheet), precision (mitre joints, flush glazing) and output (a finished framed panel) match the fabrication half of a framed interpretive display built in a fixtured cell.

sources.system: Hilti Jaibot
sources.title: Hilti Unveils BIM-Enabled Construction Jobsite Robot
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot is a commercially sold semi-autonomous construction robot that drills BIM-specified overhead holes automatically once an operator has driven it by remote control into each drilling area; it does not place or fasten the mounted item.

roles.title: Foresters
roles.description: Manage public and private forested lands for economic, recreational, and conservation purposes. May inventory the type, amount, and location of standing timber, appraise the timber's worth, negotiate the purchase, and draw up contracts for procurement. May determine how to conserve wildlife habitats, creek beds, water quality, and soil stability, and how best to comply with environmental regulations. May devise plans for planting and growing new trees, monitor trees for healthy growth, and determine optimal harvesting schedules.

instances.label: Industrial/company forester builds the annual and multi-year cutting program for fee timberlands: pulls stand inventory and growth-and-yield data into GIS/planning software, allocates stands to harvest by year, and balances volume, species mix, and age-class targets against the mill's production goals. Output is an approved harvest schedule and unit list.

Preparing and marketing an individual timber sale: appraising stumpage value from cruise data, writing the sale prospectus and contract terms (volume, species, payment, operating period, BMP requirements), soliciting and evaluating bids from logging contractors or mills, and awarding the sale.

Administering an active sale to meet production goals: tracking scale tickets and load counts against contracted volume, reconciling payments, adjusting weekly delivery quotas among loggers and mills as weather or market conditions shift, and documenting contract compliance and sale closeout.

Field reconnaissance of candidate harvest units before scheduling: walking the stand, checking merchantability, terrain, access and stream buffers, GPS-mapping unit boundaries, and choosing a logging system and silvicultural prescription that will be written into the cutting plan.

Consulting forester managing a sale for a private nonindustrial landowner or a public agency: explaining harvest options, negotiating with prospective buyers, coordinating the timing of the cut with landowner objectives and market prices, and reporting proceeds and production results.

instances.label: Routine inspection of a managed forest tract or stand (industrial timberland, state or federal ownership): the forester walks or drives the stand, assesses stocking, growth, tree size/condition, storm or animal damage and general site condition, records notes/photos, and writes a short condition report with recommendations. Rolling terrain, brush, no fixed layout.

Inspection of an active or recently completed timber harvest for contract and BMP compliance: stream crossings and buffers, skid-trail rutting and water bars, stump height and utilization, residual stand damage, boundary lines, landing cleanup — usually on foot, often with equipment and crews working on site.

Post-planting regeneration/survival and stocking survey on an open cutover or young plantation: count surviving seedlings on plots or across the unit, note species and competing vegetation, and judge whether the unit meets stocking/free-to-grow standards.

Damage-extent survey of a tract after a windstorm, drought, wildfire or bark-beetle outbreak: map where and how severely crowns are dead/discolored or trees are blown down across the property, and report acreage affected.

Diagnostic forest health inspection: close, hands-on examination of individual trees — needles, bark, boring dust and galleries, fruiting bodies, root collars — sometimes with sample collection, to identify the responsible insect or pathogen and rate severity.

Forest nursery inspection: walking bareroot seedbeds and greenhouse benches at a state, federal or industrial forest nursery to count seedlings, measure height and stem caliper, and check for disease, insects, weeds and cull-grade quality before lifting and shipping.

tasks.label: Monitor contract compliance and results of forestry activities to assure adherence to government regulations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inspection of an active logging operation under a timber sale or harvest contract (private industrial land, consulting client tract, or state/federal sale): the forester drives in, walks the landing, skid trails and unit boundary, checks streamside management zone width and stream crossings, rutting, leave-tree/retention marking, stump heights and utilization, talks with the logging crew about corrections, photographs and GPS-tags problems, and records findings against the contract and state forest-practices rules. Terrain is as-found: slash, stumps, mud, brush, slopes, moving machinery.

Post-harvest closeout / BMP audit before final payment or bond release: walking the completed unit and haul/skid roads to verify water bars and outsloping, culvert and temporary-crossing removal, seeding/mulching of disturbed soil, slash pulled out of streams, landings cleaned up, gates/road closure, and boundary integrity (no trespass), then signing off or issuing a corrective-action notice.

First- or second-year survival and stocking check on an open, recently planted harvest unit under a planting contract or reforestation requirement: counting live seedlings on sample plots or across the unit, computing trees per acre and survival percent against the contract/regulatory stocking standard, and mapping deficient areas for replanting. Seedlings are visible above light ground vegetation.

Planting-quality inspection while a planting or site-prep crew is working, plus later regeneration surveys on sites where competing brush, hardwood sprouts, grass or slash obscure seedlings: pulling seedlings to check planting depth, J-roots, soil packing and spacing, checking bag storage/handling, judging herbicide or site-prep results, and deciding whether contract specifications were met.

Remote/aerial verification over a tract: flying or ordering imagery of the harvest unit to confirm the cut stayed inside the permitted boundary, measure harvested area, check riparian buffer and retention patch widths and road construction against the approved permit/contract map, and document the result for the file.

Office review of the contract file: checking load tickets and scale/weight slips against contract volumes and payments, verifying permits, insurance, notifications and contractor certifications, reconciling harvest reports, and writing the inspection report, compliance certification, or notice of violation.

tasks.label: Map forest area soils and vegetation to estimate the amount of standing timber and future value and growth.

instances.label: Cruise of a managed conifer/southern-pine plantation or thinned even-aged stand (40-500 acres) for a harvest plan or timber appraisal: lay out plots, tally species/DBH/heights/form, walk the stand, then compute volume by product class, stumpage value and projected growth. Planted rows, gentle-to-moderate terrain, relatively open understory, road access.

Cruise of a mixed natural stand (Appalachian/Lake States hardwood or mixed conifer) on a nonindustrial private woodlot or state land: dense understory and brush, many species, leaning/forked stems; value hinges on species calls plus defect, sweep, cull and log-grade judgments made tree-by-tree, then volume/value/growth estimates.

Ownership- or landscape-scale mapping: delineate stand types, cover and site classes across thousands of acres from aerial imagery/LiDAR plus soil survey layers in GIS, acquire new imagery over the tract, stratify and produce stand-level standing-timber, value and growth estimates for the management plan.

Remeasurement of permanent/continuous forest inventory (CFI) plots on institutional or industrial timberland to update growth: relocate monumented plots, re-tally tagged trees (DBH, height, mortality, ingrowth), and recompute stand volume, growth rate and future value. Managed conifer/plantation stands with maintained road networks.

Field soil and site mapping component of the inventory: auger holes or small pits at points across the tract, describe texture, depth, color/drainage and rooting restrictions, delineate wet or low-productivity ground, and assign site index/productivity classes used to project future growth.

Cruise of a steep, roadless or remote tract (PNW mountain slopes, backcountry parcels): hike in with compass/GPS, work slopes over 40%, brush and blowdown, sometimes limited daylight or seasonal access, tally plots and produce volume and value estimates.

tasks.label: Choose and prepare sites for new trees, using controlled burning, bulldozers, or herbicides to clear weeds, brush, and logging debris.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Choosing the site and writing the prescription: walking a recently harvested tract or idle field, checking soils, drainage, wet areas and access, judging competing vegetation and species suitability, locating streamside buffers and property lines, and hanging flagging to mark the treatment unit before any treatment is ordered.

Broadcast chemical site preparation on a cutover unit (roughly 20-300 acres of stumps, slash and resprouting hardwoods, often with standing snags): mixing an imazapyr/glyphosate tank, applying a uniform rate across the whole unit while keeping herbicide out of streamside management zones and off neighboring property, and documenting acres and weather.

Selective/spot herbicide site prep on small, steep, wet or sensitive tracts: backpack spraying individual competing stems, basal-bark and hack-and-squirt treatment of residual hardwoods, and spot release around planting rows on small private woodlots.

Prescribed site-preparation burning: preparing and blacklining firelines, checking fuel moisture and wind, igniting a broadcast burn over a cutover (drip torch or aerial ignition), holding the fire inside the unit, and mopping up smoldering slash; or lighting and tending machine-built slash piles.

Heavy mechanical site preparation on cutover ground: dozer with V-blade/rake shearing brush and small stems and windrowing or piling logging debris, drum chopping, subsoiling/ripping and bedding, working around stumps, wet holes, steep pitches and buffer boundaries.

Manual and small-equipment cleanup of odd areas: hand-piling slash, brush-saw/chainsaw clearing of competing brush along edges and on steep or wet spots too small or too sensitive for heavy equipment, and mulching small patches before planting.

tasks.label: Plan and implement projects for conservation of wildlife habitats and soil and water quality.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Assess a tract and design a conservation project: walk unroaded private woodlot or public forest ground to locate streams, seeps, wetlands, erodible soils and habitat features; take photos, soil/channel measurements and GPS points; combine with GIS/aerial data; write the prescription, BMP specs and cost-share/permit paperwork the landowner or agency will accept.

Lay out the project on the ground before an operation: flag streamside management zones, wetland and buffer boundaries with tape, paint-mark leave trees, snags and den trees, stake stream-crossing and road/landing locations, over steep brushy terrain with slash, poison ivy, blowdown and no site preparation.

Install or direct installation of soil and water BMPs during/after a harvest or road job: water bars and broad-based dips on skid trails and roads, culverts and crossing armoring, silt fence and check dams, seeding and mulching bare soil, closing and stabilizing trails, then inspecting to standard.

Broadcast vegetation-control treatment over an open, harvested cut-over, burned unit or old field to knock back invasive/competing woody and herbaceous plants for habitat or seedling-release objectives: define the treatment polygon, mix the labeled herbicide, apply it evenly across tens of acres of stump-filled, uneven ground while avoiding buffers and drift into water.

Hand-scale habitat and riparian improvement inside standing forest: plant seedlings/mast trees and riparian buffer stock to spacing and stocking standards, install tree shelters or fencing, girdle or inject trees to create snags, cut-stump/basal-bark treat scattered invasive stems, build brush piles, hang nest or bat boxes.

Equipment- or crew-based habitat treatment: implement a prescribed burn for habitat restoration (line prep, ignition, holding, mop-up), mechanical fuels mastication, instream large-wood placement or an undersized culvert replacement for aquatic organism passage, coordinating contractors and inspecting the finished work.

tasks.label: Monitor forest-cleared lands to ensure that they are reclaimed to their most suitable end use.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Post-harvest regeneration/stocking check on an open clearcut or newly planted block on industrial or state timberland: forester drives to the unit, walks plots across the cutover, counts and identifies seedlings, judges stocking and survival, and reports whether interplanting is needed. Open sky, no residual canopy, slash and stumps underfoot.

Regeneration / free-to-grow assessment on a partially cut, shelterwood, or heavily brushed unit where seedlings sit beneath residual canopy, slash piles or dense competing vegetation; requires ground plots, species identification, height and vigor calls, and brush-competition judgments made under the canopy.

Post-harvest site-rehabilitation / BMP compliance inspection of a recently logged tract: walk skid trails, landings, haul roads, stream crossings and riparian buffers; verify water bars, culvert removal, seeding and mulching of landings, check rutting and sediment delivery; document deficiencies and require corrective work from the operator.

Broad-area monitoring pass over several recently cleared units to map ground cover, vegetation re-establishment and problem spots (bare soil, gullies, failed patches) and to prioritize follow-up; deliverable is a georeferenced map/report rather than a plot-by-plot ground call.

Monitoring reclamation of cleared land being returned to a non-timber or restored end use: surface-mine bench, quarry, pipeline right-of-way, well pad or utility corridor. Assess revegetation cover, planted tree survival, erosion and gullying, grading and drainage stability, for bond release, permit compliance or contract acceptance.

On-site follow-up with planting/reclamation contractors or landowners: inspect planting quality (root placement, spacing, seedling handling), dig or pull sample seedlings, verify corrective treatments such as release or re-seeding were done, and sign off on the work at the site.

tasks.label: Direct, and participate in, forest fire suppression.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Initial attack ground work on a small wildfire (roughly 0.1-10 acres) on state, federal or industrial forest land: hike or drive in, size up, construct handline with pulaski/McLeod and chainsaw, direct attack with backpack pump or engine hose lay, secure the burning edge. Steep brushy terrain, smoke, heat, snags, shifting wind.

Immediate attack on an incipient ignition (single lightning-struck smoldering snag or spot fire under ~0.1 acre) found within minutes in a remote monitored forest: knock it down with water/dirt and confirm it is out.

Mop-up and patrol after containment: grid the black, cold-trail by hand, dig out stump holes and burning root systems, fell fire-weakened snags with a chainsaw, work hose lays and water to cool hotspots until the fire can be declared out.

Engine, water tender and dozer support: drive a Type 6 engine on rough forest roads, pump-and-roll along the flank, lay and progressively extend hose, swamp/guide a dozer cutting line, shuttle water. Rutted roads, downed timber, poor visibility in smoke.

Firing operations: burnout or backfire from a road, handline or dozer line with a drip torch or fusees, timing ignition to fuel, slope and wind, then holding the line and catching slopovers with hand tools and water.

Directing on scene as a type 4/5 incident commander or division supervisor: scout the fire on foot and by vehicle, give a size-up, assign crews, engines and dozers to tactics, order additional resources by radio, brief crews, act as ground contact for air support, and document the incident.

sources.title: Dryad Networks Reaches XPRIZE Wildfire Finals Milestone, Demonstrating Autonomous Detection and Suppression of Wildfires in Alaska
sources.claim: Dryad's Silvanet sensor network plus Silvaguard drones autonomously detected a small wildfire within ... dispatched a suppression drone that located and attacked it with no human involvement, during XPRIZE Wildfire finals across a 1,000 km2 remote test area near Nenana, Alaska in June 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family as a forester's initial attack on a newly reported smoke: locate the ignition in wildland fuels and apply suppressant before spread.

sources.transferJustification: Aerial initial attack on early-stage fires is a component of the same suppression task; comparable wildland terrain, but delivers only water drops, not line construction or mop-up.

tasks.label: Procure timber from private landowners.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small non-industrial private woodlot (20-100 acres, mixed pine/hardwood) in a rural county. Procurement forester responds to a landowner inquiry or cold call, checks deed and tax maps, walks the tract with the owner over brush, deadfall and uncertain property lines, runs cruise plots (prism/DBH tape) to estimate volume by product, checks access, stream crossings and haul route, prices the tract, then negotiates and executes a lump-sum timber purchase contract at the landowner's kitchen table and issues payment.

Southern pine plantation clearcut or thinning of 100-500 acres offered directly or through a consulting forester's bid sale. Forester uses aerial/GIS imagery, then field-verifies stocking with a plot cruise, walks and flags sale boundaries and streamside management zones, evaluates deck and road locations, prepares and submits a bid, and negotiates terms and a harvest window with the landowner or their agent.

Hardwood selective/partial harvest on private land where the sale must be marked: forester paints each crop tree to be cut and a boundary line, tallies marked trees by species and grade, appraises value from grade recovery, and negotiates a per-unit or lump-sum purchase with a landowner who is sensitive about residual stand quality.

Repeat or dealer-sourced tract from a known landowner: appraisal mostly from prior inventory data, imagery and a brief drive-through/spot field check; price agreed by phone, contract e-signed and harvest scheduled. Minimal field time.

Salvage procurement after a storm, fire or beetle outbreak: rapid field assessment of blown-down, leaning or degrading timber under hazardous conditions, quick estimate of recoverable volume and degrade, and an urgent negotiation and contract with a distressed landowner.

Constrained small tract: steep terrain, wetlands, unclear or disputed boundary lines, or wildland-urban interface neighbors. Forester walks and verifies lines with adjoining owners, negotiates access easements or road use, addresses landowner concerns and regulatory constraints before contracting.

tasks.label: Monitor wildlife populations and assess the impacts of forest operations on population and habitats.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-operation wildlife/habitat reconnaissance on foot: forester walks a proposed harvest unit off-trail (brush, slash, slopes, downed wood), searching for raptor/heron nests, den and cavity trees, bat roosts, burrows, tracks, scat and browse sign; records locations by GPS, flags protection buffers and wildlife leave trees, and writes findings into the sale prescription.

Post-operation habitat impact assessment: after a harvest or thinning, the forester walks and/or flies the unit, riparian buffers and haul roads to check retained wildlife trees and snags, downed-wood levels, canopy retention, buffer width and integrity, and ground/soil disturbance; documents whether habitat objectives and wildlife prescriptions were met.

Deploying, servicing and retrieving field monitoring gear across a forest ownership over a season: hiking to scattered points to strap trail cameras and acoustic recorders to trees, aiming and setting them, swapping batteries/SD cards, re-establishing pellet-count and browse-transect plots, and collecting the data.

Broad-area wildlife population counts to estimate abundance/trend on managed forest land: aerial or night thermal counts of deer, elk or colonial nesting birds over hundreds to thousands of acres of mixed forest and openings, producing a density estimate used for management planning.

Species-protocol ground surveys tied to operations: spotted-owl or goshawk call-back surveys at night, bat emergence counts at roosts, songbird point counts at dawn, amphibian egg-mass searches in forested wetlands — following an agency protocol at fixed stations in the woods and recording detections.

Landscape habitat-change assessment for a plan or annual report: acquiring/ordering aerial or drone imagery and LiDAR over harvest areas, mapping habitat loss, fragmentation and structural change attributable to operations, and compiling the impact assessment with limited field verification.

instances.label: Cell-based exposure experiment in a university/government research lab: seed cultured human or animal cells into multiwell plates, dose with a dilution series of a drug, pesticide or other toxicant, incubate, add assay reagents (viability, reporter, stain), read plates/image cells, and fit dose-response curves for cytotoxic or morphological effect.

Microbiological work in a BSL-2 lab: process clinical or environmental specimens, inoculate culture media or infect cell monolayers with the microorganism, incubate, read growth/plaques/colony counts, identify and quantify the organism, and record results for the exposure study.

Molecular endpoint analysis of exposed material: harvest treated cells or tissue, extract nucleic acid or protein, set up qPCR / sequencing library prep / immunoassay plates, run the instrument, and analyze the readouts against control samples.

Histology/cytology of tissue from exposed animals or 3D cultures: fix, process, embed and section tissue, stain slides, examine microscopically for changes in cell structure and tissue architecture, and score/quantify lesions.

Inhalation/gas or whole-animal exposure work: culture cells at an air-liquid interface (or house animals in an exposure chamber), expose them to a gas, smoke or aerosol in an exposure system, then harvest inserts or tissues and run the downstream assays.

tasks.label: Follow strict safety procedures when handling toxic materials to avoid contamination.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine bench handling of hazardous chemical reagents in a research lab: weighing a toxic powder (acrylamide, ethidium bromide), preparing and aliquoting stock solutions of formaldehyde, phenol-chloroform or organic solvents in a chemical fume hood, capping and labeling vials, dropping contaminated tips into the designated hazardous-waste container and wiping the surface. Repeated, protocol-driven work with familiar labware.

BSL-2 biological work in a Class II biosafety cabinet: aliquoting human blood/tissue or culturing and inoculating infectious agents and cell lines, aseptic technique to prevent cross- and self-contamination, surface decontamination with 70% ethanol/bleach, bagging biohazard waste for the autoclave. Research lab or associated translational specimen lab.

Handling cytotoxic or highly potent compounds: reconstituting and serially diluting chemotherapeutic agents, toxins or potent test articles from vials into syringes/plates for cell treatment or animal dosing, using closed-system transfer devices, double gloves and containment, with wipe monitoring for surface contamination. Research lab or investigational-drug pharmacy.

Radioisotope work in a licensed lab area: dispensing stock activity and setting up radiolabeling reactions (32P, 125I, 18F, 177Lu) behind lead/acrylic shielding, using tongs and dosimetry, surveying the bench with a Geiger counter, performing wipe tests and segregating radioactive waste.

Ad hoc, non-routine hazardous manipulations outside any fixed workflow: setting up an unfamiliar procedure with a new reagent from its SDS, handling odd or legacy containers, carrying hazardous samples between rooms in secondary containment, loading a shared centrifuge/autoclave/analyzer with hazardous material and decontaminating that shared equipment afterwards.

Incident and waste-stream duties: cleaning up a chemical or biohazard spill with a spill kit, decontaminating after a broken tube in a rotor, packaging, labeling and moving satellite-accumulation hazardous and biohazardous waste for EHS pickup, and entering/exiting BSL-3 space with PAPR/Tyvek donning, doffing and decontamination.

instances.label: In vitro cell-based evaluation of a drug candidate, pesticide or other chemical: seed cultured cells in multiwell plates, prepare serial dilutions, dose, incubate, add viability/reporter reagents, read plates, and fit concentration-response curves to derive potency/cytotoxicity. Done at a bench in an academic, government or pharma research lab with shared incubators and plate readers.

Molecular/biochemical characterization of exposure effects: enzyme-inhibition or receptor-binding assays, lysing treated cells and running qPCR / gene-expression profiling, ELISA or Western-blot style protein quantification to determine at what level and by what mechanism the agent acts. Bench work in a standard research lab.

In vivo rodent study: dose mice/rats with a compound, pesticide, or infect with a parasite/microorganism; observe clinical signs and body weight over days-weeks; take timed blood samples; euthanize, necropsy, harvest and fix tissues; prepare and read histopathology. Occurs in an AAALAC-style vivarium, procedure room and necropsy suite.

Microbiology/parasitology bench work: culture bacteria, fungi or parasites, plate and streak, expose them to candidate drugs or disinfectants, determine MIC/zone diameters or growth inhibition, count colonies, and interpret susceptibility; or infect host cells and score effects. BSL-2 laboratory with hoods, incubators and imaging.

Evaluation of drug effects at the human level using clinical-trial or patient biospecimens: receive and process blood/tissue, run hematology, clinical chemistry and immunoassay pharmacodynamic/safety panels, review and release results against reference and flagging rules. Clinical or translational core laboratory.

instances.label: Cell-based toxicity/viability work in a BSL-2 research lab: maintain cell lines (thaw, feed, passage), seed multiwell plates, dose with compound dilution series, incubate, run viability/cytotoxicity or reporter readout on a plate reader or high-content imager, and analyze dose-response. Standard labware (flasks, 96/384-well plates), biosafety cabinet, CO2 incubators.

Histology/cell-structure work: fix and process tissue blocks, embed in paraffin, cut sections on a microtome, mount and stain (H&E, special stains, IHC), coverslip, image on a microscope or slide scanner, and score morphology/marker expression. Input is grossed tissue in cassettes; work occurs in a histology/pathology lab.

Microbiology: plate tissue homogenates, fluids or swabs onto agar, streak for isolation, incubate, read plates for growth, and identify bacteria/fungi (MALDI-TOF, biochemical panels, susceptibility) in a clinical or research micro lab with standard media, incubators and identification instruments.

Cell-suspension analytics: dissociate tissue or harvest cultured cells into single-cell suspension, lyse/wash, stain with antibody panels, and run flow cytometry / immunophenotyping (or prep for single-cell sequencing), then analyze the data. Tubes and plates handled at the bench and on benchtop instruments in a core facility or research lab.

Gross work-up of organs and whole tissue: rodent or large-animal necropsy, or receipt of surgical/autopsy specimens — identify and remove organs, weigh, inspect, cut representative sections with scalpel/knife, and allocate pieces to fixative, cassettes, OCT or liquid nitrogen. Performed in a necropsy suite or gross room on soft, deformable, variable specimens.

Novel or exploratory preparation: setting up a protocol that does not yet exist in the lab's automation — organoid/3D culture handling, electron-microscopy prep, primary tissue explants, one-off troubleshooting with improvised labware and shared instruments across the lab. Judgment-heavy, low-repetition work at an open bench.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plate/liquid-handling-amenable method optimization in a biomedical research or biotech lab: iteratively screening a defined parameter space (reagent formulation, media/differentiation conditions, assay buffer, PCR/ELISA conditions) over successive rounds, analyzing the resulting data, and writing up the optimized protocol for the group and a paper/poster.

Bespoke bench experimentation to develop a new laboratory method: primary tissue or patient-derived cells, custom sample prep, dissection, microscopy, blots/flow cytometry, improvised fixes when a step fails, on a shared human bench with equipment the scientist adapts; then analysis and presentation at lab meeting and a conference.

Developing instrumentation or a device for medical use (microfluidic chip, biosensor, imaging/optics rig, catheter or wearable prototype): CAD and fabrication, hand assembly, alignment and calibration, bench testing against biological samples, several redesign cycles, then presenting characterization data to collaborators and at a conference.

Preclinical in vivo procedure development in an animal facility: refining a surgical/dosing/imaging model in rodents, handling and injecting animals, tissue harvest, histology and imaging readouts, statistical analysis and presentation of the validated procedure.

Clinical/translational procedure development in a hospital or clinical research unit: piloting a new specimen-collection, imaging-acquisition or point-of-care measurement protocol with human participants and fresh clinical specimens, refining it against clinical workflow, then analyzing results and presenting to clinicians and lay/patient audiences.

Analysis-and-dissemination-dominant episode at a desk: consolidating accumulated experimental/clinical datasets, statistics and code, making figures, writing the manuscript, and presenting the findings in a conference talk and to journalists or a patient/public audience.

instances.label: Bench wet-lab investigation of physiological/disease mechanisms in cells, tissues and biospecimens at a research lab: prepare reagents, culture and treat cells, run assays (ELISA, qPCR, western blot, plate-reader metabolic/viability assays, flow cytometry), read out and interpret results to decide the next experiment. Standard labware, biosafety cabinets, institutional lab space.

Multi-week in vivo rodent model study in an institutional vivarium: identify and handle mice/rats, dose or feed an intervention, weigh and health-score animals, run behavioral/metabolic phenotyping, collect serial blood samples, then terminal necropsy and tissue harvest, with welfare judgement throughout.

Acute instrumented physiological recording from a prepared animal on a rig: anesthetized, head-fixed or stereotaxically mounted animal; advance electrodes/pipettes, obtain in vivo electrophysiology or patch-clamp recordings, deliver stimuli and log physiological responses over a session.

Human-subject measurement session in a clinical research unit or hospital: obtain venous blood samples from a seated participant and/or acquire non-invasive physiological measurements (cerebral/vascular blood flow, organ ultrasound, hemodynamics) to protocol standard, with a cooperative, positioned participant.

Complex human physiology protocol in a clinical research facility: consent and screen the volunteer, instrument them with multiple sensors (ECG leads, respiratory mask, catheters), run graded exercise or metabolic challenge testing, take biopsies or invasive hemodynamic measures, and manage the subject through the protocol.

On-site study of animal health away from the research campus: assess health, welfare and physiological indicators of a production or colony animal population in a barn, farm or veterinary facility, detecting disease signs and environmental exposures across the group over time.

tasks.label: Investigate cause, progress, life cycle, or mode of transmission of diseases or parasites.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Standardized in vitro campaign in an academic/industry research lab (BSL-2, sometimes BSL-3): plate-based infection or perturbation assays, nucleic-acid extraction, qPCR, ELISA, sequencing library prep, high-content imaging, run in microplate format with commercial reagents to test a mechanistic or transmissibility hypothesis; output is an analyzed data set with conclusions.

Bespoke mechanistic bench experiment in a shared research lab: novel constructs, primary or organoid cultures, tissue dissection, custom live-imaging or electrophysiology rigs, frequent troubleshooting and mid-course redesign, using shared human-scale equipment scattered across benches and rooms.

Animal-model infection/transmission study in a vivarium/ABSL suite: mouse, ferret or hamster inoculation, daily clinical scoring and weighing, contact-transmission cage setups, terminal bleeds, euthanasia, necropsy, organ harvest and titration.

Microscopy/histopathology characterization in the lab: making and staining blood films or tissue sections, scanning and reading slides to identify and quantify parasite life-cycle stages or infection-associated pathology.

Clinical/laboratory specimen work to establish etiology and reconstruct transmission: receiving patient or environmental specimens in a hospital or public-health lab, culture and organism identification, susceptibility testing, and genomic typing/sequencing of isolates.

Field or outbreak-site investigation: visiting endemic-area sites, farms, wetlands or affected buildings; collecting vectors (mosquitoes, ticks, snails), water/soil/wastewater samples and host specimens under variable weather and terrain, then shipping/processing them.

tasks.label: Use equipment such as atomic absorption spectrometers, electron microscopes, flow cytometers, or chromatography systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Flow cytometry batch in a research/core lab: stain a set of blood, marrow or cultured-cell samples with an established antibody panel (cocktail, lyse, wash, centrifuge), load tubes/plates on a benchtop cytometer, run QC beads and compensation, acquire events and export gated data.

Routine quantitative chromatography: prepare a batch of biological samples (dilution, protein precipitation/SPE) into vials or a plate, load the autosampler, run a validated HPLC/LC-MS/MS or GC method with calibrators and QCs, and deliver quantified results.

Electron microscopy session: prepared specimens (clipped cryo-EM grids, resin sections on grids/tape, sputter-coated SEM stubs) are loaded, the scope is aligned/focused, targets are selected and a multi-hour to multi-day image dataset is collected in a shared EM facility.

Elemental analysis of tissue, fluid or environmental samples by atomic absorption spectrometry or ICP-MS/OES: weigh and acid-digest samples, prepare calibration standards and internal standards, run the autosampler sequence, and report concentrations.

Optimization within an established instrument platform: antibody/voltage titration for a cytometry panel, chromatographic gradient or MS parameter tuning, calibration/standard-curve series, screening several sample-prep conditions to pick the best - iterative runs inside a defined parameter space on standard labware.

Non-routine instrument work: a novel or irreplaceable specimen with no established protocol, bringing up a new assay or modality, or diagnosing and fixing a misbehaving instrument (clogged cytometer fluidics or HPLC column, drifting EM alignment, leaking nebulizer) mid-experiment.

Custom subsystem build-up and integration in the instrument lab: mounting a detector in a cryostat, harness wiring and soldering, vacuum pump-down and cool-down, mechanical fit-up of one-off machined parts, and debugging readout electronics anomalies.

Design and prototype fabrication: optical/mechanical CAD, tolerance and thermal analysis, drafting, machining or 3D-printing prototype parts in the departmental shop, PCB layout for a detector controller, then checking fit and revising the design.

Instrument integration and commissioning at the telescope: transporting and mounting the instrument at the Cassegrain/Nasmyth focus, cabling and services hookup, alignment to the telescope reference, night-time on-sky testing and iterative fixes inside the dome, often at altitude.

Field or remote hardware development: radio antenna/receiver front-end work at a remote array site, or balloon/field-campaign instrument setup and repair outdoors, weather-exposed with no controlled layout.

sources.system: OptoMate (AI-driven robotics platform for free-space optics)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous assembly and alignment of tabletop free-space optics experiments. Transfers to the astronomer's bench-optics instance because the objects (catalog lenses, mirrors, mounts on a breadboard), the micrometer/arcsecond tolerances, and the lab-bench setting are the same as when an astronomer builds and characterizes a small optical train.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous build-and-align of a precision optical system on a bench. It transfers to instrument-lab optical prototyping because it covers the same closed-loop 'assemble, measure, correct until it meets spec' loop on comparable optomechanical hardware at micrometer tolerances.

instances.label: Optics/AMO/quantum-optics bench work: the physicist builds and aligns a free-space or fiber laser setup on an optical table (mirrors, lenses, polarizers, cavities, vacuum cell), tunes and locks the laser, then records spectra, interference or fluorescence data to probe atomic or photonic structure. Bespoke, frequently reconfigured apparatus in a university or corporate lab.

Condensed-matter/quantum-device measurement: mounting a sample or wafer in a cryostat, probe station or magnet system, cooling it, connecting electrical/optical lines, and running hours- to days-long transport, magnetometry or spectroscopy sweeps to observe properties of matter. Institution-run lab with standard cryogenic and measurement hardware.

Routine characterization on shared instruments in a university or industrial core facility: carrying samples to XRD, SEM, spectrometers, NMR or ellipsometers, loading holders, running the measurement recipe, and collecting and screening the data. Instruments are commercial and standard; the room is a normal human-occupied lab.

User-facility experiment: a beamtime shift at a synchrotron, neutron source, accelerator or big-laser facility. Samples/targets come in standardized holders or dewars, are exchanged into an interlocked hutch or chamber, and data are taken under remote control over shifts, with settings re-optimized between scans.

Astronomical/telescopic observing run: configuring the instrument, acquiring and guiding on targets, taking calibration and science frames through the night, and reacting to weather or transient alerts, either at the mountaintop observatory or via remote/queue operation.

Field/in-situ observation outside a controlled lab: taking spectra or radiation/atmospheric measurements at a site as found - outdoor test range, remote station, or vehicle/drone/rover-borne instrument - with targets, terrain and conditions uncontrolled.

instances.label: Routine synoptic 00Z/12Z sounding at a fixed CONUS upper-air station (NWS weather forecast office or military site): technician preps and ground-checks a radiosonde, inflates a latex balloon with hydrogen/helium in the inflation shelter, releases it, tracks the flight to burst (~30 km), and encodes/transmits the temperature, humidity and wind profile. Ordinary weather; institution-run fenced station grounds.

Routine scheduled soundings at remote or harsh fixed stations (Alaska sites, Pacific island stations, Arctic/Antarctic research bases): same procedure but with extreme cold, blowing snow or high wind, minimal on-site staff, and infrequent consumable resupply.

Special/supplemental on-demand sounding at a fixed station ahead of or during high-impact weather (severe convective outbreak, landfalling hurricane, winter storm), launched off-schedule at short notice, often at night and in gusty surface winds, with data needed immediately for models and warnings.

Sounding at a temporary field-campaign site taken as found (remote field camp, tent or trailer, portable gas cylinders, uneven ground, nearby trees/structures), with frequent launches during intensive observation periods.
Sounding launched from the deck of a research vessel underway at sea: pitching/rolling platform, strong relative wind over the deck, salt spray, limited deck space, coordination with ship's crew.

Mobile targeted sounding from a vehicle at an ad hoc roadside or open-field location (storm-chase inflow sector, wildfire, urban field study): site selected minutes beforehand, gas and power carried on the vehicle, launch into an unstructured, sometimes hazardous setting.

instances.label: Routine repeated vertical-profile flask sampling from a chartered light aircraft over a fixed reference site (greenhouse-gas network style): a 12-flask package with a compressor is carried aloft, samples are taken at pre-set altitudes during level flight, flush volumes/fill pressures and GPS/T/P metadata are logged, and the filled flasks go to a central lab.

Systematic sampling on a large research aircraft over land or ocean: whole-air canisters, flask packages and aerosol/filter samplers run on a pre-planned schedule along transects and profiles during a multi-hour mission, with a scientist aboard monitoring inlets and instrument status.

Adaptive, targeted sampling during a campaign flight: intercepting an urban, wildfire, volcanic or ship-track plume identified in real time, triggering canisters on the spot, swapping filter media mid-flight, and hands-on troubleshooting of leaking fittings, pumps or inlet lines at altitude in a cramped, turbulent cabin.

Underway marine-air sampling from a research vessel on a multi-week cruise: ambient air drawn from a bow/mast intake into automated analyzers plus discrete flask and filter samples, with sector/contamination control against stack exhaust, calibration gases, and daily checks in ship motion and salt spray.

Pre- and post-mission handling of the sampling hardware: preparing and loading evacuated flasks/canisters, bolting sampler packages and racks into the aircraft or ship lab, connecting and leak-checking inlet plumbing, then removing, labelling, packing and shipping the filled samples to the analysis lab (hangar, dock or shipboard lab).

Sampling in adverse or remote conditions from a small platform: a small boat, small aircraft or small uncrewed aircraft operated from an unimproved site to sample a plume, a storm-influenced marine boundary layer, or a remote ocean region, with conditions taken as found and improvised setup.

Non-routine investigation: unknown contaminant identification, deformulation of a competitor product, out-of-specification/failure investigation or instrument troubleshooting, requiring adaptive choice of extraction and analytical technique and expert interpretation of ambiguous chromatograms/spectra.

Analytical method development and validation: screening columns, mobile phases and detection wavelengths, running DOE optimization and robustness experiments on an LC/GC, establishing system suitability criteria and documenting the validated method.

At-line or on-site analysis at a plant floor, warehouse receiving dock or field site: sampling a process stream or drum and analyzing it with a portable/process instrument (NIR, Raman, FTIR, process GC/IC) to release material or steer the process.

tasks.label: Conduct quality control tests.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine instrumental analysis of a liquid/solution QC sample in an industrial or contract QC lab (pharma, petrochemical, environmental, specialty chemicals): sample arrives in a labelled/barcoded vial or bottle, chemist mixes, aliquots and dilutes it, filters into autosampler vials, runs HPLC/GC/ICP-OES with standards and system-suitability checks, integrates peaks, compares to specification and releases the result to LIMS.

Classical wet-chemistry and physicochemical tests on liquid samples: potentiometric titration (acid value, TAN/TBN, chloride), Karl Fischer moisture, pH, conductivity, density, refractive index. Weigh or pipette a sample portion into a beaker, add solvent, run the determination on a benchtop analyzer, clean and condition electrodes, calculate and report against spec.

QC test on a solid or heterogeneous sample: tablets/capsules, powders, polymer pellets, food, ore or soil. Requires sub-sampling and homogenizing (grinding, milling, quartering), gravimetric weighing out of a bulk container, digestion/ashing/extraction or dissolution with sonication, filtration, then an instrumental or gravimetric finish and reporting.

In-process / at-line QC: chemist goes to the production floor, draws a sample from a reactor, tank, transfer line, drum or tote through a sample port (PPE, hot or pressurized process), and either tests it at-line (pH, density, viscosity, moisture, chromatography) or carries it back to the lab for a rapid release test that gates the batch.

Performance / physical-property QC on solid product specimens: coatings draw-downs and spray panels, plastic bars, films, catalyst pellets. Specimen must be prepared, conditioned and mounted in the test instrument for gloss, color, hardness, tensile, melt-flow or particle-size measurement, with the reading judged against spec.

Non-routine QC work: out-of-specification investigation, atypical or unknown sample, method verification/transfer, instrument troubleshooting and re-preparation. The physical operations are decided on the fly and differ from the standard SOP.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-throughput QC/contract lab (pesticide, environmental, food): between sample sets on dirty matrices the chemist swaps the contaminated GC inlet liner and seal and exchanges the autosampler syringe/injection tool, then restarts the sequence so response stays within spec.

Daily pre-use calibration and conditioning of potentiometric bench devices: multipoint pH/ion electrode calibration in buffers, rinsing and conditioning the sensor, checking slope/offset against acceptance limits, and recording the result before a measurement batch.
Weighing-instrument upkeep: level and clean the analytical balance, run an adjustment, verify with external check weights against tolerance, and log the result; tag the balance if out of tolerance.

Scheduled preventive maintenance on an HPLC/UHPLC or GC: replace pump seals, pistons and check valves, change guard column/column and ferrules, replace needle seat/rotor seal and inline filters, purge and prime, leak-check, then run a system-suitability injection and document.

Unplanned malfunction mid-analysis: over-pressure or clog, solvent/vacuum leak, drifting or noisy baseline, ghost peaks, autosampler jam or cryptic error code. Chemist isolates the cause with staged tests, cleans or swaps the offending part, re-verifies performance, and escalates to a vendor service engineer if unresolved.

Deep periodic service on major instruments: venting and cleaning an MS ion source and re-tuning, roughing-pump oil change, ICP-MS torch/cones/nebulizer cleaning, NMR cryogen fill and shimming, detector lamp or flow-cell replacement.
