tasks.label: Prepare test solutions, compounds, or reagents for laboratory personnel to conduct tests.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Regulated QC lab (pharma, food, environmental): prepare a compendial reagent or reference standard solution — retrieve reagent from the chemical store, weigh dried solid on an analytical balance, quantitatively transfer and dissolve, adjust pH, dilute to the mark in a volumetric flask, filter or degas, label with expiry, and record preparation in the logbook/LIMS for analysts to use.

Industrial or academic R&D lab: prepare stock and working solutions, buffers, catalyst/reagent solutions in vials or small bottles for colleagues' experiments; varied reagents and labware, moderate accuracy, frequent recipe changes.

Prepare a calibration standard series / serial dilutions and spiking solutions from a certified stock into autosampler vials or plates so analysts can calibrate HPLC, GC or ICP instruments; accuracy-critical volumetric or gravimetric dilution, capping and labelling.

Bulk reagent preparation: make up multi-litre mobile phases, titrants, digestion acids, wash/dilution solutions or media in 4–20 L carboys — lifting solvent bottles, dissolving large solid charges with stirring, filtering and degassing, then distributing to benches.

Hazardous, air-sensitive or high-potency reagent preparation in a fume hood or glovebox: concentrated acid or peroxide reagents, moisture-sensitive titrants/electrolytes, potent API standards; containment, inert atmosphere and strict handling required.

Prepare a test compound by small-scale synthesis: run the reaction, work it up, purify (chromatography/recrystallisation), dry, verify identity/purity, and hand the isolated material over for others' testing.

aliases: Micro Electrical/Mechanical Systems Device Scientist (MEMS Device Scientist)
R and D Scientist (Research and Development Scientist)
roles.description: Research and study the structures and chemical properties of various natural and synthetic or composite materials, including metals, alloys, rubber, ceramics, semiconductors, polymers, and glass. Determine ways to strengthen or combine materials or develop new materials with new or specific properties for use in a variety of products and applications. Includes glass scientists, ceramic scientists, metallurgical scientists, and polymer scientists.

tasks.label: Conduct research on the structures and properties of materials, such as metals, alloys, polymers, and ceramics, to obtain information that could be used to develop new products or enhance existing ones.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Industrial or academic R&D lab: solution/formulation screening of polymers, coatings, electrolytes or composite resins — weighing and dispensing components, mixing formulations, casting or coating films, curing, then measuring properties (conductivity, rheology, thermal, optical) and iterating toward a target property.

Materials lab: solid-state synthesis of inorganic ceramics/glasses/oxides — weighing and milling precursor powders, pressing pellets, firing in box or tube furnaces, then X-ray diffraction/phase analysis to relate processing to structure, iterating recipes.

Metallurgical lab: alloy and metal specimens — sectioning, mounting, grinding/polishing, etching, optical/SEM microstructure and grain-size analysis, hardness and tensile/impact testing, correlating microstructure with mechanical properties.

Shared core facility or synchrotron: advanced structure characterization campaign — specimen preparation (thin sections, FIB lamellae, sample bars), instrument alignment and data collection on SEM/TEM/EBSD/XPS/diffraction, and interpretation of the structural data.

Bench work with bespoke or one-off apparatus: assembling and troubleshooting a custom rig (in-situ cell, new deposition or electrospinning setup, novel processing route), improvising fixtures and adapting the experiment as unexpected behavior appears.

Plant floor, pilot line, or field/customer site: sampling material from production or from a failed component in service, on-site observation and portable measurements, and scale-up trials under uncontrolled conditions.

tasks.label: Test metals to determine conformance to specifications of mechanical strength, strength-weight ratio, ductility, magnetic and electrical properties, and resistance to abrasion, corrosion, heat, and cold.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine conformance tensile testing in a company or contract materials lab: a batch of machined metal coupons (sheet, bar, plate, forging, or AM build) is measured for cross-section, gripped in a universal testing machine, pulled to failure with an extensometer, and yield strength, UTS, elongation, and r/n values are reported against ASTM E8 / ISO 6892 specification limits.

Hardness and metallographic conformance work in a met lab: a sample is sectioned and mounted, ground, polished and etched, then a Rockwell/Brinell bulk hardness or Vickers microhardness traverse is run for case depth, and grain size/phase content are measured on the microscope and reported against the specification.

Toughness and wear testing: Charpy V-notch specimens conditioned in a low-temperature bath and struck within 5 s per ASTM E23 (absorbed energy, lateral expansion, shear area), plus abrasion/wear-resistance runs on lab tribometers or pin-on-disk/abrasion rigs with mass-loss and friction reporting.

Magnetic and electrical property conformance: core loss and permeability of electrical steel by Epstein frame or single-sheet tester to IEC 60404, conductivity/resistivity checks, and eddy-current structure/hardness verification of production lots against specified property limits.

Corrosion and environmental resistance testing by chamber exposure: coupons and parts are cleaned, edge-masked, racked at specified angles and loaded into a salt-fog/cyclic-corrosion/humidity or hot-cold soak chamber, inspected periodically over hundreds of hours, then removed, corrosion products cleaned off, and rated (creepage, red rust, mass loss) against the spec.

On-site verification of metal outside the test lab: positive material identification with handheld XRF/LIBS on incoming bar, pipe or plate in a receiving area or fabrication shop, portable hardness checks on welds or installed components, and sorting of mixed or suspect lots for heat-treat/alloy conformance.

tasks.label: Test material samples for tolerance under tension, compression, and shear to determine the cause of metal failures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Materials/metallurgical lab: batch of standard machined tension coupons (ASTM E8 / ISO 6892) cut from a suspect heat, lot, or weld. Worker measures cross-sections, mounts each coupon in wedge/hydraulic grips, attaches an extensometer, runs to fracture, and compares yield/UTS/elongation against spec to show whether the material met tolerance.

Lab: sections taken from a failed or suspect part are mounted, ground, polished and etched, then subjected to a macro/micro hardness traverse (Rockwell/Vickers case-depth or weld HAZ survey) to check for improper heat treatment, decarburization or over-hardening as the failure cause.

Lab: compression and shear tolerance tests on prepared metal specimens and small components - compression cylinders/tube crush, double-shear pin or fastener shear, punch-shear coupons - run on a universal testing machine with the appropriate standard fixture, to compare measured strength with design allowables.

Lab: temperature- or rate-dependent tolerance testing of a specimen set to explain a brittle or hot-service failure - Charpy V-notch transition curve over a series of conditioning temperatures, or elevated/low-temperature tension tests in a furnace/chamber.

Full failure investigation of a fractured field-returned component (shaft, bracket, casting, pipe): scientist decides where to sample relative to the fracture, sections the irregular part, has sub-size tension/compression/shear specimens machined, tests them, and correlates the mechanical results with fracture-surface features into a cause determination.

On-site work at a customer plant, refinery, or structure: in-situ evaluation of a failed component using portable hardness testers, in-place sampling (boat samples), and selection/removal of material for later laboratory tension and shear testing.

instances.label: Lab-scale ceramic/inorganic processing study: in a corporate or national-lab materials lab, weigh and mill precursor powders, mix binder, press pellets or cast bodies, load crucibles/setters into a box or tube furnace, run a firing schedule (800–1600 °C, controlled atmosphere), then measure density/phase/microstructure and revise the next batch of processing conditions.

Polymer/composite or thin-film processing trials: compound or dissolve resin, cast/spin/blade-coat films or hot-press plaques, cure or anneal at set temperature-time profiles, then measure thickness, defects, conductivity or mechanical properties and iterate the processing window.

Glass/optical materials melt study: batch and mix oxide raw materials, melt in a crucible furnace up to ~1500–1700 °C, cast and anneal the melt, then cut/polish specimens and measure Tg, modulus, transmission or devitrification to refine the melting and annealing process.

Pilot- or production-scale process trial: at a pilot plant or plant line, run a scale-up campaign (batch prep, forming/pressing/casting, kiln or heat-treat cycle, machining), pull samples, and adjust process parameters between runs with plant engineers.

Non-routine, hands-on process development: building or modifying a bespoke rig (custom die, fixture, furnace atmosphere setup), hand-forming an odd-geometry prototype (a plate, a lens blank, a dental-filling mock-up), troubleshooting a failed run, or glovebox/hazardous-material work with improvised setups.

instances.label: Computational study of an alloy's behavior at a workstation/HPC cluster: DFT or molecular-dynamics calculations of defect and deformation energetics, CALPHAD phase-stability screening, or finite-element/crystal-plasticity simulation of a component's response to applied loads; output is analyzed data, plots and a written interpretation. Occurs at a desk in a corporate or university research facility.

Mechanical testing of prepared metal specimens in a materials test lab: retrieve machined tensile/compression/fatigue coupons, measure cross-sections, mount them in wedge or pneumatic grips of a universal test frame, fit an extensometer, run the standard method (e.g., ASTM E8 / ISO 6892), plus Rockwell/Vickers hardness; record and reduce the stress-strain data.

Metallographic preparation and microstructural characterization: abrasive-section a coupon, hot-mount it, grind and polish through successive abrasive steps, etch, then image on an optical microscope or SEM (with EDS/EBSD) and quantify grain size, phases, porosity or fracture features. Lab bench with saw, mounting press, polisher, fume hood, microscopes.

Alloy synthesis and thermal processing: weigh out elemental charges or powders, melt/cast (arc melter, induction furnace) or print a composition by laser deposition, then homogenize, solution-treat, age or quench in box/tube furnaces, tracking temperatures and times. Performed in a lab or pilot-scale metals processing bay with furnaces, gloveboxes and quench baths.

Diffraction and spectroscopy characterization: mount samples in an X-ray diffractometer for phase and residual-stress analysis, run optical-emission or XRF composition analysis, or run an in-situ loading/heating experiment on a lab or beamline instrument; then index patterns and fit the data. Instrument room of a research or plant laboratory.

instances.label: Quarterly groundwater monitoring event at a landfill, UST or remediation site: drive to 10-30 wells scattered over the property, unlock and open well caps, gauge depth to water, purge with a low-flow pump until field parameters stabilize, fill/preserve/label bottles, complete chain of custody, then validate lab data and report.

Broad-acre georeferenced soil sampling of open ground (farm fields, large land parcels, land-application areas): traverse a sampling grid, pull cores at GPS points, composite and bag labeled samples, ship to the lab, then map and interpret nutrient/contaminant results.

Contaminated-site, sediment or spill soil and waste sampling: hand auger or direct-push cores at set depth intervals on a brownfield, industrial yard or streambed, PID field screening, VOC-preserved jars, boring logs, working around pavement, debris and buried utilities; then data tables and a site investigation report.

Facility or building contaminant survey round: traverse a plant fenceline/process area or the rooms of a building with gas, particulate or radiation instruments, record concentrations at set points, localize leaks or hot spots, and deliver a mapped measurement report.

instances.label: Routine weekly and rain-event erosion & sediment control (SWPPP/NPDES construction general permit) inspection at an active land-development or highway construction site: walk the disturbed acreage over mud, spoil piles and steep slopes among moving equipment; judge whether each BMP (silt fence trenched in, inlet protection, stabilized entrance, check dams, basin risers) is installed and functioning; look for off-site sediment tracking or discharge; take turbidity/pH readings at discharging outfalls; photo-document and issue a signed inspection report with corrective actions and deadlines.

Water, sediment and soil sampling around a development: collect surface-water grab samples upstream/downstream of the project in streams and wetlands, or purge and sample groundwater monitoring wells at a site under construction; record field parameters with a multiparameter sonde; filter/preserve, label and ice bottles, complete chain-of-custody and deliver to the lab within hold times. Streambanks, ditches, brush, uneven ground.

Perimeter air (PM10/PM2.5, dust deposition), noise and vibration monitoring at a development, quarry or plant expansion: site and level the monitors, run calibrations, swap filters/media and batteries, download loggers, note weather and site activity, and compare readings against permit action levels.

Fugitive-emission / gas surface-emission compliance survey at an operator-controlled facility associated with energy or waste development: component-level optical gas imaging of an oil & gas production pad, or grid-pattern methane surface emissions monitoring across a landfill cell, producing a regulator-accepted survey record of detected emission points.

Ground-based ecological and habitat monitoring in and adjacent to the development footprint: vegetation plots and revegetation/mitigation success counts, wetland hydrology and hydric-soil checks, invasive species mapping, and protected-species or nest surveys, with species-level identification and a monitoring memo.

Scheduled remote-sensing monitoring pass over the project footprint for the compliance record: repeat aerial imagery/orthomosaic and change mapping of disturbance extent versus the approved limits of disturbance, stabilization and cover, stockpiles and sediment basin status, delivered as georeferenced imagery and measured areas to the project file.

instances.label: Spill/release at an industrial or commercial facility (tank overfill, transformer oil release, truck-offload spill at a terminal or plant). Scientist mobilizes within hours, walks the affected yard/containment area, photographs and sketches extent, screens with PID/multi-gas meter, collects soil and water grab samples with hand tools under chain of custody, interviews operators, estimates volume released and reportability, and writes an incident investigation report with cause and corrective actions.

Release into open terrain or a waterway (pipeline rupture, tank-battery or produced-water release, discharge found in a ditch or stream) in rural, wooded or muddy ground. Scientist traverses banks and uneven terrain, delineates the affected footprint, collects water, sediment and soil samples at multiple points, checks receptors (wells, wetlands, fish kills), photo-documents, and prepares an agency-facing incident report.

Transportation accident with hazardous materials (highway tanker rollover, rail derailment, truck fire). Scientist works an active scene under incident command with responders, identifies product from placards/manifests, performs downwind and perimeter air monitoring, checks storm drains and ditches for runoff, collects samples where safe, advises on protective actions, then writes the release-notification and investigation report.

Indoor accidental release in a building (ammonia or solvent release in a plant, laboratory chemical or mercury spill in a school, refrigerant release). Scientist conducts indoor air monitoring, collects wipe/bulk samples, interviews occupants, determines exposure and re-occupancy/clearance, and issues an incident report with corrective recommendations.

Marine or large open-water spill (vessel grounding, offshore platform or terminal release). Scientist supports overflight/vessel-based assessment, shoreline assessment of oiling, collects surface water and shoreline samples, tracks the slick, and contributes an assessment report for the response and damage-assessment record.

Desk-based investigation of a reported accident with no field visit: reviewing operator logs, SDS, monitoring and telemetry data, photographs and witness statements, calculating the quantity released, determining regulatory reportability, and drafting the written incident report and notification.

instances.label: Bench-scale treatability/abatement experiments in the employer's or a university laboratory: preparing dosing series and reagents, running jar tests, sorption isotherms, column or microcosm/photocatalytic degradation tests on water, sludge or soil-slurry samples, taking timed aliquots, measuring turbidity/COD/contaminant residuals, and iterating conditions until an effective treatment condition is identified.

Laboratory sample preparation and instrumental analysis supporting the research: logging and weighing samples, filtration, extraction/digestion, dilution and spiking, loading autosamplers on GC-MS/ICP/IC, running calibration and QA/QC blanks and duplicates, and generating the analytical dataset for the study.

Pilot- or demonstration-scale trial of a treatment or abatement process at a wastewater plant, drinking-water plant or industrial site: installing/commissioning a skid or reactor on a real side-stream, operating it for weeks, varying dose/flow/residence time, pulling influent and effluent samples, cleaning fouled surfaces, and evaluating performance.

Source-characterization / performance measurement campaign at an institution-controlled facility (refinery, gas production pad, landfill, plant): surveying and quantifying emissions or discharges before and after abatement measures, at fixed and repeatable measurement points, and reporting quantified results to a regulatory-grade standard.

Field research at unstructured outdoor sites: contaminated-site soil and groundwater sampling from monitoring wells, surface-water and sediment sampling, ambient air sampling, installing and monitoring in-situ amendment or bioremediation trial plots, over uneven terrain, variable weather, site-specific access and chain-of-custody handling.

Desk-based study episodes: literature and regulatory synthesis, experimental/sampling design, statistical analysis and process or fate-and-transport modeling of collected data, and preparation of the technical report, journal paper or recommendation memo that is the accepted output of the research.

sources.claim: A mobile robot autonomously ran a multi-day closed-loop experimental campaign in an ordinary chemistry laboratory, choosing its own experiments with a Bayesian optimizer and finding photocatalyst mixtures six times more active for hydrogen production from water.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bench-scale aqueous photocatalysis optimisation. Same physical operations as bench treatability research (dispensing solids and liquids into vials, mixing, sparging, timed sampling, instrument measurement) on aqueous mixtures, in a human laboratory, with the robot selecting successive experimental conditions.

sources.system: Autonomous mobile robotic chemists (mobile manipulators, Dai et al.)
sources.title: Autonomous Mobile Robots for Exploratory Synthetic Chemistry (Nature 635:890-897) - repository record
sources.claim: Two mobile robots autonomously carried out exploratory synthetic chemistry in a shared human laboratory, operating standard analytical instruments (UPLC-MS, NMR, photoreactor) and making decisions from multiple measurements without redesigning the lab.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: exploratory bench chemistry with instrumental characterisation. Sample handling, reaction set-up, operating analytical instruments and acting on the data are the same manipulations and precision required for laboratory treatability experiments and their analytical work-up, in a standard human lab.

sources.system: A-Lab

sources.title: Google DeepMind Adds Nearly 400,000 New Compounds to Berkeley Lab's Materials Project
sources.claim: An autonomous laboratory planned, executed and interpreted solid-state synthesis experiments continuously for 17 days in a purpose-built robotic cell, making dozens of new compounds; a later correction disputed some product assignments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous materials synthesis research. Demonstrates a full experiment-analyse-decide research loop executed by robots in a fenced, purpose-built cell, the E1 analogue of bench research on sorbents or catalysts used for pollution abatement.

sources.system: RoboChem (and RoboChem-Flex)
sources.title: RoboChem Flex: Democratisation of the autonomous synthesis robot
sources.claim: An autonomous benchtop continuous-flow platform optimises reaction conditions on a real flowing process stream, using in-line NMR analysis and a machine-learning optimiser to choose the next operating conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous optimisation of a continuous chemical process. A pilot treatment trial is the same activity (vary flow, dose and residence time on a running stream, measure the output, decide the next setting), shown done autonomously when the process is plumbed into a purpose-built rig with in-line analysis.

sources.system: Percepto autonomous OGI drone system
sources.title: Autonomous Methane Detection Drones Earn EPA Approval for Oil and Gas Compliance
sources.claim: Autonomous drone-in-a-box optical gas imaging systems fly repeatable emission surveys at oil and gas facilities, detect and quantify methane releases and generate compliance-grade reports; EPA approved the system as an Alternative Test ... and operators use it in daily operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: quantitative emissions source characterisation at a facility. This is the field-measurement core of applied research on emission abatement - locating and quantifying pollutant sources at controlled sites and delivering a defensible quantified dataset and report.

sources.system: Robot Scientist 'Adam'
sources.developer: Aberystwyth University / University of Cambridge (King et al.)
sources.title: The Automation of Science (Science 324:85-89)
sources.claim: The Robot Scientist Adam autonomously generated hypotheses, designed and executed the experiments to test them, and interpreted the results, within an integrated purpose-built laboratory robot system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hypothesis-driven laboratory research. Establishes that a closed research cycle (hypothesis, experiment design, execution, interpretation) can be run by a robotic system in an enclosed purpose-built automated lab, the E1 case for applied bench research.

instances.label: Wetland/jurisdictional habitat assessment on a parcel proposed for development or mitigation credit release: walk the tract as found, dig soil pits and auger borings to read hydric-soil indicators, run vegetation plots and species ID, check hydrology indicators, flag and GPS boundaries, photo-document, then produce the delineation/certification report.

Periodic monitoring assessment of a small-to-mid restoration site (2-50 acres riparian planting, wetland mitigation site, urban prairie): plot- and transect-based survival counts under shelters and shrub canopy, percent cover, invasive species search, erosion and hydrology checks, fixed photo points, judged against performance standards.

Large-area rehabilitation/vegetation condition survey (mine reclamation lease, rangeland, mangrove, post-fire landscape; hundreds to thousands of hectares) where the deliverable is mapped ground cover, species composition, weed infestations and erosion features scored against completion criteria for regulatory sign-off.

Contaminated-site or damage assessment (brownfield, spill, illegal fill, post-flood): reconnaissance walk of a cluttered site as found, field screening with PID/XRF, judgment-based selection of soil, sediment and water sampling points, collecting and preserving samples with chain of custody, documenting conditions for the remedial-need determination.

Stream/riparian aquatic habitat assessment for restoration design or effectiveness monitoring: wading the channel to take cross-sections and pebble counts, scoring bank stability and in-stream cover, kick-net macroinvertebrate sampling, water quality readings, mapping headcuts and barriers.

Coastal or submerged habitat condition survey (seagrass bed, oyster reef, nearshore benthic or coral habitat) to establish baseline condition or document damage: systematic imagery/mapping transects over the bottom, condition scoring of the habitat, delivered as a benthic condition assessment.

instances.label: Compliance oversight walkthrough of an active soil-removal/demolition remediation site (brownfield or Superfund cleanup): verify excavation limits and work-plan conformance, dust suppression and air-monitoring stations, exclusion zones and PPE, stockpile covers, decontamination and truck loadout; take photos, complete a checklist, raise deficiencies with the contractor. Layout changes daily; heavy equipment and crews active.

Inspection of an ecological restoration site under construction or in the establishment period (wetland, stream bank, riparian planting): check grading and hydrology, planting density and survival, invasive encroachment, bank stabilization and in-stream structures, erosion-control blankets, browse protection; walk uneven natural terrain in variable weather and record findings against permit conditions.

Routine compliance/operational inspection of an operating remediation treatment compound at a facility (pump-and-treat, soil vapor extraction, air stripper, bioreactor): fenced pad or building with fixed equipment; read gauges and flow totalizers, check pumps, piping and blowers for leaks, verify secondary containment, alarms, discharge point and signage, note deviations from permit operating limits.

Periodic O&M compliance inspection of a capped/closed site or mine reclamation area (landfill cap, capped Superfund unit, reclaimed tailings area): survey cover for erosion rills, settlement, cracks, burrowing, vegetative cover, leachate seeps, gas vents, surface methane emissions, perimeter security and monitoring-well condition across tens of acres of graded, vegetated ground.

Stormwater and erosion/sediment control compliance inspection (SWPPP/NPDES) during or after a rain event at an active remediation site: inspect silt fences, wattles, inlet protection, sediment basins, stabilized entrances and discharge outfalls; observe discharge clarity, note failures needing repair, complete the regulatory inspection form within the required window.

Transfers to inspecting an operating remediation treatment compound because the objects (valves, piping, blowers, tanks), the leak/deviation findings, and the fenced facility environment are comparable, and the output is an accepted compliance record.

instances.label: Exploratory field study at an operating industrial facility (factory, refinery, recycler): tour production lines with a host engineer, log energy/material inputs from meters and plant records, characterize and sample waste and by-product streams, take improvised spot measurements and photographs, interview operators, and reconcile findings into a material/energy flow inventory for the study.

Repeat monitoring rounds inside a facility over a multi-week study period: follow a fixed route through process areas, capture gauge/meter readings, thermal, acoustic and gas measurements at designated points, and log a consistent time series of process/emission data into the study database.

Prescribed-point sampling campaign on open ground: drive/walk a georeferenced grid across farmland, reclaimed land or ground around an industrial site, extract soil cores to a set depth, bag, label and log each sample with GPS coordinates, and deliver the batch to the analytical lab.

Aquatic field campaign in a receiving water body near industrial or agricultural activity: run transects on a lake, reservoir or large river, log in-situ water-quality parameters, collect and preserve water samples at chosen locations, and return near-real-time data for the study; weather and boat traffic vary.

Terrestrial ecological and site-instrumentation field work: lay out plots/transects in semi-natural or disturbed habitat near industrial land, count and identify species, assess vegetation and habitat condition, and install, calibrate, service and download dataloggers, air/dust monitors and flow meters scattered across the site.

Planning the field research at the desk: framing questions and hypotheses, designing the sampling scheme and QA/QC protocol, negotiating site access and permits, building equipment and staffing lists, and scheduling the campaign; output is an approved written field research plan.

instances.label: Phase II environmental / geotechnical site investigation at a commercial, industrial or roadside site: mobilize a direct-push or hollow-stem auger rig, site and clear each boring, describe and log soil/rock as it comes up, collect discrete soil samples into jars/liners, install and develop monitoring wells, then purge and sample groundwater with field parameters and chain-of-custody. Terrain, utilities, pavement, brush and weather taken as found.

Geologic field mapping and outcrop/rock sampling on foot in remote or rugged terrain (mineral exploration, USGS/state survey, academic): traverse the ground, identify lithology and alteration, measure structural orientations, break fresh rock with a hammer, bag and label representative samples, photograph and record station notes and GPS positions over a multi-day campaign.

Ground geophysical acquisition that requires placing and coupling instruments on a planned line or grid: planting geophones/nodal seismometers, driving resistivity/IP electrodes and reeling cable, occupying gravity and GNSS stations with leveling and repeat readings, dragging GPR antennas over rough ground, with daily QC of the acquired records.

Systematic geochemical sampling program on open, vehicle-accessible ground (farm field, brownfield surface soils, pediment or till plain): pull georeferenced soil/auger cores to a prescribed depth on a designed grid, bag, label and log hundreds of samples per day with QA/QC duplicates, then ship to the lab.

Survey acquisition from a mobile sensor platform over a planned survey block: UAV magnetometer/radiometric/LiDAR-photogrammetric lines over open terrain or a mine, LiDAR mapping of inaccessible workings, or offshore multibeam/sub-bottom/magnetometer lines over a marine block; the geoscientist designs line spacing and altitude/depth and QCs the returned data.

Exploration or grade-control drilling program at a mine or exploration camp: holes drilled on the planned pattern, then the returns handled at the core shed - core laid in trays, recovery/RQD measured, core photographed and logged for lithology, alteration and structure, assay intervals marked, cut and bagged with standards and blanks inserted.

instances.label: Field traverse and outcrop work: geologist hikes or drives to rough/remote terrain (rangeland, desert, forest, road cuts, coastal exposures, fossil localities), locates outcrops, examines rock with hand lens and acid, measures strike/dip with compass, photographs and describes units, hammers off fresh samples, bags/labels them and records observations on a map or GIS tablet.

Site investigation: geologist stands at a drill rig, direct-push probe, hand auger or test pit on an environmental/geotechnical site (industrial yard, brownfield, roadway, landfill), recovers soil and rock from each interval, describes and classifies it (texture, color, moisture, USCS), screens with a PID, selects and preserves samples for the lab, and writes the boring log.

Systematic soil/sediment sampling on a grid over open, vehicle-accessible ground (regional soil geochemistry, reclamation or land-use monitoring, agricultural or floodplain terrain): drive to georeferenced points, extract cores to a set depth, composite, bag and barcode for laboratory analysis.

Core and cuttings logging at a core shed, wellsite core facility or state core repository: lay out trays, describe lithology/alteration/veining, measure RQD and structural angles, photograph, mark and cut sample intervals, and record a continuous log with sub-samples sent for assay.

Laboratory examination, measurement and classification of submitted samples: crushing/pulverizing/mounting or thin-section prep, optical microscopy, XRD/XRF, SEM-EDS automated mineralogy, mineral identification and modal classification, and recording of quantitative results.

Operating mine or quarry: mapping a freshly blasted bench or underground face, logging lithology and mineralization on the exposure, taking chip/channel or grab samples for grade control, in dust, water and traffic under an active production schedule.

sources.system: Rogo SmartCore autonomous soil sampler

sources.transferJustification: Related task: agronomic grid soil sampling. The physical act is the same as a geoscientist's systematic soil-geochemical survey — navigate to georeferenced grid points on open ground, extract soil cores to a fixed depth, composite and bag them for laboratory analysis; same material, same depth/location precision, same taken-as-found outdoor terrain.

tasks.label: Study historical climate change indicators found in locations, such as ice sheets or rock formations to develop climate change models.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Desk/office instance: a paleoclimate scientist compiles existing proxy records (ice-core isotope series, PAGES2k/NOAA paleo databases, published speleothem and marine records), performs statistical analysis and age-model work, runs and tunes climate model simulations (e.g., CESM/PMIP experiments), compares model output with the proxy evidence, and writes up the resulting model/reconstruction. Work occurs at a workstation with computing-cluster access; no sample handling.

Laboratory instance (judgment-heavy portion): in a core repository cold room or sediment lab, the geoscientist selects depth intervals from an archived ice, sediment, speleothem or coral core, cuts/subsamples them, washes and sieves sediment, picks and weighs specific foraminifera species under a microscope, cleans carbonates, and decides what is contaminated or unusable before analysis. Heterogeneous natural material, variable preservation, protocols adapted per core.

Laboratory instance (protocolized batch measurement): a prepared tray/carousel of weighed proxy samples (carbonate microfossils, speleothem powders, water aliquots) is run as an overnight or multi-hour batch on an automated preparation device coupled to an isotope-ratio mass spectrometer or ICP-MS, interleaved with standards, yielding a calibrated proxy data series for the loaded batch. Standard equipment, fixed benchtop workflow in a stable-isotope lab.

Terrestrial field instance: a campaign at rock formations, caves or lake basins - hiking to outcrops, measuring and logging stratigraphic sections, identifying climate indicators (paleosols, loess, glacial dropstones, lake varves, speleothem growth), photographing and sketching, hammering and bagging oriented samples, recording GPS/context. Rough natural terrain, weather-dependent, layout differs at every site.

Polar/glacier field instance: a season at a remote ice-sheet or glacier camp - operating an ice-core drill and handling, logging and packing core sections in a drill trench or snow shelter, digging and sampling snow pits/firn, towing radar for internal-layer stratigraphy, all in sub-zero conditions with crevasse hazards and improvised camp infrastructure.

Shipboard/large-drilling-program instance: aboard a scientific drilling vessel or at an onshore core-repository science party (IODP-style), recovering cores, curating and splitting sections, running them through automated multisensor logging tracks, then visually describing lithology, making smear slides, and building a preliminary paleoclimate stratigraphy on a 12-hour shift schedule. Standard shipboard lab layout, institution-controlled.

sources.system: Forabot
sources.developer: North Carolina State University (Lobaton, Richmond et al.)

sources.claim: Forabot is a bench robot with AI vision that physically isolates and images individual foraminifera from processed marine-sediment samples - a single prep step of marine paleoclimate proxy work - at 27 forams/hour and 79% identification accuracy, described by its authors as a proof-of-concept prototype.
sources.transferJustification: Foram picking is the standard sample-preparation step for generating marine paleoclimate proxy records; it shows one manipulation step of the lab instance is automatable, but only at prototype accuracy and without interval selection, geochemical measurement, or interpretation.

sources.system: Thermo Scientific Kiel IV Carbonate Device + Delta V Plus IRMS

sources.transferJustification: Geochemical proxy measurement batches (water isotopes, trace elements) are run on exactly this class of autosampler/prep robot, so the demonstrated capability transfers to the protocolized batch-measurement instance.

instances.label: Geotechnical / engineering-geology site investigation for a public works or development project (highway, bridge, dam, school, landfill): mobilize to a raw or partly built parcel, direct and observe drilling of soil borings and test pits, log soil and rock in the field, run in-situ tests (SPT, packer), collect and preserve samples, then evaluate foundation, groundwater and seismic conditions and issue recommendations. Terrain, weather, traffic and buried utilities vary site to site.

Field reconnaissance and geologic mapping / geohazard assessment for regional development or route selection: traverse hillsides, road cuts, stream banks and outcrops on foot and by vehicle, identify units and structures, measure strike/dip, evaluate landslide, fault, karst, expansive-soil or subsidence hazards, take photos, GPS points and samples, and compile a site geology map with hazard findings.

Near-surface geophysical survey over a proposed site or alignment (seismic refraction/MASW, electrical resistivity, GPR, gravity or ground magnetics): lay out lines across fields, brownfields or road shoulders, plant geophones/electrodes or tow the antenna, operate source and recorder, QC in the field, then process and deliver depth-to-bedrock, velocity (Vs30) or void/utility interpretations.

Office-based (desk) study for site selection or regional planning: compile existing geologic maps, boring databases, LiDAR/aerial imagery and well records in GIS, run models (slope stability, seismic hazard, resource or settlement), interpret constraints, and write the report, figures and recommendations used by planners, agencies and permitting bodies.

Marine / nearshore geophysical route or site survey for a public-works or energy project (port deepening, bridge crossing, submarine cable or outfall route, offshore wind lease): run planned survey lines with multibeam, sub-bottom profiler and magnetometer over open water, and deliver a seabed characterization dataset for routing and siting decisions.

Airborne/UAV survey of a project site or corridor for site characterization: fly pre-planned lines with LiDAR/photogrammetry or a drone-borne magnetometer over the site, produce a bare-earth terrain model or magnetic map used to identify structures, fill, or geologic contacts for siting decisions.

tasks.label: Measure characteristics of the Earth, such as gravity or magnetic fields, using equipment such as seismographs, gravimeters, torsion balances, or magnetometers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Land seismic instrumentation: siting, installing and servicing seismographs/geophones — burying and levelling a broadband seismometer at a remote temporary station, laying a refraction/MASW spread, planting nodal recorders on an exploration or microseismic monitoring grid, then recovering data. Rough ground, vegetation, weather, variable soils.

Ground magnetic survey of a site or property: walking or cart-towing a proton/cesium magnetometer with a base station along staked lines over a mineral claim, brownfield, archaeological area or suspected UXO ground; brush, fences, cultural noise; produces a gridded TMI/gradient map.

Airborne geophysical survey over a property or region: planning line spacing and drape, operating a magnetometer (± radiometrics, ± airborne gravity) from a drone or aircraft over hilly, forested or desert terrain, and QC-ing the flown data into levelled maps.

Gravity survey on the ground: occupying dozens of stations with a relative gravimeter (CG-6/Burris) on a tripod — levelling, reading, repeat base-station ties, precise elevation control — for microgravity void/cavity work, reservoir monitoring or regional/geodetic control; roadside, farmland, volcano flanks.

Marine/waterborne geophysical survey: towing a marine magnetometer, running sub-bottom profiler/multibeam or shipborne gravimeter along planned lines offshore or on a lake/river, or deploying seabed sensors, with weather, currents and traffic to contend with.

Indoor/laboratory measurement: running cores and hand samples through magnetic susceptibility, remanence (cryogenic magnetometer), density and velocity instruments in a core lab or campus lab, plus calibrating and drift-testing field gravimeters and seismometers on a pier.

instances.label: Sand-and-gravel prospect evaluation for an aggregate producer: geologist screens geologic maps, LiDAR and aerial imagery, then walks a rural property (pasture, brush, river terraces, floodplain), sites and logs auger holes and backhoe test pits, describes stratigraphy, collects representative bulk samples for gradation/quality testing, interprets lab data and delineates a usable deposit.

Hard-rock quarry (crushed stone) evaluation: geologist examines bedrock outcrops, road cuts and existing faces in rough terrain, designs and supervises a core drilling program, logs core for lithology, weathering and deleterious zones, selects intervals for LA abrasion, sulfate soundness and ASR testing, and judges suitability for concrete aggregate or base course.

State DOT / highway project materials source identification: geologist reconnoiters potential borrow, base-course and riprap sources along an alignment or on adjacent private land, digs or directs shallow test pits, takes hand samples, checks material against specification limits, and approves or rejects the source.

State geological survey regional industrial-minerals mapping: geologist makes field stops across a county (outcrops, stream cuts, active and abandoned pits) on varied private and public land, describes and hand-samples units, and compiles a GIS aggregate-resource map for land-use planning.

Sample-level suitability determination in a materials/petrographic laboratory: geologist performs petrographic examination (ASTM C295) of aggregate samples and thin sections, identifies chert, clay, weathered or alkali-silica-reactive constituents, reviews physical test data, and issues a written suitability opinion.

Site visit at an operating pit or due-diligence evaluation of a property for purchase: geologist walks active benches, faces and stockpiles inside an operator-controlled quarry, maps face variability, identifies clay seams and overburden problems, samples faces and stockpiles, and assesses whether remaining material meets aggregate specs.

instances.label: Open-pit grade control: after a bench is blasted, the mine geologist walks/drives the bench and pit face, maps lithology, alteration and structure onto the bench plan, reconciles with blasthole assays, then flags or spray-paints the ore/waste dig lines and polygons for the shovel crew. Dusty, uneven blasted muck, active haul equipment, changing bench layout every shift.

Underground face mapping at active headings: after a round is blasted and mucked, the geologist goes to the face, sketches/logs lithologic contacts, veins, faults and joint sets, takes compass-clinometer orientations, collects chip or grab samples for assay, notes ground conditions and water, and records the face sheet for the level plan. Wet, muddy, dark headings that advance daily.

Mine technical office: designing and drafting geological mine maps and models in Vulcan/Leapfrog/Surpac/Deswik — level plans, cross-sections, ore wireframes, block-model updates from drillhole and face data — for mine planning and regulatory submissions. Desk work at a computer.

Underground excavation monitoring: scanning stope voids, drawpoints, orepasses and drifts to produce as-built void models, measure overbreak/dilution, and run change detection/convergence comparisons against earlier scans to flag deformation or fall-of-ground risk; reporting findings to the ground-control team. Includes inaccessible or recently failed ground.

Open-pit and surface structural integrity monitoring: keeping slope stability radar, prism/robotic-total-station arrays and drone survey coverage on pit walls, highwalls, waste dumps and tailings dams; reviewing continuous deformation data, setting alarm thresholds, and issuing movement/evacuation advisories. Monitoring stations on benches plus a control room feed.

Advising and monitoring mining crews on the ground: briefing jumbo, drill and loader operators on where the ore contact lies and how the next round should be taken, checking that development follows the geological plan, answering questions about ground conditions during the shift, and calling for extra support or a stand-down when conditions look bad.

instances.label: Routine construction observation on a building or site-development project: the engineering geologist walks the open excavation, evaluates the footing subgrade and cut/fill slopes, probes and hand-tests soils (pocket penetrometer, hand auger, probe rod), checks for undocumented fill, soft spots and seepage, and issues a field report accepting or rejecting the exposed conditions against the design assumptions. Active site with equipment, mud, changing layout.

On-site supervision and logging of exploratory drilling at a project: directing a truck/track-mounted auger, sonic or core rig, running SPT/split-spoon and Shelby sampling, classifying each recovered sample by hand (texture, plasticity, moisture, consistency), recording blow counts, drilling-rate behavior, caving and groundwater, collecting samples for lab, and producing the signed boring log.

Earthwork quality-control testing during construction: in-place compaction/density tests with a nuclear gauge or equivalent on engineered fill and subgrade, moisture checks, observing proof-rolls, and giving pass/fail direction to the contractor at multiple lifts across an open, muddy, traffic-heavy earthwork site.

Investigating an emergent engineering problem on a live project: slope movement, wall or foundation settlement and cracking, sinkhole or karst void, unexpected rock or artesian groundwater. Reconnaissance mapping of the distress, reading instrumentation (inclinometers, piezometers, survey prisms), spot tests, and a rapid diagnosis and remediation recommendation so work can resume.

Geologic mapping of an underground or dam/bridge foundation excavation during construction: mapping the tunnel heading or cleaned rock foundation, measuring discontinuity orientations and spacing, assigning rock-mass classification (RMR/Q), and recommending support or foundation treatment. Dusty, dim, cramped active heading with blasting/mucking cycles.

Marine or remote-access investigation for a construction project (bridge over water, offshore wind foundation, pipeline landfall): supervising vessel- or barge-based borings and cone penetration testing, logging recovered cores onboard, and interpreting the stratigraphy for the foundation designer, under weather and vessel-motion constraints.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous construction-site progress/QA documentation. It establishes that robots can move and capture 3D/visual data unaided on E3 job sites, but the geoscientist's task requires hand-testing soils, running penetration or density tests, drilling, and rendering an engineering judgment on subsurface conditions — none of which this system does, so the transfer fails.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous production drilling. It shows drilling machinery itself can be run without an operator on a prepared mine bench, but the geoscientist instance requires sample recovery, hand classification, groundwater and drilling-behaviour observation and a signed log/interpretation, which these rigs neither produce nor attempt.

It falls short because the scanner supplies guidance datasets for a geologist who still classifies the material, and it handles rock core only — not the soil sampling, groundwater and field-behaviour observations that make up a geotechnical boring log.

instances.label: Mine-site or commercial assay laboratory: a batch of drill-chip or pulp rock samples is dried, crushed, split, pulverized, pressed/fused and analysed by XRF (or digested for ICP), with QA/QC standards and blanks, to report elemental geochemistry to the exploration or process geologist.

Mineralogy/petrology lab: identify minerals and characterize rock samples using powder X-ray diffraction, polarized-light microscopy of thin sections, and/or automated SEM-EDS mineralogy on polished blocks; occasionally QC checks on industrial abrasive or diamond material (grit sizing, X-ray/optical inspection).

Geotechnical/environmental soil laboratory: soil and sediment samples are sieved, moisture-conditioned, specimens remoulded or trimmed and loaded into test apparatus; carbonate/acid reaction, pH, and chemical screening tests run on the same batch.

Core shed or drill-site logging facility: run drill core or cuttings, apply dilute HCl for carbonate, use hand lens, measure specific gravity/RQD and take handheld-XRF spot readings along the core to characterize lithology, alteration and grade, marking sample intervals.

Field outcrop testing during geological mapping or reconnaissance: hike rough, vegetated or steep terrain, hammer fresh surfaces, use hand lens, streak/hardness and dilute-acid fizz tests, and take portable XRF/LIBS readings on rock faces to identify lithology on the spot.

In-situ screening at an environmental or contaminated field site (brownfield, tailings area, reserve pit): traverse the site, collect shallow soil/sediment at georeferenced points and take portable XRF/probe readings to characterize contaminants and soil chemistry, retaining splits for lab confirmation.

instances.label: Wading discharge measurement on a small/medium natural stream: hydrologist drives to the site, wades the section with a top-setting rod and mechanical or acoustic current meter, measures depth and velocity at 20-30 verticals, reads the outside/staff gauge, computes discharge and plots the point on the station rating and hydrograph. Uneven cobble/mud bed, brush, variable weather.

Routine (non-flood) discharge measurement on a large river or tidal reach with an ADCP mounted on a manned boat, tethered board, bridge board or cableway: several reciprocal transects, moving-bed test, QA of the ensemble, discharge computed and plotted against the rating.

Flood/high-flow measurement on a large river: measurement made during a rising or peak event with high velocity, floating debris and ice, from a bridge, cableway or tethered platform, under time pressure, then plotted to extend the upper end of the rating.

Lake or reservoir level and storage: measure water-surface elevation (staff/reference gauge, RTK GNSS) and run a boat-based sonar bathymetric survey of the pool, then compute and graph the stage-area-capacity curve and the change in storage volume since the previous survey.

Synoptic low-flow / seepage run or ungauged-site work: many small measurements in one day at headwater reaches, irrigation ditches, culverts, spring outflows and wetland outlets using a portable flume/weir, handheld electromagnetic meter or salt-dilution tracer; results plotted as a longitudinal gain/loss profile.

Office compilation and graphing of continuous records: pull telemetered stage/velocity records from the agency's or client's gauge network (or NWIS), apply and check ratings and shifts, flag bad data, and produce hydrographs, lake-level time series and water-volume-change plots for a report or a real-time web page.

instances.label: Wadeable stream or small river at a streamgage: hydrologist wades the cross section, collects a depth/width-integrated or grab sample with hand sampler, measures field parameters (temp, specific conductance, pH, DO, turbidity) with a calibrated meter to check the site's continuous sonde, then filters, preserves, labels bottles and completes chain of custody. Variable flow, bank access, weather.

Groundwater monitoring well at a controlled site (landfill, refinery, remediation site, municipal well field): set up pump/tubing, low-flow purge until field parameters stabilize in a flow-through cell, record readings, fill and preserve VOC/metals/nutrient bottles, decontaminate equipment, complete paperwork.

Reservoir or lake sampled from a boat: run vertical profiles with a multiparameter sonde, collect depth-discrete samples with a Van Dorn/Niskin bottle at several stations (e.g., for algal bloom or drinking-water source monitoring), bottle and ice samples for laboratory analysis.

Laboratory or field-office analysis of collected samples: filtration, alkalinity titration, turbidity, nutrient/colorimetric determinations, sample preparation and extraction, running instruments, blanks/duplicates and QC, logging results against the continuous-monitor record.

Storm-event, high-flow or hazardous-access sampling: sampling from a bridge with a reel and weighted sampler during a runoff event, flood or spill response, or hiking to a remote backcountry/snowmelt site; adverse weather, debris, time pressure.

instances.label: Install a new streamgage/stage-monitoring station on a creek or river: set a stilling well or submersible pressure transducer/gas-purge orifice line in the channel, anchor conduit, erect shelter or mount on a bridge pier, wire datalogger, solar panel and telemetry, set reference marks, run differential levels to datum, and verify sensor against a staff gauge. Uneven bank, mud, flowing water, variable weather, site-specific geometry.

Routine field maintenance/calibration visit to an existing gauging station: clear debris and sediment from the intake or orifice, purge lines, swap desiccant and batteries, check recorded stage against an independent staff/wire-weight reading, adjust sensor offset in the logger, repair mounts damaged by high flow or vandalism, download and verify the record.

Groundwater monitoring wells: unlock well vault, sound depth to water with an electric tape, pull and reinstall vented pressure transducers/dataloggers on suspension cable at a set depth, verify and correct transducer calibration against the manual measurement, reseal cap and vault. Wells scattered along roadsides, farm fields, industrial parcels, often reached on foot.

Precipitation and met instrumentation at remote sites: install or service tipping-bucket rain gauges, weighing gauges, snow pillows and associated sensors; level the gauge, clean insects/debris from funnel and screen, run a field calibration with a known-volume drip kit, adjust the tipping mechanism screws, and document the calibration.

Sediment/turbidity instrumentation in the stream: wade or boat out to install pump-sampler intakes, bubbler lines and optical turbidity or acoustic sediment sensors on booms or pilings; clean fouled optical windows, calibrate turbidity sensors against formazin/StablCal standards on site, and re-secure hardware after high flow.

Bench/lab prep in the office or field-office lab: calibrate multiparameter water-quality sondes (pH, conductivity, DO, turbidity) against standard solutions in a cal cup, bench-check pressure transducers, program dataloggers and telemetry, verify tipping buckets on a bench rig, and record calibration sheets before deployment.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: attaching an inspection sensor to infrastructure, the closest published robotic analogue to field instrument installation. It places a lightweight adhesive pod on a flat wall with lab-verified perception, far short of anchoring, plumbing, wiring and datum-referencing a stream or well instrument.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous data collection on the same waterbodies where hydrologists site instruments. It shows robots operate in this environment for sensing only, performing no installation, maintenance or calibration of station hardware.

instances.label: Seasonal snow survey at snow courses / study plots in mountain terrain: travel in by ski, snowshoe or snowmobile in winter conditions, take depth and SWE at prescribed points with a Federal sampler, dig a pit to log density, temperature and stratigraphy, record and transmit the readings.

In-situ field campaign on a glacier or permafrost site: drill and read ablation stakes, probe and core the winter snowpack, dig accumulation pits, run GPS/GNSS points, probe active-layer depth on a monitoring grid, log borehole thermistors and swap dataloggers; helicopter/boat/ATV access, crevasse, bear, bog and weather hazards.

Geophysical / uncrewed-vehicle surveying of cryosphere features: towed ground-penetrating radar transects across a snowfield, firn or glacier to map depth, layering and ice thickness; UAV lidar or photogrammetry mapping of glacier surface change, snow depth or thaw features; profiling beneath floating ice.

Installing and maintaining automated cold-region monitoring instrumentation: erecting or servicing SNOTEL/automatic weather stations, snow-depth sensors, cameras and dataloggers, replacing batteries and sensors, digging in cables, calibrating and retrieving data on remote winter/tundra site visits.

Laboratory processing of collected snow, ice and meltwater samples: melt and weigh samples, filter and aliquot, run isotope/ion/turbidity analyses on bench instruments, decant and archive, QC and log the results in an institutional lab or cold room.

Desk-based investigation: compiling and quality-checking station, airborne and satellite records, running snow/glacier/permafrost models, interpreting the results and writing them up for a report or paper, in an office.

instances.label: Install or service a ground-based/in-situ remote sensing station at an outdoor site: level and anchor a tripod/mast, mount a radiometer, GNSS base, met/flux sensors or a field node network, run and weatherproof cables, hook up solar/battery power and telemetry, then troubleshoot a dead logger or corroded connector on a return visit. Terrain, vegetation, weather and site layout differ every time.

Routine pre-mission setup and upkeep of a UAS-based sensing platform operated from a fixed site or industrial facility: fit/change the standard imaging or LiDAR payload, install charged batteries and storage media, run power-on and GNSS/IMU self-checks, keep the aircraft sheltered and charged between repeat data-collection sorties.

Custom integration of a new sensor onto a UAV or ground vehicle in a lab/shop: fabricate or fit a mount plate and vibration isolators, route and secure a wiring harness, tap power, wire GNSS/IMU/PPS triggering, configure the acquisition software, then verify data streams and perform a boresight/lever-arm calibration flight.

Install and maintain an airborne sensor in an aircraft at a hangar or shop: fit a camera/LiDAR/hyperspectral head into a belly port or pod, torque mounts, connect power, data and IMU cabling in confined spaces, clean the optical window, and run functional checks before a survey campaign.

Bench calibration and characterization of a sensor in a lab or cleanroom: mount the instrument to the optical bench, run radiometric calibration against an integrating sphere or reference panel, check spectral/geometric response, dark current and uniformity, and record the calibration coefficients used in downstream processing.

Install and maintain the receiving and ingest hardware of a data collection system in a facility: mount and align a downlink antenna on a rooftop or pad, cable receivers and timing, rack and swap servers/storage, replace a failed receiver card or drive, and verify ingest of a live pass.

instances.label: UAV data-acquisition campaign at a field site (construction/earthworks, quarry, farm, burn scar): drive to site, pre-flight checks, launch, fly automated grid/oblique mapping patterns with RTK camera or lidar payload, swap batteries, verify coverage and image quality on site, return data for processing. Variable wind, dust, sun angle; layout changes between visits.

On-foot ground-truth / calibration-validation plot work over accessible vegetated terrain (row-crop fields, plantations, grassland, managed forest plots): navigate to GPS-referenced plots, measure canopy/plant structure (height, stem diameter, LAI, DBH), pull gridded soil cores, log georeferenced records, return samples/data.

Ground truth in heterogeneous natural terrain (wetland, rangeland, mixed forest, coastal dune): identify cover type and species, judge condition, take handheld field-spectroradiometer signatures with white-reference calibration, photograph, hand-record observations at points chosen partly on the spot to represent image pixels.

Field instrumentation work: haul and erect tripods/masts and eddy-flux or radiometer towers, install and level GNSS base stations, mount and boresight sensors in an aircraft or vehicle at a hangar, lay out corner reflectors/calibration tarps, cable, power and troubleshoot equipment, then dismantle.

Terrestrial/mobile laser-scanning survey of a built or industrial site (jobsite, plant, bridge, streetscape): occupy multiple scan stations along a planned route, capture registered point clouds and panoramas, check coverage/registration, deliver an as-built cloud. People, vehicles and clutter present.

Vessel-based coastal/marine survey: run planned survey lines collecting multibeam bathymetry and oceanographic/optical data for calibration of satellite or airborne products, monitor acquisition quality over multi-day missions offshore.

sources.claim: A docked drone system flew automated mapping missions over an active construction site to build 3D models and track earthwork/dirt movement, with the survey firm reviewing data remotely.

sources.system: DJI Dock 2 + Matrice 3D with DroneDeploy
sources.title: Everything you need to know about the DJI Dock 2 (DroneDeploy)
sources.claim: Dock-based automated flights with the Matrice 3D deliver survey-grade, centimetre-level mapping accuracy from onboard dual RTK, so repeat missions need no on-site ground control placement.

sources.system: Percepto AIM drone-in-a-box
sources.title: Percepto approved to deploy highly automated Beyond Visual Line of Sight drones
sources.claim: FAA authorised highly automated BVLOS drone-in-a-box operations, including mapping and modelling use cases, at a large outdoor industrial site with no pilot or visual observer on ....

sources.system: Trimble X7 + FieldLink on Boston Dynamics Spot
sources.title: Trimble Releases Turnkey Autonomous Robotic Scanning Solution
sources.claim: A commercial turnkey product mounts a survey-grade 3D laser scanner on the Spot quadruped for autonomous scanning missions on construction sites, producing ongoing as-built/progress point clouds.

sources.system: Leica BLK ARC on Boston Dynamics Spot
sources.title: Leica BLK ARC Autonomous Laser Scanning Module
sources.claim: The BLK ARC scanning module on Spot performs fully autonomous, repeatable mobile laser-scanning missions; partners have deployed it on live nuclear sites and energised substations.

sources.system: Saildrone Surveyor USV
sources.title: Saildrone Completes Bathymetric Survey of Cayman Islands EEZ
sources.claim: An uncrewed surface vehicle autonomously completed a ~90,000 km2 bathymetric survey of the Cayman Islands EEZ over roughly 300 mission days, and is under contract collecting NOAA seafloor mapping data off the Mariana Islands.
sources.transferJustification: Multibeam bathymetric/oceanographic acquisition on planned survey lines is the vessel fieldwork remote sensing staff participate in to acquire and validate seafloor and coastal data products.

sources.system: LemnaTec Field Scanalyzer (TERRA-REF)
sources.developer: LemnaTec / University of Arizona Maricopa Agricultural Center / USDA-ARS
sources.title: TERRA REF - Phenotyping field scanner system
sources.claim: A 30-tonne rail gantry autonomously traverses field plots continuously imaging crops with a hyperspectral, thermal, fluorescence and 3D sensor suite - automated plot-level radiometric measurement in a purpose-built rail facility.
sources.transferJustification: Plot-level hyperspectral/thermal radiometry over vegetation is the machine equivalent of the worker's handheld field-spectroradiometer ground-truth readings, performed here with the plots brought to a purpose-built rail machine.
